docs.title: Run a heavy test once. Reuse the result safely everywhere
docs.text:
Aval signs a test result and ties it to the exact inputs it used. A job with the same inputs and a trusted signer skips the test.

  1. List the inputs. Write the files and tools your test reads in aval.yaml. Aval hashes them into one fingerprint.
  2. Run once, sign the result. On a miss the test runs. With --push, Aval signs the result and stores it in your OCI registry.
  3. Verify, then skip. Same fingerprint, trusted signer: the test is skipped. Anything else: the test runs.

A result that fails verification is a security event, never a quiet miss.

Already have CI for a monorepo? Integrate Aval in 5 files.

docs.title: Artifact format
docs.text: How Aval stores a result in an OCI registry, what it signs, and the JSON aval verify -o json prints. The Go types in pkg/evidence are the source of truth. The identifiers and JSON shapes below are frozen; see Versioning.

docs.title: Identifiers
docs.text:
All constants live in pkg/evidence.

Constant Value Used for Status ArtifactType application/vnd.trianalab.aval.execution.v2 artifactType of the OCI manifest frozen ArtifactTypeFingerprint application/vnd.trianalab.aval.fingerprint.v1 artifactType of the per-fingerprint anchor manifest frozen MediaTypeDSSE application/vnd.dsse.envelope.v1+json Media type of the signed DSSE envelope layer DSSE standard MediaTypeExecution application/vnd.trianalab.aval.execution.v2+json Media type of the raw predicate JSON, when carried on its own frozen PayloadType application/vnd.in-toto+json DSSE payloadType in-toto standard StatementType https://in-toto.io/Statement/v1 in-toto Statement _type in-toto standard PredicateType https://aval.trianalab.io/attestation/execution/v2 in-toto predicateType frozen SchemaVersion v2 Predicate schemaVersion frozen ArtifactTypeOutputs application/vnd.trianalab.aval.outputs.v1 artifactType of the manifest that carries the output files of one execution frozen MediaTypeOutput application/vnd.trianalab.aval.output.v1 Media type of one output file layer frozen ReportVersion aval.trianalab.io/verify-report/v1 version of the verify report frozen RunRecordVersion aval.trianalab.io/run-record/v1 version of a run record provisional ArtifactTypeRun application/vnd.trianalab.aval.run.v1 artifactType of a run record manifest provisional MediaTypeRun application/vnd.trianalab.aval.run.v1+json Media type of the run record layer provisional ArtifactTypeStats application/vnd.trianalab.aval.stats.v1 artifactType of the per-test stats anchor manifest provisional StatsReportVersion aval.trianalab.io/stats-report/v1 version of the aval stats --output json document provisional

The bundle layer uses the Sigstore media type application/vnd.dev.sigstore.bundle.v0.3+json. Manifests carry the annotation io.trianalab.aval.fingerprint (informational, frozen: verification reads the fingerprint from the signed predicate); the stats anchor carries io.trianalab.aval.test (provisional) with the test id. The contract apiVersion and the aval-fingerprint/v2 manifest version are also frozen (see the table under Versioning).

docs.title: OCI layout
docs.text:
There is no Aval server or database. The registry is the only index.

flowchart LR
  tag[tag sha256-FP] --> anchor[fingerprint anchor]
  e1[execution manifest] -- subject --> anchor
  e2[execution manifest] -- subject --> anchor
  e1 --> layers[layers: DSSE envelope,<br>Sigstore bundle]
  o1[outputs manifest] -- subject --> anchor
  stag[tag stats-TEST] --> sanchor[stats anchor]
  r1[run record] -- subject --> sanchor

Per fingerprint there is one anchor manifest, and one execution manifest per execution whose subject is the anchor, so the OCI 1.1 referrers API lists every execution for a fingerprint. The anchor is deterministic: its bytes, and so its digest, depend only on the fingerprint. It is tagged sha256-<fingerprint hex>.

Anchor manifest 
{
  "schemaVersion": 2,
  "mediaType": "application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json",
  "artifactType": "application/vnd.trianalab.aval.fingerprint.v1",
  "config": {
    "mediaType": "application/vnd.oci.empty.v1+json",
    "digest": "sha256:44136fa355b3678a1146ad16f7e8649e94fb4fc21fe77e8310c060f61caaff8a",
    "size": 2,
    "data": "e30="
  },
  "layers": [
    {
      "mediaType": "application/vnd.oci.empty.v1+json",
      "digest": "sha256:44136fa355b3678a1146ad16f7e8649e94fb4fc21fe77e8310c060f61caaff8a",
      "size": 2,
      "data": "e30="
    }
  ],
  "annotations": {
    "io.trianalab.aval.fingerprint": "sha256:<fingerprint hex>"
  }
}
Execution manifest 
{
  "schemaVersion": 2,
  "mediaType": "application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json",
  "artifactType": "application/vnd.trianalab.aval.execution.v2",
  "config": {
    "mediaType": "application/vnd.oci.empty.v1+json",
    "digest": "sha256:44136fa355b3678a1146ad16f7e8649e94fb4fc21fe77e8310c060f61caaff8a",
    "size": 2,
    "data": "e30="
  },
  "layers": [
    {
      "mediaType": "application/vnd.dsse.envelope.v1+json",
      "digest": "sha256:<envelope digest>",
      "size": 1834
    },
    {
      "mediaType": "application/vnd.dev.sigstore.bundle.v0.3+json",
      "digest": "sha256:<bundle digest>",
      "size": 4210
    }
  ],
  "subject": {
    "mediaType": "application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json",
    "digest": "sha256:<anchor digest>",
    "size": 512
  },
  "annotations": {
    "io.trianalab.aval.fingerprint": "sha256:<fingerprint hex>"
  }
}
  • config: the OCI empty descriptor ({}).
  • layers: the signed DSSE envelope, then the Sigstore bundle. Push refuses an attestation without a valid bundle. Fetch treats a missing bundle or envelope, any other or repeated layer, a manifest that is not sha256-addressed, over 4 MiB, or not matching its digest as a verification failure.
  • subject: always the anchor of the execution's fingerprint. The tested revision or artifact is recorded inside the statement, not in the manifest, so the referrers of a tested image do not list its evidence.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
A contract with outputs publishes the files before the attestation, as one manifest with artifactType application/vnd.trianalab.aval.outputs.v1, the OCI empty config, one layer per file (media type application/vnd.trianalab.aval.output.v1, annotation org.opencontainers.image.title = the path relative to the contract root) and the fingerprint anchor as subject. The predicate's execution.outputs holds its digest and every file's path, digest and size, so the signature covers them. Lookup lists only execution manifests: an outputs manifest is never a candidate and does not count toward the 64-candidate cap, and readers that do not know it ignore it.

After a candidate verifies, Aval fetches its outputs by the signed digests, with the caps (256 files, 16 MiB each, 64 MiB in total) checked before reading. Each of these is a verification failure, never a miss:

  • the outputs manifest or a blob is missing, or does not match its digest or size
  • the manifest's layers differ from the predicate's list (extra, missing, renamed or reordered)
  • a path that matches no outputs glob, is the contract file, is in scope or is or lies under a .git entry (directory or file) or .aval; a glob that matches no path; a predicate without outputs for a contract with outputs, or the reverse

aval run then writes the files: each is staged next to its target and renamed into place once all are staged. A symlink on the way or anything but a regular file at the target stops the restore; the test runs and the command exits 1. A failure while renaming can leave some files restored; the test then runs and rewrites them.

docs.title: Push
docs.text:
• Push never replaces: identical bytes are a no-op, anything else adds a referrer. Re-tagging the deterministic anchor also repairs a moved tag.
  • Registries without the referrers API (GHCR): oras keeps the referrers tag schema index, which concurrent pushes can overwrite. Aval checks that the new digest is listed, re-pushing up to 3 times, 1 s apart; otherwise exit 1. A registry that indexes for longer than about 2 s, or more than 64 attestations, also makes the check fail. A dropped execution is never a candidate.
  • Push needs no DELETE rights.

docs.title: Env file
docs.text:
aval run writes the env file next to the result (--env-file, default .aval/env.txt, .aval/<test>/env.txt with --test), and aval push --env-file FILE takes the env section of the manifest from it instead of its own environment, for a publish job whose variables differ from the job that ran the test:

aval-fingerprint/v2
env GOFLAGS unset
env GOTOOLCHAIN 25bf8e1a2393f1108d37029b3df5593236c755742ec93465bbafa9b290bddcf6
  • The first line is the fingerprint manifest version; the rest are the manifest's env NAME unset|<sha256 hex> lines exactly as hashed, the same lines aval explain prints, and nothing else. The file has no version of its own beyond that line.
  • It holds hashes, never values. A hash of a low-entropy secret can be found by trying values, as with aval explain.
  • It is neither signed nor published, and is no more trusted than the result.json beside it: it replaces only the env section. Sources, dependencies, toolchain and contract lines are hashed from the publish checkout, so an edited env file cannot make push sign a result for files the checkout does not have, and a different hash changes the digest, which must still equal the result's and the report's.
  • Push refuses it (exit 1, nothing published) when the version line is not the current manifest version, a line is malformed or repeats a name, a hash is neither unset nor 64 lowercase hex digits, the lines are not sorted, an exact environment.env name has no line, or a line names a variable that no exact name covers and no prefix pattern matches (as a set variable, upper-cased on Windows).
  • With a prefix pattern (APP_*) the file has one line per variable the pattern matched in the job that ran the test. Push cannot know which those were: a matched variable set only in the publish job is not hashed, and a line removed from the file changes the digest, which then no longer equals the result's.
  • Contracts in scope.contracts are covered by their digests: push still hashes their environment.env from its own environment.
  • An existing env file inside the contract scope and outside .aval/ is an input: run and push exit 2, as for --result-file.

docs.title: Lookup and consumption
docs.text:
1. Compute the fingerprint locally (aval explain --digest).
  2. Resolve the tag sha256-<fingerprint hex> in the --registry repository. It must point at the anchor digest Aval computes for that fingerprint; anything else is a verification failure (the tag was moved).
  3. List the anchor's execution referrers; each is a candidate, by digest. A malformed referrer entry is still a candidate, and fetching it fails verification, so it never turns into a miss.
  4. Fetch each candidate by digest (repo@sha256:...), never by tag.
  5. Verify each envelope and apply the trust policy.
Limit Value When exceeded candidates per fingerprint 64 error (the test runs) referrer listing requests 64 error manifest size 4 MiB verification-failed --registry-timeout 1m; lookup and fetch share it, push has its own; runner.command is never under it error a listed candidate returns 404 skipped with a warning; all gone: miss

A missing tag, or an anchor without executions, is a miss (evidence.ErrNotFound, exit 4). An artifact that exists but is malformed or fails signature or policy checks is a verification failure (evidence.ErrVerification, exit 5) and a security event.

docs.title: Registry credentials
docs.text:
Aval reads registry credentials the way Docker does: from $DOCKER_CONFIG/config.json, or ~/.docker/config.json when DOCKER_CONFIG is not set, including the credential helpers it names (credsStore, credHelpers, for example docker-credential-osxkeychain or docker-credential-ecr-login). Log in with docker login <registry> (or oras login, which writes the same file). Without an entry for the registry, Aval connects anonymously, which is enough to read a public repository. $AVAL_DOCKER_CONFIG, when set, names a directory whose config.json Aval reads instead, for every command; runner.command never sees it, and keeps the job's $DOCKER_CONFIG.

A config file that cannot be parsed, or a helper that fails, is outcome error (exit 1): aval run runs the test and nothing is reused. Loopback registries (localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1) use plain HTTP; every other registry uses HTTPS.

docs.title: Multiple attestations per fingerprint
docs.text:
Every execution stays a referrer of the anchor, so a later push cannot hide an earlier one. aval verify verifies every candidate:

  • The verified candidate with the highest level wins; on a tie a non-passed result, then the lowest digest.
  • A candidate that cannot be checked (error) blocks reuse: it might have outranked the winner.
  • A signer below minTrustLevel is rejected as miss and does not block.
  • If nothing is reused: verification-failed beats error beats miss.

Unused candidates are listed in the report's rejected; any that failed verification add one aval: SECURITY: ... line on stderr. Such a candidate is a security event even beside a verified one: the report keeps outcome verified and its reference, but aval verify exits 5 and aval run does not reuse, runs the test and exits 5.

docs.title: The 64-candidate cap and cleanup
docs.text:
Every push adds one execution, even for the same inputs (hostname and timestamps differ), and Aval never deletes one. Past 64 executions, every lookup for that fingerprint is verification-failed (the reason names the cap): nothing is verified, so trust cannot be proven and someone with push access may be flooding the fingerprint to hide an untrusted attestation. The lookup prints an aval: SECURITY: line naming the cap, aval run runs the test and aval verify and aval run exit 5; every push still adds one, then exits 1. Other fingerprints are not affected, so the next input change also ends it.

Push from one place (for example CI on the main branch). aval run --push does not push after a reuse, but aval run --shadow --push pushes every time.

To clean up, list the executions and delete the ones you no longer need, for example with ORAS:

aval explain --digest                 # prints sha256:<hex>
oras discover --artifact-type application/vnd.trianalab.aval.execution.v2 <repo>:sha256-<hex>
oras manifest delete <repo>@sha256:<execution digest>

The registry must allow deletes (registry:2 needs REGISTRY_STORAGE_DELETE_ENABLED=true; on GHCR, delete the package versions). Deleting executions is safe: it can make a result stop being reusable, never make an untrusted one reusable. Keep any execution that failed verification until you have looked into it.

docs.title: Run records
docs.text:
aval run --stats publishes one run record per run, for every outcome, so reuse can be measured from the registry alone. --stats-file <path> writes the same record to a file, and aval stats publish <path> publishes it later, for example from a job that has write credentials but runs no tests.

Records are statistics, never evidence: unsigned, and never read by aval run or aval verify, so a record, forged or not, cannot cause reuse, change an outcome or count toward the 64-candidate cap.

Recording never changes the exit code: a record that cannot be published or written is a warning (aval: warning: run record not ...). --stats needs --registry. An existing --stats-file that is not an Aval file is never overwritten. A run that stops before the lookup (bad flags, an invalid contract, aval explain) publishes no record.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
Per test there is one stats anchor, separate from every fingerprint anchor. It is deterministic (its digest depends on the test id alone) and tagged stats-<test id> (registry.StatsTag); fingerprint tags and OCI referrers tag schema tags start with sha256-, so the tags cannot collide. It has the same shape as the fingerprint anchor, with "artifactType": "application/vnd.trianalab.aval.stats.v1" and the annotation "io.trianalab.aval.test": "<test id>".

Each record is an OCI 1.1 image manifest with "artifactType": "application/vnd.trianalab.aval.run.v1", the empty config, one layer of media type application/vnd.trianalab.aval.run.v1+json holding the record JSON, and the stats anchor as subject. Records are listed by the stats anchor's referrers. Unlike registry.Push, publishing a record does not confirm the referrers listing, so on a registry without the referrers API two concurrent records for one test can drop one of them. On such registries all records of a test also share one referrers index, which grows with every record; once it exceeds the registry's manifest size limit, publishing a record fails with a warning; prune old records (see Pruning run records).

docs.title: Record JSON
docs.text:
evidence.RunRecord, parsed by evidence.ParseRunRecord:

Field Type Present Meaning version string always aval.trianalab.io/run-record/v1. testId string always metadata.name from the contract. fingerprint string always sha256:<hex>; empty when the fingerprint could not be computed. outcome string always The lookup decision, as in the verify report, except a verified lookup beside a rejected verification-failed candidate: the run did not reuse, so it records verification-failed. reused bool always true when a verified result was reused and the test did not run. With --shadow, or when --report-file cannot be written, it is false. result string when known The reused or the real passed / failed; omitted when runner.command could not start. verifiedResult string when outcome is verified The result of the verified attestation. With reused false and the test run (--shadow), a verifiedResult that differs from result is a false hit. Records made before it was added (#88) lack it. testDurationMs integer always How long runner.command ran, in milliseconds; 0 when it did not run. savedDurationMs integer always On reuse, the test duration recorded in the reused attestation (finishedAt - startedAt); 0 otherwise. avalVersion string always Version of the aval binary that ran. recordedAt RFC 3339 timestamp always When the record was made. ciRunUrl string when passed --ci-run-url, a link to the CI run. Aval does not derive it from any CI vendor. repository string when passed --source-repo on aval run (or aval stats publish, which overrides the record's), the source repository, e.g. acme/orders. Aval does not derive it from any CI vendor. aval stats --by repository counts records without it (made before it was added, #88) as unknown. 
{
  "version": "aval.trianalab.io/run-record/v1",
  "testId": "orders-integration",
  "fingerprint": "sha256:3f9a7c2e1b4d5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f9012a3b4c5d6e7f8091a2b3c4d5e6f7",
  "outcome": "verified",
  "reused": true,
  "result": "passed",
  "verifiedResult": "passed",
  "testDurationMs": 0,
  "savedDurationMs": 1184000,
  "avalVersion": "0.3.0",
  "recordedAt": "2026-11-06T09:00:00Z",
  "ciRunUrl": "https://ci.example.com/acme/orders/runs/42",
  "repository": "acme/orders"
}

evidence.ParseRunRecord rejects an inconsistent record: reused true with an outcome other than verified or a non-zero testDurationMs, and a verifiedResult without outcome verified. aval stats publish refuses it and aval stats skips it.

docs.title: Statistics: aval stats
docs.text:
aval stats reads the run records of a repository and aggregates them on demand (flags: CLI reference). It writes nothing and needs only read access. Records are unsigned, so anyone with push access can skew the numbers; they never affect reuse. Registry data is untrusted, so reading is bounded:

Case Result a record that is unreadable, over 64 KiB, inconsistent or of another test skipped and counted in skipped more than 1000 records, or 64 pages in one listing aval: warning: stopped reading run records: ... and truncated a listing fails, or --registry-timeout passes exit 1 --since filters after reading: bounds, timeout and skipped cover every record listed

Records are fetched one at a time (about 0.7 s each on GHCR), so the default 1m timeout covers some 80 records; raise --registry-timeout or prune old records.

docs.title: Stats report JSON
docs.text:
aval stats --output json prints evidence.StatsReport:

Field Type Present Meaning version string always aval.trianalab.io/stats-report/v1. registry string always The repository read. since RFC 3339 timestamp with --since Records made before it are left out (not counted, not skipped). total object always Run statistics over every test in tests. tests array always One {"testId", "stats"} per test with records, sorted by test id; [] when there are none. repositories array with --by repository One {"repository", "stats"} per source repository, sorted; records without a repository are under unknown. Omitted when there are no records. skipped integer always Records read but not counted (see above). truncated string when a bound was hit Which bound, e.g. more than 1000 run records.

Run statistics (total, tests[].stats, repositories[].stats); runs is the sum of reused, the three misses and verificationFailures:

Field Meaning runs Records counted. reused Records with reused true. hitRate reused / runs; 0 when runs is 0. misses.noTrustedResult Outcome miss: no trusted attestation, an unacknowledged mutable reference (Pin your dependencies) or --no-reuse. misses.error Outcome error: Aval could not decide. misses.verifiedNotReused Outcome verified with reused false: --shadow, or the --report-file file could not be written. verificationFailures Outcome verification-failed: security events, not misses. shadowFalseHits Of verifiedNotReused, the runs whose result differs from verifiedResult. Records without both are not counted. testDurationMs Sum of testDurationMs: time spent running tests. savedDurationMs Sum of savedDurationMs: test time reuse saved.

A negative duration in a record (a clock jump, or an edit) counts as 0, and duration sums stop at the largest int64 instead of wrapping. The golden file is pkg/evidence/testdata/stats-report-v1.golden.json.

docs.title: Pruning run records
docs.text:
Records accumulate: one per recorded run. Aval never deletes one. To keep aval stats below its read bound, and the referrers index of registries without the referrers API below their manifest size limit, delete old records, for example with ORAS:

oras discover --artifact-type application/vnd.trianalab.aval.run.v1 <repo>:stats-<test id>
oras manifest delete <repo>@sha256:<record digest>

oras discover --format json shows each record's digest; fetch one with oras manifest fetch and oras blob fetch to read its recordedAt. Deleting records only changes statistics: run records never affect reuse. The registry must allow deletes (see the 64-candidate cap and cleanup).

docs.title: DSSE envelope
docs.text:
The layer is a DSSE envelope (evidence.Envelope):

{
  "payloadType": "application/vnd.in-toto+json",
  "payload": "<base64 of the in-toto Statement JSON>",
  "signatures": [
    { "keyid": "", "sig": "<base64 signature>" }
  ]
}

Signed by sigstore-go (trust model).

docs.title: in-toto Statement
docs.text:
The envelope payload is an in-toto Statement v1 (evidence.Statement). Its subject is the same one recorded in predicate.subject. aval run writes the test id as name and the fingerprint as the digest:

{
  "_type": "https://in-toto.io/Statement/v1",
  "subject": [
    {
      "name": "orders-integration",
      "digest": { "sha256": "<fingerprint hex>" }
    }
  ],
  "predicateType": "https://aval.trianalab.io/attestation/execution/v2",
  "predicate": { "...": "see below" }
}

runner.identity is the host name (a claim; trust comes from the signer), runner.trustLevel is 0, and execution.environment holds os and arch plus the declared toolchain. Recording a git commit or image as the subject is milestone 3 work (TODO(milestone-3)).

docs.title: Predicate
docs.text:
evidence.Predicate, JSON tags exactly as below. Required fields are the ones checked by Predicate.Validate (called by evidence.Parse).

Field Type Required Meaning schemaVersion string yes, must be v2 Predicate schema version. subject object yes Tested revision/artifact. subject.name string yes e.g. git+https://github.com/acme/orders or an image reference. subject.digest map string to string yes, non-empty e.g. {"gitCommit": "..."} or {"sha256": "..."}. test object Test identity: what was checked, independent of inputs. test.id string yes metadata.name from aval.yaml. test.cacheability string Class declared in the contract: hermetic, controlled-environment, external-dependencies, non-deterministic. result string yes passed or failed. execution object This run: its inputs and conditions. execution.fingerprint string yes, sha256:<64 hex> Fingerprint over the declared inputs. execution.fingerprintVersion string Manifest format, e.g. aval-fingerprint/v2. execution.environment map string to string no (omitted when empty) Conditions of the run (toolchain, OS/arch). Only keys declared under environment.toolchain in aval.yaml are part of the fingerprint; anything else here is informational. os and arch are always the real values, whatever the toolchain declares; probe.<key> is the output of an environment.probe. execution.exitCode integer Exit code of runner.command. execution.outputs object no (omitted without contract outputs) The outputs of the run. execution.outputs.manifest string yes, sha256:<64 hex> Digest of the outputs manifest. execution.outputs.files list of {path, digest, size} yes, non-empty In layer order. path is relative to the contract root (scope.root, default the contract's directory), slash-separated and clean (no .., ., empty segment, leading /, backslash or control character), listed once; digest is sha256:<64 hex>; size is not negative. runner object Who produced the result, as claimed. runner.identity string yes Claimed producer identity. runner.issuer string no (omitted when empty) Claimed identity issuer, e.g. an OIDC issuer URL. runner.trustLevel integer 0 unknown, 1 developer, 2 runner, 3 isolated. startedAt RFC 3339 timestamp yes Execution start. finishedAt RFC 3339 timestamp yes, not before startedAt Execution end. annotations map string to string no (omitted when empty) Free third-party metadata. Aval never reads it.

The runner block is a claim: trust comes from the verified signer and the policy, never from it. The Go fields Runner.Issuer, Runner.TrustLevel and Verification.TrustLevel are deprecated.

evidence.Parse only checks structure. A parsed predicate is a claim, not evidence; use evidence.Verify to get something you can rely on.

docs.title: Annotations
docs.text: Keys use reverse-DNS of the owner, e.g. com.example.team, com.acme.ticket. Aval does not define, validate or interpret any key. Do not put secrets there: the predicate is published to the registry.

docs.title: Verify report
docs.text:
aval verify --output json prints one evidence.Report to stdout, and aval run --report-file <file> writes the same document for its lookup decision. This is the stable machine interface for CI scripts and external tools.

Field Type Present Meaning version string always aval.trianalab.io/verify-report/v1. outcome string always See outcomes below. testId string always metadata.name from the contract. fingerprint string always Locally computed sha256:<hex>. reference string when an attestation was found Immutable repo@sha256:<manifest digest>. result string verified only passed or failed from the verified predicate. signer object verified only Accepted policy identity that matched (issuer, subjectRegexp, trustLevel, and trustLevelName: developer, runner or isolated, derived from the policy entry's level, never from the predicate) plus the identity the signature actually carried: subject, the certificate subject (SAN) for keyless signatures, or keyId, base64(sha256(DER public key)) for key-based ones. subject and keyId are omitted when empty. predicate object verified only Full verified predicate. reason string non-verified outcomes Human-readable cause. rejected array when a candidate was not used Each {reference, outcome, reason}; outcome is verification-failed, error or miss. A verification-failed entry is a security event even when outcome is verified: alert. A miss entry is an authentic attestation whose signer the policy lists below minTrustLevel: routine non-reuse, no alert.

Outcomes:

outcome Meaning What the caller does verified Valid attestation satisfies the policy. Reuse result. miss No attestation for this fingerprint that the policy can reuse: none found, or only authentic ones whose signer the policy lists below minTrustLevel. Run the test. verification-failed Attestation exists but fails signature or policy, or the fingerprint holds more than 64 attestations (none verified). Run the test and alert. Never hide this. error Aval could not decide (registry unreachable, bad policy file, trusted root unavailable). Treat as a miss: run the test (fail closed).

aval verify exits with the outcome (exit codes); aval run acts on it and exits with the test result (Outcomes).

  • A fingerprint error: aval verify prints no report and exits 1; aval run --report-file writes outcome error with an empty fingerprint, then runs the test. Bad flags or an invalid contract: no report, exit 2.
  • No --policy (or AVAL_POLICY), or a non-deterministic contract: miss, no lookup.
  • A policy, or a trusted root a candidate needs, that cannot load: error.

Example (verified):

{
  "version": "aval.trianalab.io/verify-report/v1",
  "outcome": "verified",
  "testId": "orders-integration",
  "fingerprint": "sha256:3f9a7c2e1b4d5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f9012a3b4c5d6e7f8091a2b3c4d5e6f7",
  "reference": "ghcr.io/acme/orders-aval@sha256:8c1d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f9012a3b4c5d6e7f8091a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0",
  "result": "passed",
  "signer": {
    "issuer": "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com",
    "subjectRegexp": "^https://github.com/acme/orders/\\.github/workflows/ci\\.yaml@refs/heads/main$",
    "trustLevel": 2,
    "trustLevelName": "runner",
    "subject": "https://github.com/acme/orders/.github/workflows/ci.yaml@refs/heads/main"
  },
  "predicate": { "...": "as in the predicate example" }
}

Example (miss):

{
  "version": "aval.trianalab.io/verify-report/v1",
  "outcome": "miss",
  "testId": "orders-integration",
  "fingerprint": "sha256:3f9a7c2e1b4d5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f9012a3b4c5d6e7f8091a2b3c4d5e6f7",
  "reason": "no attestation found for fingerprint"
}

docs.title: Versioning and compatibility
docs.text:
These rules apply to every frozen format:

Format Version identifiers (move together) Frozen at Statement and predicate PredicateType, SchemaVersion, MediaTypeExecution, ArtifactType .../execution/v2, v2, execution.v2 Fingerprint anchor ArtifactTypeFingerprint fingerprint.v1 Verify report, outcomes and exit codes ReportVersion aval.trianalab.io/verify-report/v1 Run record and stats anchor RunRecordVersion, ArtifactTypeRun, MediaTypeRun, ArtifactTypeStats run-record/v1, run.v1, stats.v1 (provisional) Stats report StatsReportVersion aval.trianalab.io/stats-report/v1 (provisional) Contract and policy file apiVersion aval.trianalab.io/v1 Fingerprint manifest header line, execution.fingerprintVersion aval-fingerprint/v2

The predicate keeps v2: v1 was used before and an identifier is never recycled, and v2 is already under aval.trianalab.io and is what v0.1.0 writes, so attestations published by v0.1.0 stay readable. The report and the contract moved from the pre-freeze aval.dev/.../v1alpha1 names to aval.trianalab.io at v1. There is no accept window for the old names: a contract or policy file with aval.dev/v1alpha1 is invalid.

docs.title: Additive changes (same identifier)
docs.text:
• A new optional field, omitted when empty, whose absence means what it meant before.
  • A new key under annotations.
  • A new optional contract field. Older aval binaries reject a contract that uses it (unknown fields are rejected), which fails closed.
  • A new contract kind whose tests expand to kind: Test contracts that fingerprint as before. Older aval binaries reject it, which fails closed.
  • Widening the validation of a contract field to accept values it used to reject, when every value it accepted before keeps its manifest. Older aval binaries reject the new values, which fails closed.
  • A new manifest section that only a new optional contract field brings. Every contract without the field keeps its manifest byte for byte, and a contract with it cannot have had a fingerprint before, so no fingerprint changes meaning.

Existing fields keep their name, JSON tag, type and meaning.

docs.title: Breaking changes (new identifier)
docs.text:
• Renaming or removing a field, changing its type or its meaning.
  • Making an optional field required, or tightening validation of an existing one.
  • A new value of a closed set: outcome, result, trustLevel, cacheability class, or an exit code.
  • A change to what the fingerprint covers or how it is hashed: a new aval-fingerprint/vN. There is no accept window: old attestations become misses, never false hits.

A new predicate version changes PredicateType, SchemaVersion, MediaTypeExecution and ArtifactType together (execution/v3, execution.v3). Old and new artifacts can coexist in one repository.

docs.title: How consumers treat versions
docs.text:
• Unknown version: not evidence. Reject a predicateType, schemaVersion, report version or artifactType you do not know, and run the test. evidence.Verify does this for predicates.
  • Unknown fields: ignore them within a version you know. Do not decode Aval documents strictly. evidence.Parse ignores unknown fields.
  • Unknown values of a closed set: fail closed. An outcome other than the four listed above, a result other than passed or failed, or an unknown trust level or cacheability class means "not verified": run the test. Within a version such a value can only come from a bug or tampering.
  • No field grants trust. Trust comes from the verified signer and the policy (see trust-model.md), never from a field that is new or that you do not understand.

docs.title: Deprecation
docs.text: Aval writes only the newest version of each format. When a breaking change mints a new version, the release notes say whether Aval keeps reading the old one for a transition. If it does, the old parser stays next to the new one, dispatching on the identifier, and old documents get no more trust than new ones; any identifier Aval does not know fails closed. Ending a transition is announced in the release notes of the release that removes it.

docs.title: Golden files
docs.text: pkg/evidence/testdata/*.golden.json set every field of the statement, predicate, verify report, run record and stats report, and only grow: an additive change adds its field to the golden of its version, and a new version adds a new file. The tests that enforce this: CONTRIBUTING.md.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
History
  • Predicate v1 became v2 when the execution manifest's subject changed from the tested artifact to the fingerprint anchor and the Sigstore bundle layer was added. Aval no longer reads or writes v1: a v1 artifact is never a candidate.
  • At the freeze (#17), the verify report moved from aval.dev/verify-report/v1alpha1 to aval.trianalab.io/verify-report/v1 and the contract and policy apiVersion from aval.dev/v1alpha1 to aval.trianalab.io/v1; every fingerprint changed, so older results are misses and the tests run once.
  • Within verify-report/v1 (#65), a signer below minTrustLevel became miss instead of verification-failed, and rejected[].outcome may be miss. No new value, field or exit code, so the version stays.
  • Within the provisional run-record/v1 (#88), records gained verifiedResult and repository, and inconsistent records are rejected; no record aval writes is affected.
  • Within aval-fingerprint/v1 (#102), scope.resolve adds resolve lines after the env lines; manifests without it are unchanged.
  • Within execution/v2 (#141), the predicate gained execution.outputs and the outputs manifest (outputs.v1, output.v1) was added; the contract gained outputs, omitted when empty, so no existing fingerprint changes.
  • aval-fingerprint/v1 became aval-fingerprint/v2 (#199) when a .git file or symlink (the gitfile of a linked worktree or submodule) stopped being hashed, like a .git directory. Every existing attestation is a miss once and the tests run again; there is no lookup by v1.
  • Within aval.trianalab.io/v1 and aval-fingerprint/v2 (#253), environment.env accepts PREFIX_* patterns, which write the existing env lines, one per matching variable. Contracts without a pattern keep their manifest.
  • Within aval.trianalab.io/v1 (#206), the contract gained kind: TestSet. Each of its tests fingerprints byte for byte like the same kind: Test, so the manifest version stays aval-fingerprint/v2.

docs.title: Patch Changes
docs.text:
• d4a98a6: Dependencies: github.com/sigstore/sigstore 1.11.3, and actions/setup-node 7.1.0 in the release workflow (with its automatic package-manager cache off).
  • be64eb3: Docs: a lookup-only step must not skip setup that environment.probe checks, since the run step probes before its lookup; the example now gates npm ci and the browsers instead of setup-node.

docs.title: Minor Changes
docs.text:
• 52911eb: environment.env accepts prefix patterns such as APP_* (#253): every set variable whose name starts with the prefix is hashed, one env NAME <sha256> line each, so a tool configured by prefix no longer needs every name listed by hand. * may only end the entry; *, *_TOKEN and patterns that would match AVAL_RUN_STACK (AVAL_*) are rejected. Names compare case-sensitively on Linux and macOS and case-insensitively on Windows. A pattern also hashes credentials that share the prefix; list exact names when it covers secrets. aval run records the matched variables in its env file, and aval push --env-file accepts the names a pattern matches. Contracts without a pattern keep their fingerprint; older aval binaries reject a contract that uses one.
  • 0c4a8b7: environment.paths declares files and directories outside the tree as fingerprint inputs (#254), such as ~/.config/pacto or ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME}/pacto. Each entry adds a path <entry> <hash> manifest line with the entry as written, so another $HOME with the same content shares a result; absent and unset are hashed too. A symlink, a special or unreadable file fails the fingerprint, and an entry inside the contract tree is a contract error. aval explain lists the lines. Format change: an additive optional contract field under the same apiVersion, with a manifest line kind only it brings; the manifest stays aval-fingerprint/v2 and existing contracts hash as before. An older aval rejects a contract that uses paths (unknown field), which fails closed.
  • cef4b7b: A TestSet matrix variable can be {count: N} (N from 1 to 1024): it takes the values "1" to "N" and defines {v_count} = N, so a sharded runner writes PW_SHARD={shard}/{shard_count} and the total is stated once. The expanded tests and their fingerprints are the same as the list form. A bad count, an extra key in the mapping, or a v_count variable beside a count variable v is a contract error (exit 2). Additive within aval.trianalab.io/v1: older aval binaries reject the mapping form.
  • 6c24fde: A TestSet matrix now substitutes {var} into environment.toolchain values, so one test can declare a value per leg (for example platform: "{os}") and each leg gets its own fingerprint. An unknown {var} in a toolchain value, or a {var} in a toolchain value of a test without a matrix, is now a contract error (exit 2); before, it was hashed as literal text. Contracts without {var} in toolchain values keep their fingerprints.
  • 7fa8978: scope.optionalSource declares source globs that may match no file yet (#257), for inputs a test discovers by pattern such as **/*testdata*.yaml. Matching files are hashed as source lines, with the same exclude rules, so adding the first one is a miss. A glob may not be in both source and optionalSource, and source plus optionalSource must still hash at least one file. aval explain names optional globs that matched nothing on stderr. Format change: an additive optional contract field under the same apiVersion; the manifest stays aval-fingerprint/v2. Existing contracts hash as before; an older aval rejects a contract that uses optionalSource (unknown field), which fails closed.
  • 597b9d6: The GitHub run action takes lookup-only: "true" (#252): it runs aval verify with the default branch's trust policy and trust minimum, sets the outcome output and never runs the test, uploads or writes .aval/. A later setup step can be skipped on verified; the run step after it still decides reuse. A miss succeeds the step, exit 5 fails it with the aval SECURITY annotation, and lookup-only with shadow: true exits 2.
  • da68465: The GitHub run action raises the trust minimum to runner on the default branch (#251), so main no longer goes green on a developer-signed result that aval push would then not publish. The new min-trust-level input (auto by default, or developer, runner, isolated) passes the highest of itself, the job's AVAL_MIN_TRUST_LEVEL and the policy's minTrustLevel, so it never lowers the policy's minimum; min-trust-level: developer opts out. A policy minimum of isolated is kept instead of failing with exit 2, and the log and step summary show the effective minimum. Workflows can drop their hand-written AVAL_MIN_TRUST_LEVEL expression.
  • c17e62f: The GitHub run action reads a private attestations registry: new optional inputs registry-username and registry-password (default empty, anonymous as before) write credentials for the host of the default-branch policy's registry only, in a directory of the step that is deleted when it ends. aval reads it through the new AVAL_DOCKER_CONFIG, a directory whose config.json replaces $DOCKER_CONFIG's for Aval's registry client and that runner.command never gets; the test keeps the job's DOCKER_CONFIG. The test no longer sees the job's GH_TOKEN.

docs.title: Patch Changes
docs.text:
• d87eec2: The GitHub actions no longer put cosign on the job's PATH. They install the cosign that verifies the aval release into $RUNNER_TEMP, checked against a per-platform sha256, instead of using sigstore/cosign-installer, which writes GITHUB_PATH. The test and later steps see the job's own tools again.
  • 1261177: examples/github-monorepo and the "Integrate Aval in 5 files" guide that embeds it pin the GitHub actions at the commit that pins v0.8.2, with a # v0.8.2 comment, instead of a commit that installed v0.7.0 (#261). After each pin PR merges, the new pin-examples job of release.yaml opens a PR (branch release-pins/examples) that moves the examples to the merge commit, and pin-examples-ci dispatches ci on it. An architecture test fails when an example's action pin installs an older release than main pins (one pin behind is allowed while that PR is open) or when its comment names another version, and when a doc other than docs/install.md names a hard-coded aval version. docs/install.md now pins v0.8.2 in its example and says the verified-install flags first ship in v0.8.1. No CLI or format change.
  • 8f1912d: The pinning scanner no longer reports npx --no, npx --no-install, npm exec --no, pnpm exec and yarn exec: they run only what is already installed. Plain npx, npm exec, pnpm dlx, yarn dlx and bunx are still reported, as are packages named by -p, and the fix text now mentions npx --no <bin>.
  • 01177a9: The GitHub publish action downloads the aval-* artifacts right after its guard (#260). With none, it prints a notice and exits 0 without installing cosign or aval, fetching the policy or requesting an OIDC token, so a publish job that runs on !cancelled() after path-filtered test jobs no longer fails in a repository whose policy is not merged yet. With artifacts and no policy it still exits 1.
  • 311b2fc: aval push accepts a result from a job with other environment variables (#247). aval run writes an env file next to the result (--env-file, default .aval/env.txt, .aval/<test>/env.txt with --test): the fingerprint manifest version, then the manifest's env NAME unset|<sha256> lines, hashes only, neither signed nor published. aval push --env-file FILE takes the env section from it instead of its own environment; every source, dependency, toolchain and contract line is still hashed from the checkout, and the digest must still match the result and the report. A file with another manifest version, a malformed or repeated line, or names other than environment.env exits 1 and publishes nothing; inside the contract scope and outside .aval/ it exits 2, as --result-file does. Without the flag push is unchanged. The publish action passes the artifact's env.txt when the installed aval has the flag, so a variable such as GOTOOLCHAIN=local from setup-go no longer fails the push. No format change: the manifest stays aval-fingerprint/v2. docs/artifact-format.md documents the env file.
  • 5312533: The run action uploads aval-<test> with overwrite: true. Re-running a failed job no longer fails with 409 on the earlier attempt's artifact, and the publish job signs the result of the attempt that just ran. Run each test in only one job per workflow run.
  • 1634652: A symlink to a regular file under a ** source glob now needs only its name in exclude (#258); <link>/** is no longer required, since no path exists under a file. A link to a directory, a dangling link or a loop still needs both. The link is never followed nor hashed; Aval only checks its target's type. The error names the exclude that would fix it. Dropping <link>/** from a contract changes its hash, so the next run is a miss.

docs.title: Patch Changes
docs.text:
• 422352d: The GitHub actions carry a test's outputs from run to publish (#236). aval run --outputs-dir DIR copies the files the outputs globs matched into an empty DIR when it records the result, and aval push --outputs-dir DIR publishes them from there instead of the contract root, refusing (exit 1, nothing published) any entry that is not a regular file matched by an outputs glob: a symlink, an extra file, an input, .git or .aval. The run action passes --outputs-dir .aval/<test>/outputs on a push to the default branch; the publish action passes the artifact's outputs/, so a test with outputs and no outputs/ exits 1 instead of publishing the checkout's files, and it refuses an artifact with any entry outside result.json, report.json, record.json and outputs/. docs/guides/github-actions.md documents the artifact layout. No format change. This closes the known gap noted in 0.8.1 (the publish action could not push a test with outputs). With a pinned release without --outputs-dir (0.8.1), the actions keep running and publishing tests without outputs, and refuse a test with outputs, as aval explain --expand reports it, with exit 1 naming aval v0.8.2 or later, instead of dropping its outputs or signing the checkout's files.
  • 8f78554: The aval run action takes a shadow input (default false): true passes aval run --shadow, so the test runs beside a verified result and a false hit fails the step; any value other than true or false exits 2 before anything runs (#216). The job's AVAL_MIN_TRUST_LEVEL still reaches aval, which only lets it raise the policy's minimum. Aval's own CI now runs its suites through integrations/github/run and publishes through integrations/github/publish: aval.yaml is a kind: TestSet with the tests aval-engine and aval-e2e (same fingerprints as the former aval.yaml and aval.e2e.yaml), one .github/aval/policy.yaml carries the registry and replaces main.yaml and pr.yaml (main and releases raise the minimum to runner), and .github/aval/install.sh, trust-from-base.sh and summary.sh are removed. The release gate verifies with the release the actions pin, under main's policy. No change to the aval binary, its exit codes or formats.
  • 15cc546: Build with Go 1.27.4, which fixes GO-2026-6859 in net/http (govulncheck reports it as reachable from required modules, not from Aval's code).

docs.title: Patch Changes
docs.text:
• 806588c: New guide "Integrate Aval in 5 files" and the example examples/github-monorepo (#217): a monorepo with a Go module, a Node UI, a Dockerfile, a data directory and an end-to-end suite in 3 shards, put on Aval by adding aval.yaml and .github/aval/policy.yaml and editing ci.yml and .gitignore. Aval's tests check that the integration is exactly those files, run every test through the CLI (miss and push, reuse per shard, a fragment edit reruns only its tests, an unaccepted mutable reference, exit 5 on a tampered attestation), and CI checks that the run action ignores a trust policy edited in a pull request. No CLI or format change. Known gap: the GitHub publish action cannot push a test with outputs yet, because the run action's artifact holds .aval/<test>/ only.
  • 6815771: The release gate verifies the e2e attestation with the aval release ci.yaml pins, the one that signed it, instead of a binary built from the tag (#234). A newer aval computes aval-fingerprint/v2, so the gate missed (exit 4) on v0.8.0 and published nothing: the v0.8.0 tag has no GitHub Release, and this patch ships its changes as v0.8.1.

docs.title: Minor Changes
docs.text:
• 7de8cd6: scope.allowMutable entries take an optional files list of globs (#208). One entry accepts its exact ref in every file in scope a glob matches, instead of one entry per file. files excludes file, which stays an exact path; each glob must match a file in scope, otherwise aval exits 2. Format change: an additive optional contract field under the same apiVersion. Existing contracts hash as before; an older aval rejects a contract that uses files (unknown field), which fails closed.
  • b0b968a: Every security event Aval detects now exits 5 (#195). A verified result beside an attestation that failed verification is no longer reused: aval run runs the test and exits 5, and aval verify exits 5 with the unchanged report (outcome verified, the bad attestation in rejected). More than 64 attestations for one fingerprint is now outcome verification-failed (exit 5 in aval run and aval verify) instead of error. The run record of such a run says verification-failed, so aval stats counts it under verificationFailures. Consumers no longer need to inspect rejected: the exit code alone separates miss, error and security event. No new outcome or exit code; the verify report, predicate and fingerprint are unchanged.
  • b518636: New GitHub composite action integrations/github/publish (#212): one step in the consumer's own publish job signs and pushes every aval-<test> artifact the run action uploaded in the workflow run. It refuses any ref but the default branch unless allow-unprotected: true, always refuses pull_request_target and workflow_run, and needs id-token: write; installs the same pinned, verified aval release as the run action; fetches the trust policy from the default branch and pushes to its registry (credentials default to github.actor and github.token); downloads the artifacts into $RUNNER_TEMP; and runs aval push --test <name> per artifact with a fresh OIDC token, trying every artifact and exiting with the worst code (5 is never downgraded). stats: true also publishes each pushed test's run record, best effort. It is a composite action, not a reusable workflow, so the certificate names the calling workflow; CI checks this on Aval's main. No change to the aval binary, its exit codes or formats.
  • 15ade1b: New GitHub composite action integrations/github/run (#211): a CI job runs one test through Aval with uses: TrianaLab/aval/integrations/github/run@<sha> and with: {test: <name>} (inputs file and policy are optional). It refuses pull_request_target, workflow_run and any job with id-token: write; installs the aval release pinned in its action.yml, checked against the per-platform sha256, signature and provenance; fetches the trust policy, and the registry inside it, from the default branch through the contents API on every event (no policy: nothing is reused, with a warning); writes the outcome to the step summary; turns exit 5 into an aval SECURITY error annotation; uploads .aval/<test>/ as the artifact aval-<test> on a push to the default branch only; and warns when the policy trusts a refs/pull/ subject at or above minTrustLevel. The action pins 0.7.0 until the next release, which has --test and the policy's registry (#213). docs/guides/github-actions.md is rewritten around it. No change to the aval binary, its exit codes or formats.
  • ecc519f: aval init --set writes a two-file starting layout (#215): aval.yaml as a kind: TestSet with the test and one fragment holding the source globs, and .github/aval/policy.yaml with one placeholder keyless identity whose anchored subjectRegexp trusts no signer until <OWNER>/<REPO> is replaced. Scope and cacheability stay required. An existing file exits 2 unless --force. No format change.
  • 6a91ec3: The installers can pin and require verification for CI (#202). get-aval.sh --sha256 <hex> (or AVAL_SHA256; <os>_<arch>=<hex> per platform, the entry for the detected platform required) refuses an archive with another digest or one that checksums.txt does not list with it. --require-verify (AVAL_REQUIRE_VERIFY=1) makes a missing cosign an error, --require-provenance (AVAL_REQUIRE_PROVENANCE=1) does the same for gh; both need --version and exclude --no-verify. install.ps1 reads the same variables. Interactive installs behave as before. docs/install.md has a CI recipe, and Aval's own CI installs its pinned release this way.
  • 4f70316: aval run and aval verify take --min-trust-level (or AVAL_MIN_TRUST_LEVEL) to raise the trust policy's minTrustLevel for one run (#214), so one policy can trust developer keys on PRs and require runner on main. A value below the policy's minimum, or an unknown level, exits 2. A result below the raised minimum is a miss (exit 4), never exit 5. The verify report is unchanged. runner.command does not see AVAL_MIN_TRUST_LEVEL.
  • e5cf98f: The trust policy takes an optional registry field (#209). aval run and aval verify use it when neither --registry nor AVAL_REGISTRY is set, and the config: line names the source that won (registry=<x> (policy <file>)). Reading the policy from a protected branch now carries the registry too. A policy registry with credentials (user:password@) exits 2 without printing them.

Format change (additive): kind: Policy gains an optional field under the same apiVersion. Older aval releases reject a policy that uses it (unknown field), which fails closed; policies without it work everywhere. - 83ba4b5: aval push --report-file FILE reads the report written by the aval run that recorded the result (#201). When its outcome is verified, push prints nothing to push: ..., signs nothing and exits 0, so split-credential publishing is one command and a stale result file is not published again. Any other outcome publishes the result as before. A report for another test id or fingerprint, an unknown report version or an unreadable report exits 1. No format changes: the predicate, verify report, fingerprint and exit codes are unchanged. - 1c8baae: aval push --test <name> publishes only the test an artifact is named after (#210). A result or report for another test, or for inputs other than the ones push recomputes from the checkout (a changed file or declared env value), exits 1 and publishes nothing. Behaviour changes: a report that records a security event (outcome verification-failed, or a rejected entry that failed verification) now makes push sign nothing and exit 5, where it used to publish; and aval push never publishes a non-deterministic test, it prints nothing to push: ... and exits 0. aval run --push is unchanged. - 8efc307: New optional contract field scope.root (#200): the path from the contract's directory up to the root of its tree, .. segments only (.., ../..). A contract such as aval/unit.yaml with root: .. behaves as if its file sat in the root: globs, outputs, allowMutable[].file and files, manifest and finding paths, and execution.outputs.files[].path are relative to the root; runner.command and environment.probe run there; the --result-file, --report-file and --stats-file skip set is computed against it. scope.contracts paths stay relative to the contract file. The root must lie inside the git working tree that holds the contract, otherwise aval run, explain, verify and push exit 2. aval explain prints the resolved root. Globs still cannot contain ...

Format changes: additive change to the contract schema (aval.trianalab.io/v1 stays). Contracts without scope.root keep their fingerprint byte for byte; setting or changing it changes the contract manifest line and so the fingerprint. The manifest version (aval-fingerprint/v2) does not change. Older aval binaries reject a contract that uses the field. - a4e260c: -t/--test <name> on aval run, explain, verify and push selects one test of a contract file (#207). A TestSet of more than one test without --test exits 2 and lists the names; on a kind: Test the flag is optional and must equal metadata.name. With --test the output files default to .aval/<name>/{result,report,record}.json, and aval run removes a stale .aval/<name>/ first; without it nothing changes. aval explain --test <name> --expand prints the expanded standalone kind: Test, and aval explain --all [-o json] fingerprints every test without running anything, reports every failing test by name and exits 2 (or 1). A TestSet expands to at most 1024 tests in total, plain tests included.

Format changes: additive CLI flags only. No new exit code; the verify report, predicate and manifest version do not change. - 013ebd5: The fingerprint skips every entry named exactly .git, whatever its type (#199). A linked worktree or a submodule has a .git file that holds a machine-specific path; a ** source glob used to hash it, so the main checkout, each worktree and each machine got a different fingerprint for the same commit and scope. They now share one, and the exclude: ["**/.git"] workaround is no longer needed. A .git symlink is skipped instead of failing the fingerprint. The match stays case-sensitive (.GIT is still an input). An exact glob such as source: ["pkg/.git"] now matches no file and fails the fingerprint (exit 1, matched no files). outputs skip a .git file too, so it is never published.

Format changes: the fingerprint manifest moves from aval-fingerprint/v1 to aval-fingerprint/v2. Every existing attestation becomes a miss once, so each test runs again and publishes a v2 result; there is no fallback lookup by v1. - 26058a5: New contract kind kind: TestSet (#206): many tests in one file, with defaults, named fragments a test pulls in with use, and a matrix that creates one test per value. Merge order is defaults, the used fragments, then the test; lists are unioned, so nothing inherited is removed, and a toolchain, probe or scope.root key set to two values exits 2 naming both sources. matrix substitutes {var} into metadata.name and runner.command only. Each test expands to a standalone kind: Test and fingerprints byte for byte like it. Unknown or unused fragments, a fragment that uses another or sets exclude, runner, metadata, outputs, matrix or cacheability, an unknown {var}, duplicate expanded names and a scope.contracts entry that points at a TestSet exit 2. aval run, explain, verify and push take a TestSet of one test; selecting one test of many comes with #207.

Format changes: additive new kind under aval.trianalab.io/v1. Older aval binaries reject kind: TestSet with exit 2 (fail closed). The manifest version (aval-fingerprint/v2) does not change.

docs.title: Patch Changes
docs.text:
• f8dbb8a: aval run no longer exits 1 when an environment.probe fails without --push (#197). It still looks nothing up (outcome error), runs the test and records nothing to --result-file, so aval push cannot publish the result; it now warns result not recorded: <reason> and exits with the test's code (0 passed, 3 failed). With --push it still exits 1 (result not published: <reason>), or 3 when the test failed. No new exit code or outcome; the verify report, predicate and fingerprint are unchanged.
  • fb575db: aval run no longer loops without end when runner.command starts aval run on the same contract again, directly or through other contracts (#196). It passes AVAL_RUN_STACK to runner.command, and a nested run of a contract already in it exits 2; the outer run records the test as failed (exit 3). A nested run of a different contract still works. environment.env may no longer list AVAL_RUN_STACK. No format changes: the fingerprint, predicate and verify report are unchanged.
  • 21f9727: After each release, the release workflow opens a PR that moves the aval version and per-platform sha256 pinned in integrations/github/run and integrations/github/publish to that release, from its checksums.txt (#213). Pinning either action by commit SHA pins the aval binary too, and one Dependabot bump upgrades both. tests/release fails when a pin does not match the pinned release's checksums.txt. No change to the aval binary, its exit codes or formats.
  • 9cc6596: The fingerprint no longer refuses a symlink that scope.exclude covers by name and contents, such as node_modules/.bin/tool under pkg/** with **/node_modules/** excluded (#198). The symlink is skipped, not followed, and stays out of the manifest. A symlink a dependencies glob reaches, or one excluded only by name or only by its contents, is still an error. No format changes: every tree that fingerprinted before keeps its fingerprint.

docs.title: Minor Changes
docs.text:
• f5c436b: New aval explain [--digest]: it prints fingerprint manifest for <test> (aval-fingerprint/v1), the manifest, and fingerprint sha256:... as the last line; --digest prints only the digest. It never looks up a result and never runs the test; a fingerprint error exits 1 with aval: fingerprint: ..., as run --explain does. run --explain and run --fingerprint-only keep their behaviour. New aval stats publish FILE publishes a run record and replaces aval record. Flags are named for what they hold; the old names keep working, hidden from help, and print a deprecation notice on stderr only (stdout, files and exit codes are unchanged). Deprecated in 0.7.0, removable no earlier than 0.8.0:

  • aval run --result and aval push --result: use --result-file

  • aval run --report: use --report-file
  • aval run --record: use --stats
  • aval run --record-file: use --stats-file
  • aval run --repository and aval record --repository: use --source-repo
  • aval record --record-file FILE: use aval stats publish FILE

Messages that name these flags use the new names (for example --stats requires --registry), and aval record without a file now says a run record file is required. The browser demo accepts aval explain and aval explain --digest. - f5c436b: --registry and --policy fall back to AVAL_REGISTRY and AVAL_POLICY (flag > environment > unset; an empty value counts as unset). There is no config file and no aval.yaml field: an architecture test keeps the registry and policy out of the contract and out of any file in the tree. When a value comes from the environment, aval run prints one config: line on stdout, and verify, push, stats and record print it on stderr. runner.command no longer sees AVAL_REGISTRY and AVAL_POLICY, like the signing token. aval record without --record-file now says --record-file is required. Exit codes and the verify report are unchanged. - f5c436b: Error messages say what to do (#167). Exit codes, outcomes and the verify report are unchanged: a report's reason keeps the raw error.

  • A registry that cannot be dialled or does not answer in time reads cannot reach <host> (<cause>); is the registry running? check AVAL_REGISTRY or --registry: in aval run's reuse-off warning, on stderr for aval verify (stdout unchanged), and for push, run --push and stats publish.
  • --registry with a scheme says drop https://: try --registry <host/name> (exit 2, as before).
  • A public key passed as --key says <x>.pub is a public key; pass the private key (<x>.key).
  • Signing without a key, a token or a terminal lists the three ways to sign, one indented line each.
  • aval push without a saved result adds run aval run first, or use aval run --push (exit 1, as before).
  • aval run --push --key with a policy that does not list the key warns aval: warning: key <file> (key id <x>) is not in <policy>; consumers with this policy will reject the result. The result is still published.
  • Contract errors print as aval: <file>: invalid contract: and one indented, escaped line per problem, in YAML terms: line 8: scope.sources: unknown field; did you mean source?, line 6: runner.command: got a string ..., want a list of strings. The browser demo prints them the same way.
  • f5c436b: aval --help groups commands into Core, Publishing and Statistics, and every command has an example. A mistyped command gets a suggestion (aval rn and aval help rn print unknown command "rn"; did you mean "run"? and exit 2; aval help rn used to print the root help and exit 0). A mistyped flag gets the closest flag of that command and a pointer to its help (unknown flag: --registy; did you mean --registry? see aval run --help). aval run --help is shorter. The exit code constants are unchanged; aval help <typo> now exits 2 (usage) instead of 0.
  • f5c436b: aval init --name NAME --source GLOB... --cacheability CLASS --key NAME|--keyless [--force] -- <command> writes aval.yaml (validated before it is written), with --key a signing key pair (NAME.key and NAME.pub) and policy.yaml trusting it at trust level developer, and adds the key and .aval/ to .gitignore. Nothing is inferred: --source and --cacheability have no default, init lists the files the globs match, rejects a glob that matches nothing and never runs the test. It never replaces a file without --force (exit 1); with --force it removes the old file and creates a new one, so a symlink is replaced, not written through, and a failed write removes the key pair it wrote. A file name in the preview or an answer is escaped before it reaches the terminal. When a value is missing it asks numbered questions only if stdin and stdout are terminals; otherwise it exits 2 and names the missing flags. The quickstart now starts with aval init.
  • f5c436b: aval keygen [name] writes a signing key without openssl: name.key (unencrypted PKCS#8 ECDSA P-256 PEM, mode 0600) and name.pub (PKIX PEM, the file a policy trusts with publicKey), with aval as the default name (a trailing .key is dropped; an empty name is a usage error, exit 2). It prints the key id the verify report shows for this signer and refuses to replace either file without --force (exit 1). The key hints of aval run --push and aval push now point to aval keygen, and the quickstart and the uv-monorepo example no longer need openssl.

  • f5c436b: Plain output of aval run v2 (CI logs and pipes). Every line CI greps today keeps its shape: <outcome> <test> <digest>, signer:, reference:, reason:, rejected:, ran <test>: <result> (exit N), reused <result> result, pushed, restored, recorded, config:. aval verify text and -o json are unchanged, and so are all exit codes. Changed lines:

  • Added: --- run <test>: <command> before and --- end <test>: <passed|failed> (exit N) in <time> after the test's own output, which passes through untouched.

  • Added: a closing summary: <test> <ran|reused>: <passed|failed>[ in <time>][; saved <time>][; result pushed][; reuse was off][; SECURITY]. saved is the reused run's signed finishedAt minus startedAt, for display only.
  • Added on stderr: aval: warning: reuse off: <cause> when an unreadable policy, a registry error or inputs that cannot be fingerprinted turn reuse off. The test still runs.
  • When the test command cannot start, --- run is not closed and no summary: follows; stderr says aval: running "<command>": ... and the exit code stays 1.
  • A fingerprint flooded with more attestations than Aval lists (#135) is a security event in aval run too: no reuse-off warning, ; SECURITY in the summary and the flooding SECURITY line repeated last on stderr. The exit code is unchanged.
  • On a verification failure aval run prints the aval: SECURITY: line when it finds it and again as the last stderr line, after any other error.
  • The SECURITY lines link to https://aval.run/<version>/trust-model/ (latest for dev, snapshot and pre-release builds) instead of the GitHub file.
  • Removed: test <name> fingerprint <digest> (the outcome line carries the digest), the cacheability <class>: ... note when the reason already names the class, and aval: test failed / aval: reused result failed: test failed (the summary and exit 3 say it).
  • Reworded reasons in aval run: no registry configured: pass --registry to reuse verified results is now reuse off: no registry (set AVAL_REGISTRY or --registry), reuse disabled (--no-reuse) is now reuse off: --no-reuse, and a missing policy is reuse off: no trust policy (set AVAL_POLICY or --policy). The outcome stays miss. aval verify keeps no trust policy configured: pass --policy to reuse verified results.
  • The browser demo prints the same lines.
  • The quickstart GIFs still show the old output until they are re-recorded (#181).
  • f5c436b: aval run on a terminal prints the styled output of Epic 13 (style A): one line per step behind a glyph (✓ done, ↺ reused, ✗ failed or SECURITY, ⚠ reuse off, · neutral), labelled detail lines, digests as 8 hex characters (whole on the REJECTED line), and one closing sentence. A flooded fingerprint and a non-deterministic contract get their own closing sentence. After a verification failure nothing is green and no ✓ appears; the SECURITY block goes to stderr when found, and stderr still ends with the plain aval: SECURITY: line. NO_COLOR drops the colour only, Windows gets no colour, and stderr is styled only when it is a terminal too. Plain output is unchanged and applies when stdout is not a terminal, with TERM=dumb, AVAL_OUTPUT=plain (any case) or the new global --plain flag. The browser demo accepts aval run --plain. Exit codes, -o json, the report file and aval verify are unchanged. The browser demo uses the styled form without colour.
  • f5c436b: aval verify -o json (verify-report/v1) gains the optional signer.trustLevelName (developer, runner or isolated) next to the numeric signer.trustLevel. It is derived from the matched trust-policy entry, never from the predicate. Additive: older reports still parse, and in pkg/evidence MatchIdentity and MatchSigner now set Identity.TrustLevelName. Older aval binaries (0.4.0 and earlier) do not recognise a report with this field as Aval output, so such a file in scope counts as an ordinary input for them (a miss, never a false hit) until they upgrade.
