• f5c436b: The quickstart follows the new flow: it removes a leftover registry before starting one, exports AVAL_REGISTRY and AVAL_POLICY once after aval init, and runs aval run --push, aval verify, aval run, a changed input and an untrusted push (AVAL_POLICY= aval run --push --key other.key) that ends in exit 5, with no flags repeated. The GIFs are re-recorded in the styled output, and the "Try it" terminal's help describes the same setup.
  • f5c436b: On a terminal, Aval shows a spinner on stderr when looking up and fetching a result, pushing one (aval run --push, aval push) or reading run records (aval stats) takes more than 300ms, for example ⠹ looking up localhost:5001… 4s. It runs only in styled mode with stderr a terminal, is erased before the decision or the test's output prints, erases itself before a warning, and leaves the terminal clean on Ctrl-C. Windows gets no spinner. Plain output, exit codes and aval verify are unchanged.
  • 6677ad3: Docs site: the install command on the home page has a copy button.
  • f5c436b: Shorter docs: each page answers one question in its first line and opens with a diagram or a terminal snippet; guides and concept pages use short bullets and tables. Edge cases moved to two new Reference pages: CLI output (plain and terminal output, spinner, stderr lines) and Mutable reference scan (the full scanner rules and limits from Pin your dependencies). No behaviour changes.
  • 58d3f3c: Docs site: on phones narrower than about 430px the version pill no longer overlaps the theme toggle in the header; it is hidden there.

docs.title: Patch Changes
docs.text: • a0395af: aval upgrade names the HTTP status when GitHub answers the latest-release lookup with something other than a redirect (for example 504 Gateway Timeout during a GitHub incident), instead of no Location header in response. Nothing is downloaded or replaced in that case, as before.

docs.title: Minor Changes
docs.text: • 750feac: New aval version (prints aval <version> (<go version> <os>/<arch>)) and aval upgrade [--version vX.Y.Z] [--check]. upgrade resolves the latest release from the GitHub Releases redirect (no API call), verifies the keyless Sigstore signature of checksums.txt against Aval's release workflow at that tag, checks the archive's sha256 against its exact entry, and only then replaces the running binary atomically on Unix (on Windows the old one is kept as aval.exe.old and moved back if the swap fails). Without --version it refuses to move to an older release. Any failed check replaces nothing and exits 1; downloads are capped at 256 MiB (1 MiB for checksums.txt and its bundle).

docs.title: Minor Changes
docs.text:
• 028329d: A contract can list outputs (globs such as coverage.xml, junit.xml): run --push and push publish those files with the result, and a reused result restores them, so a coverage gate or a junit report downstream keeps working when the test is skipped. Outputs must not be inputs or the contract file, each glob must match a regular file, and the caps are 256 files, 16 MiB each and 64 MiB in total; otherwise nothing is published (exit 1). On reuse the files are fetched by the digests the signature covers; a missing, changed or undeclared output is a verification failure (exit 5). Format changes, all additive: contract field outputs (omitted when empty, so existing fingerprints do not change; older aval binaries reject a contract that uses it), predicate field execution.outputs within execution/v2, and the OCI identifiers application/vnd.trianalab.aval.outputs.v1 and application/vnd.trianalab.aval.output.v1. Outputs are published to the registry: do not list files that hold secrets.
  • b3758d5: The mutable-reference scanner now reports container images named in test code that uses testcontainers: a quoted name:tag without a digest in a *.go, *.py, *.java, *.kt, *.ts, *.js or *.cs file that mentions testcontainers. Adopters may see new findings that turn hits into misses for hermetic and controlled-environment tests: pin the image by digest, or accept it in scope.allowMutable.
  • 318966e: New optional environment.probe in aval.yaml (additive to aval.trianalab.io/v1; older aval binaries reject contracts that use it): a map from an environment.toolchain key to an argv such as python: [python3, --version]. aval run runs each probe before the lookup, without a shell, with a 10 s timeout and without $SIGSTORE_ID_TOKEN, and requires the declared value in the output as a version token (3.13 matches Python 3.13.1, not Python 3.130). A mismatch, a probe that cannot start, a non-zero exit, a timeout or output over 4 KiB skips the lookup (outcome error), runs the test, records and publishes nothing and exits 1. The observed output goes into execution.environment as probe.<key>. verify, push, --fingerprint-only and the browser demo never run probes. Fix: a toolchain key named os or arch no longer overwrites the real values in execution.environment.

docs.title: Patch Changes
docs.text:
• 554569c: Adoption guides: find undeclared inputs with strace, fs_usage, Process Monitor or a scope-only copy (Write a contract); map uv, pnpm and cargo workspaces to contracts (Depend on another part of the repo); estimate reuse from past commits with scripts/estimate-reuse.sh, which runs aval run --fingerprint-only over a scratch worktree and counts fingerprint errors and unacknowledged mutable references as misses (Measure reuse).
  • 176cfc2: Docs: the guide "Shards and matrices" shows two ways to split a suite across CI matrix jobs with existing fields: one contract per shard (aval.shard-1.yaml, run with -f) or one contract with SHARD_INDEX and SHARD_TOTAL in environment.env. New example examples/uv-monorepo: a uv workspace with two packages, two shard contracts and coverage restored on reuse. No behaviour or format change.

docs.title: Minor Changes
docs.text: • 4c8029a: run --push and push sign keyless from a laptop: without --key or $SIGSTORE_ID_TOKEN and with a terminal (or with the new --login flag), they open the interactive Sigstore login in the browser (oauth2.sigstore.dev, client id sigstore; $SIGSTORE_OIDC_ISSUER and $SIGSTORE_OIDC_CLIENT_ID override them) right before signing, after the test ran. The token is used for that signature only and never stored. Without a terminal and without --login, a run with no key and no token still fails fast with exit 2. --key and --login exclude each other.

docs.title: Patch Changes
docs.text: • b619b24: More than 64 attestations for a fingerprint now prints an aval: SECURITY: line naming the cap, as a possible flooding attempt; the outcome stays error and the test runs. Aval's own CI and release jobs fail when a verify report lists a verification failure in rejected, even when a trusted result verified.

docs.title: Minor Changes
docs.text:
• 4b68dd5: aval stats --registry <repo> [--test <id>] [--since <duration|date>] [--by test|repository] [--output text|json] reads the run records in the registry and aggregates them on demand: runs, hit rate, misses by cause, verification failures, shadow false hits, and total and saved test time, per test (or per source repository with --by repository) and in total. It writes nothing. Records that are unreadable, oversized, malformed or inconsistent are skipped and counted; reading stops after 1000 records or 64 pages per listing, with a warning. New format, provisional: aval.trianalab.io/stats-report/v1 (pkg/evidence adds StatsReport, TestStats, RepositoryStats, RunStats, MissCauses, StatsReportVersion and StatsUnknownRepository). Run records gain the optional verifiedResult and repository (--repository on aval run and aval record; records without it count as unknown), and evidence.ParseRunRecord now rejects inconsistent records (reused: true requires outcome verified and testDurationMs 0; verifiedResult requires outcome verified), so aval record refuses a hand-edited record that claims a reuse that never happened. Docs explain pruning old records with ORAS.
  • 6351105: Registry I/O is bounded. run, verify and push take --registry-timeout (default 1m). A registry that stalls past the timeout gives outcome error, and aval run still runs the test. Lookup follows at most 64 referrers pages. A listed attestation whose manifest was deleted (404) counts as absent: the remaining candidates can still be reused, and the outcome is a miss if every candidate is gone. One credential store and one auth cache are shared by every registry call. The keyless trusted root (a TUF fetch when trustedRoot is not pinned) is loaded only when a candidate's bundle carries a certificate. After pushing, push and run --push confirm that the new digest is listed among the referrers, re-pushing up to three times, and fail if it never appears.
  • 7cd688f: Aval detects mutable references in a test's inputs and refuses to reuse them. A static, offline scanner reads the files in the contract scope and runner.command, one detector per ecosystem: container images without a digest (Compose and Kubernetes image:, Dockerfile FROM and COPY --from, docker run and podman run, compose files the command uses but the scope does not hold), Go (go.mod without go.sum, go install pkg@latest), npm, yarn, pnpm and bun (package.json without a lockfile, unpinned npm i and npx), Python (unpinned requirements*.txt entries, missing hashes, Poetry and Pipenv without a lockfile, unpinned pip install), Rust (Cargo.toml without Cargo.lock), Java (Maven and Gradle SNAPSHOT, LATEST, RELEASE, dynamic versions and ranges), Ruby (Gemfile without Gemfile.lock), PHP (composer.json without composer.lock), OS packages (apt-get install and apk add without versions), remote scripts (curl … | sh, remote ADD without --checksum) and git (git clone without a commit, submodules that track a branch). For hermetic and controlled-environment contracts any unacknowledged finding makes the lookup a miss (exit 4 for verify) whose reason lists each reference, the test runs, and run --push and push do not publish (exit 1). external-dependencies contracts get the findings as information; non-deterministic is unchanged. aval run prints each finding as a mutable: line (--fingerprint-only prints them on stderr). Contract format change, additive within aval.trianalab.io/v1: the optional scope.allowMutable list (ref and reason) acknowledges a reference by the exact text Aval reports. It is part of the contract hash; contracts without it keep their fingerprint, and the manifest stays aval-fingerprint/v1. Older aval binaries reject contracts that use the new field. A contract whose scope holds a mutable reference that earlier versions reused now misses until the reference is pinned or acknowledged. Guide: "Pin your dependencies" (docs/pinning.md).
  • 0e259b7: Aval resolves declared artifacts to immutable ids at fingerprint time. The optional scope.resolve list takes kind: reference entries for container images (image, tag to manifest or index digest), npm, PyPI, Go modules (through the module proxy, h1: hash), Maven, crates.io, RubyGems, git (ref to commit with git ls-remote) and plain URLs (sha256 of the download, up to 256 MiB). Each resolves a tag, a version range or a branch to its digest, checksum or commit, which goes into the manifest as a resolve <kind> <reference> <version> <id> line: a repushed tag, a new release inside a range or a moved branch changes the fingerprint. Resolution is opt-in and stateless, bounded by a 2-minute deadline; a reference that cannot be resolved fails the fingerprint, so nothing is looked up, the test runs and nothing is published, and the reason names the reference. aval run --explain prints the time each lookup took on stderr. scope.resolve never clears a finding of the mutable-reference scanner: it makes a move change the fingerprint, and the reference still blocks reuse until it is pinned in place or accepted with scope.allowMutable. scope.resolve binds the named artifact, not its transitive dependencies. Registries come from $npm_config_registry, $GOPROXY, $AVAL_PYPI_URL, $AVAL_MAVEN_URL, $AVAL_CRATES_INDEX and $AVAL_RUBYGEMS_URL; credentials from the Docker config, ~/.npmrc tokens, ~/.netrc machine entries and git, sent only over https or to a loopback host. Format changes, additive: the contract field within aval.trianalab.io/v1 (older binaries reject contracts that use it), and the resolve manifest lines within aval-fingerprint/v1, which only contracts with the field have; every other manifest is unchanged. Guide: "Resolve references" (docs/resolve/).
  • 8d4b8d8: Run statistics in the registry. aval run --record publishes one run record per run, for every outcome, with the test id, fingerprint, outcome, whether the result was reused, the result, the test duration, the saved duration, the aval version, a timestamp and an optional --ci-run-url. Records hang off a per-test stats anchor tagged stats-<test id>, never off a fingerprint anchor. run and verify never read them, so a record cannot cause reuse or count toward the candidate cap. Recording is best-effort: a record that cannot be published, for example without write credentials, is a warning and never changes the exit code. --record-file writes the record to a file and aval record publishes it later. New format identifiers, provisional: aval.trianalab.io/run-record/v1, application/vnd.trianalab.aval.run.v1 (+json for the layer) and application/vnd.trianalab.aval.stats.v1. pkg/evidence adds RunRecord, ParseRunRecord and these constants.
  • ff2a2c8: A contract can depend on other contracts in the same repository. The optional scope.contracts list takes paths to other aval.yaml files, relative to the contract (../backend/aval.yaml). Each referenced contract is fingerprinted from its own directory and scope, and its fingerprint goes into the manifest as a contract <path> <name> <fingerprint> line, transitively: a change inside a referenced contract's scope makes the dependent miss and run, a change outside it does not. References must stay inside the git working tree of the contract (the nearest directory with a .git entry); a missing, invalid, symlinked or cyclic reference, or more than 8 levels or 64 contracts, fails the fingerprint, so the test runs. A referenced contract's mutable references block the dependent's reuse unless the referenced contract's own scope.allowMutable accepts them. aval run --explain prints the dependency tree after the manifest. Format changes, additive: the contract field within aval.trianalab.io/v1 (older binaries reject contracts that use it), and the contract <path> manifest lines within aval-fingerprint/v1, which only contracts with the field have; every other manifest is unchanged. Guide: "Depend on another part of the repo".
  • 6b94c21: One-line installers: scripts/get-aval.sh (Linux and macOS, curl | bash) and scripts/install.ps1 (Windows, irm | iex). Both refuse a download whose sha256 does not match the release's checksums.txt, and verify the release signature (cosign) and SLSA provenance (gh attestation verify) when those tools are installed. See docs/install.md.

docs.title: Patch Changes
docs.text:
• 0553f1e: scope.allowMutable entries take an optional file: (the path a finding prints, relative to the contract, or runner.command): the entry then accepts the reference in that file only. A ref-only entry still accepts a reference that one file reports; when several files report it (generic refs such as resources[0] or patches[0] repeat across kustomizations), nothing is accepted and the finding asks for file:. With scope.contracts, each contract's entries apply to its own findings. The scanner also reports kustomize helmCharts entries other than a local chart in the scope, and patches given by a path outside the scope; checks instructions behind ONBUILD; uses the # escape= character when it splits heredoc words; and no longer reports a range loop's key variable used as a key directly under labels: or annotations: in a Helm template. Since the previous release, image refs in JSON files ("image": "postgres:16",) no longer end in ",: update an acknowledgement written with the trailing characters to the bare reference (postgres:16).
  • 2df8ee2: A signer the trust policy lists but below minTrustLevel is now reported as miss (exit 4), and with outcome miss in the verify report's rejected list, instead of verification-failed (exit 5). Such an attestation is still never reused, and a false claim from that signer stays verification-failed. The report stays aval.trianalab.io/verify-report/v1; rejected[].outcome may now also be miss. Rejected verification failures are printed with the aval: SECURITY: prefix even when another candidate verifies. evidence.Verify is unchanged.
  • e5497e1: --registry-timeout help no longer claims "push has its own" deadline on aval push, aval record and aval stats; only aval run says lookup and fetch share one. Shorter aval run, aval record and aval stats help. The docs site is shorter and single-sourced: the README links into the site instead of copying the quickstart, and the resolver pages and vision move under Reference and Project.
  • 7fae6b0: The fingerprint no longer hashes Aval's own outputs: .aval directories at any depth, and the --result and --report paths of the command when they fall inside the contract root. A broad scope such as scope.source: ["**"] now keeps its fingerprint across aval runs, and aval push accepts the result aval run recorded. The manifest format stays aval-fingerprint/v1: trees with no Aval output in scope keep byte-identical manifests and digests (the committed v1 golden and Aval's own contracts are unchanged). Only manifests that listed a file under .aval/ or a --result/--report file change, to the manifest of the same tree without those files. Such a manifest held a result from an earlier run, so it changed on every run and was not reusable in practice; results published from a clean checkout (no Aval output yet) keep their fingerprint and stay reusable. .aval/ is now reserved for Aval: a file the test reads must not live there.
  • 91a57b8: run --push and push check their preconditions before anything runs and exit 2 (usage) instead of failing with exit 1 after the test: a --key that cannot be read or is not an unencrypted ECDSA P-256 PEM key (the error names the requirement and the openssl command to create one; cosign keys are encrypted and not supported), or no --key and no $SIGSTORE_ID_TOKEN. run, verify and push reject a --registry that is not an OCI repository (a scheme, no repository, a tag or a digest) with exit 2 and an example. A --result or --report path that the contract scope includes and that holds a real input (anything other than an Aval result or report) exits 2 before the test runs, because skipping it would drop that input from the fingerprint; run also refuses to overwrite any existing file at those paths that is not exactly an Aval result or report. Exit codes keep their values; only these cases move from exit 1 to the existing exit 2.
  • c7c5888: Docs site: live run statistics. The home metric strip and a new Stats page (Project > Stats) read stats.json, which the docs workflow rebuilds twice an hour and on every push from aval stats --by repository --since 30d over the public stats registry ghcr.io/trianalab/aval-stats, without rebuilding any page; a failed refresh keeps the previous file, and a missing or stale file shows a neutral state. Aval's own CI now publishes its run records there. The Stats page explains how to keep statistics in your own registry and how a repository joins the public aggregate.
  • f14b7b4: Docs site: the mobile menu (hamburger) now slides in the site navigation on every page. On inner pages the panel opened under the dark overlay; on the home page there was no panel at all. make docs-nav-smoke, part of make ci-docs, opens the menu at a phone width on the home page and an inner page and checks the panel is on screen with links.
  • 133adf0: The README now has an Install section and a local quickstart (registry:2, an openssl P-256 key, aval run --push --key, aval verify) that reaches verified; an acceptance test runs it as written. A missing aval.yaml and a pre-freeze aval.dev/ apiVersion (contract or policy) now print a next step. aval verify --help lists exit codes 1 and 2, and docs/cli-reference.md has one exit-code table for every command. New docs: registry credentials, the network and HOME needs of keyless verification and how to pin trustedRoot, and the 64-candidate cap with its cleanup.
  • ed37d7e: New docs Quickstart page: copy-paste steps with the expected output from an empty folder to a verified reuse, a changed input and a rejected attestation (exit 5), with terminal recordings of real runs and a "what just happened" diagram; an acceptance test runs the page and checks every output it shows. make docs-demos re-records the GIFs from VHS tapes. The Install page now shows a manual release download with cosign and checksum checks.
  • 5871b37: Readable errors and reasons. Output escapes only control and non-printable characters (quotes and backslashes print as they are), and each cause of a joined error gets its own aval: line (an invalid contract) or is separated by ; in the report reason (an invalid policy). A reason is printed once, in the report: stderr no longer repeats it, and a verification failure adds a single aval: SECURITY: ... line that links to docs/trust-model.md. A signer missing from the policy gets the reason signer key id "<id>" is not in the trust policy (trust policy <file>) instead of the Sigstore error. Skipped lookups (no policy, no registry, --no-reuse, a cacheability class that is never or not allowed to be reused) say only why they did not look; they stay misses. No attest.Sign: or registry.Lookup prefixes reach users. Text-mode verify prints signer: (with the trust level name) and reference: lines for a verified result. non-deterministic is called "never reusable" everywhere. The JSON verify report is unchanged except for the wording of reason, where joined causes are now separated by ;.
  • cb81760: scope.resolve detects registry overrides as the tools read them. pip variables match in any spelling pip reads (PIP_ then any letter case, - equal to _, one optional leading --: PIP_index-url, PIP___INDEX_URL). ~/.npmrc is read as ini, like npm: quotes stripped from keys and values, ; and # comments, keys under a [section] ignored, ${VAR} expanded in keys and values as npm does (an undefined variable stays literal); a line Aval cannot read (including one with U+2028 or U+2029, or a quoted key or value that is JSON other than a string) fails the fingerprint and sends no token. A floating Maven version fails when <latest> or <release> is a SNAPSHOT or not in <versions>. Errors show only the host of a URL, so a token in a registry path (https://npm-proxy.fury.io/<token>/user/) is masked too.
  • 9082a6c: pkg/evidence: ErrNotImplemented, Verification.TrustLevel (use Verification.Signer.TrustLevel) and Runner.Issuer/Runner.TrustLevel are deprecated; nothing is removed. Pushing an attestation without a Sigstore bundle is now refused, since it could never verify. Keyless signing always uses the Sigstore public-good instance, as the CLI already did.
  • 9556f78: The mutable-reference scanner adds parser-based detection to its line-by-line pass, which still runs on every file it ran on before, so it finds everything it found before. Dockerfiles named as such (Dockerfile, Containerfile, Dockerfile.*, Dockerfile-dev, Dockerfile_windows, *.dockerfile) are also split the way BuildKit does: a comment line ending in \ no longer swallows the next instruction, continued lines join with nothing (FROM db:1\ then 6 is db:16), comment and blank lines inside a continuation are dropped, a leading # escape= sets the continuation character, and heredoc bodies are kept apart. YAML is also decoded: image: keys are matched by their decoded value ("ima\x67e":, ? image, !!binary, tagged, anchored or alias keys, nested sequences), after an anchor or an empty flow value, or after a lone CR, NEL or LS line break. The scanner also reports kustomize images: and imageTags: entries with newName, newTag or tagSuffix and no digest, kustomize patches, replacements, transformers, generators and helmCharts that set an image (by ref, such as patches[0]), kind: ImageTagTransformer, images in Helm *.tpl helpers, RUN --mount=...,from= images, JSON manifests under templates/ or listed in kustomize resources, Compose build.dockerfile_inline and docker-image:// additional_contexts, and every name of a multi-name or lowercase Dockerfile ARG. What Aval reports because it cannot tell (a templated key in a Helm template, a YAML key with an unknown tag or an undecodable escape, an undecodable heredoc name, a FROM image with a variable that is not a global ARG with a value, a kustomize resource that is remote or outside the scope (resources[2]), a tagged key in a template the parser rejects, a Dockerfile BuildKit refuses) is in the container ecosystem, so scope.allowMutable can acknowledge it; only an unreadable or oversized file stays in scan. A shell continuation at the very end of a file is no longer dropped. docs/pinning.md now says the scanner is a best-effort safety net and lists its known limits.
  • 59adaf5: The installers are served from the docs site: curl -fsSL https://aval.run/install.sh | bash and irm https://aval.run/install.ps1 | iex. The site root redirects to the latest release (to main before the first one), and the outdated-version banner shows only on releases older than latest, never on main.
  • 6a2a118: aval stats finds run records on registries that do not sort tags, such as GHCR: it lists every tag and filters by the stats- prefix instead of starting the listing after stats. Up to 64 pages of tags are read (6400 tags at a registry page size of 100); past that the report carries a truncation warning.
  • 843f7a3: A symlink in the contract directory under which a source or dependencies glob could match files (for example pkg/sub -> /elsewhere with **/*.go), now fails the fingerprint with an error naming the path. Before, it was skipped, so edits behind it kept the same fingerprint and a stale result could be reused. A symlink no glob can reach is still ignored, and a contract directory that is itself a symlink fingerprints like its target.
  • 27d7391: Try Aval in the browser: click the terminal on the home page of the docs site (or its "Try it live" button) and it runs the real Aval compiled to WebAssembly, with a simulated test, an in-memory registry and a throwaway key generated in the browser. It supports aval run (a miss, then a verified reuse), aval run --explain, aval verify -o json, edit <file>, tamper (the next verify fails with exit 5), reset and help. Nothing is fetched until the visitor clicks the terminal or presses a key in it, and without WebAssembly the page keeps the recorded transcript. Keyless signing is not available in the browser.

docs.title: Minor Changes
docs.text: • 0148c76: Formats are frozen. The contract and policy apiVersion is now aval.trianalab.io/v1 and the verify report version is aval.trianalab.io/verify-report/v1; aval.dev/v1alpha1 contracts and policy files are rejected, so change that line in yours. The contract hash covers apiVersion, so results published before are misses and each test runs once. The predicate type (https://aval.trianalab.io/attestation/execution/v2), media and artifact types (application/vnd.trianalab.aval.execution.v2, application/vnd.trianalab.aval.fingerprint.v1) and predicate schemaVersion v2 are unchanged and now frozen, so attestations written by v0.1.0 keep a valid, readable format. Compatibility rules (additive changes within a version, what needs a new version, how consumers treat unknown fields and values, deprecation) are in docs/artifact-format.md, and golden files guard the JSON shape of the statement, predicate and verify report.

docs.title: Patch Changes
docs.text:
• c17dc26: aval run and aval verify escape newlines and control characters in reasons printed as text and on stderr, so text from an untrusted attestation cannot start a log line of its own. Aval's own CI now reuses its signed e2e results, and a release requires a verified e2e attestation for its commit.
  • 59b9b66: pkg/evidence is semver-stable Go API: within a major version it changes additively only, and CI fails when an exported identifier is removed or changes type or signature without a new major module path. examples/evidence-consumer is a separate module that consumes Aval evidence through pkg/evidence alone, with its own signature verifier. The policy is in docs/integrations.md.
  • bbf9e55: Fingerprinting fails closed in two more cases: a scope.source glob that matches no file (a typo, or a name that differs on disk by case or Unicode form), and a file excluded only because a trailing ** in exclude matched zero segments (build/** against a file named build). Trees that fingerprinted before and still do keep the same fingerprint. A table-driven false-hit corpus now pins every kind of relevant and irrelevant change.

docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text: Every command, flag and exit code.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Code aval run aval verify aval push 0 the test passed, or a verified passing result was reused a verified result exists (passing or failing) and no attestation failed verification pushed 1 error (the test still runs when it can), or a false hit in --shadow error: registry, policy, trusted root or fingerprint error: signing, registry or a result that does not match the current inputs 2 bad flags or invalid aval.yaml bad flags or invalid aval.yaml bad flags or invalid aval.yaml 3 the test failed, or a verified failing result was reused not used not used 4 not used: a miss runs the test miss: no result the policy can reuse not used 5 verification failed, after running the test: a security event, also beside a verified result (never reused then) or over the 64-attestation cap; wins over 3 and 1 verification failed: a security event, also beside a verified result (the report keeps outcome verified) or over the 64-attestation cap not used 6 reserved, never returned reserved, never returned reserved, never returned

A miss (4) is routine. A verification failure (5) means someone published a result the policy does not trust; never hide it or retry it away.

docs.title: aval
docs.text:
Verifiable test execution reuse: signed test results as OCI artifacts.

--registry and --policy fall back to $AVAL_REGISTRY and $AVAL_POLICY; a flag wins, and an empty value counts as unset (an empty flag too: use --no-reuse to turn reuse off). run and verify then take the registry from the trust policy's registry field. There is no config file.

Usage:
  aval [flags]
  aval [command]

Core:
  explain     Print what the execution fingerprint covers, with the digest last
  gen         Generate one test per unit from a dependency graph into a TestSet
  init        Write aval.yaml, a signing key and a trust policy for a test
  run         Reuse a verified result for the current inputs, or run the test
  verify      Check whether a trusted result exists for the current inputs

Publishing:
  keygen      Create a signing key: name.key and name.pub (default name: aval)
  push        Sign and publish a recorded execution result

Statistics:
  stats       Aggregate the run records in the registry: reuse, misses, time saved

Additional Commands:
  completion  Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
  help        Help about any command
  upgrade     Replace this binary with a verified aval release
  version     Print the aval version, Go version and platform

Flags:
  -h, --help[=true|false]      help for aval
      --plain[=true|false]     plain aval run output even on a terminal, as in CI (also $AVAL_OUTPUT=plain or TERM=dumb)
  -v, --version[=true|false]   version for aval

Use "aval [command] --help" for more information about a command.

docs.title: aval completion
docs.text:
Generate the autocompletion script for aval for the specified shell. See each sub-command's help for details on how to use the generated script.

Usage:
  aval completion [command]

Examples:
  source <(aval completion bash)

Available Commands:
  bash        Generate the autocompletion script for bash
  fish        Generate the autocompletion script for fish
  powershell  Generate the autocompletion script for powershell
  zsh         Generate the autocompletion script for zsh

Flags:
  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for completion

Global Flags:
      --plain[=true|false]   plain aval run output even on a terminal, as in CI (also $AVAL_OUTPUT=plain or TERM=dumb)

Use "aval completion [command] --help" for more information about a command.

docs.title: aval explain
docs.text:
explain prints the fingerprint manifest (every input that was hashed) under a header, then the fingerprint as the last line. --digest prints only the fingerprint. explain never looks up a result and never runs the test; the fingerprint is the one 'aval run' computes with its default --result-file and without --report-file or --stats-file inside the contract root. With scope.root it prints the resolved root after the header. Each scope.optionalSource glob that matched no file is named on stderr.

--expand prints the test as the standalone kind: Test it expands to (a test of a TestSet with defaults, fragments and matrix applied). --all checks every test of the file: it prints one "name fingerprint" line per test (-o json: one object per test), reports every failing test by name instead of stopping at the first, and executes nothing, not even environment.probe.

Exit codes: 0 printed, 1 the fingerprint cannot be computed (unprovable inputs), 2 usage or invalid aval.yaml. With --all, 2 when any failing test is invalid, else 1 when any fingerprint cannot be computed.

Usage:
  aval explain [flags]

Examples:
  # What the fingerprint covers, digest last
  aval explain

  # Only the digest
  aval explain --digest

Flags:
      --all[=true|false]      check and fingerprint every test of the file, one line per test
  -f, --contract string       path to the test contract (default "aval.yaml")
      --digest[=true|false]   print only the fingerprint (sha256:...)
      --expand[=true|false]   print the test as the standalone kind: Test it expands to
  -h, --help[=true|false]     help for explain
  -o, --output string         output format of --all: text or json (default "text")
  -t, --test string           the test to use, by metadata.name: required on a TestSet of more than one test; output files default to .aval/<test>/

Global Flags:
      --plain[=true|false]   plain aval run output even on a terminal, as in CI (also $AVAL_OUTPUT=plain or TERM=dumb)

docs.title: aval gen
docs.text:
gen writes declared scope from a repository's dependency graph into the kind: TestSet in -f. For each unit (a package, module or project) it writes a fragment with the unit's own files and a test that uses the fragments of the unit and of every unit it depends on, both named LANGUAGE.UNIT (such as go.internal.contract). A change to a unit then re-runs its test and the tests of the units that depend on it.

gen owns only the fragments and tests whose names start with "LANGUAGE."; every other line, comments included, is kept as it is. Shared inputs (lockfiles, root build files, toolchain, cacheability) belong in the hand-written defaults. aval run, verify and push never run gen: commit its output and check it in CI with --check.

Languages: js, rust.

Exit codes: 0 written or up to date, 1 error (the language tool failed, the dependency graph is invalid, the file cannot be written) or with --check out of date (the diff is printed), 2 usage (an unknown language, no TestSet at -f, or a result that is not a valid TestSet).

Usage:
  aval gen <language> [flags]

Examples:
  # Write one test per unit into aval.yaml
  aval gen <language>

  # In CI: fail with a diff when aval.yaml is out of date
  aval gen <language> --check

Flags:
      --check[=true|false]   write nothing; exit 1 with a diff when the generated entries are out of date
  -f, --file string          the kind: TestSet to write (default "aval.yaml")
  -h, --help[=true|false]    help for gen

Global Flags:
      --plain[=true|false]   plain aval run output even on a terminal, as in CI (also $AVAL_OUTPUT=plain or TERM=dumb)

docs.title: aval init
docs.text:
init writes aval.yaml for one test, validated before it is written. With --key NAME it also writes the signing key pair (NAME.key and NAME.pub, as keygen does; a trailing .key is dropped) and policy.yaml trusting that key at trust level developer. It adds the key and .aval/ to .gitignore. --keyless writes no key and no policy.

Nothing is inferred: --source and --cacheability have no default, and init never traces the test. It lists the files the source globs match and rejects a glob that matches nothing. It never replaces aval.yaml, policy.yaml or the key without --force. If a write fails after the key pair was written, init removes the key pair again.

--set writes a two-file starting layout instead: aval.yaml as a kind: TestSet with the test and one fragment that holds the source globs, and .github/aval/policy.yaml with one placeholder keyless identity (an anchored subjectRegexp with a placeholder owner and repository that matches nothing until you edit it). It writes no key. Both files are validated before they are written; on an existing file it exits 2 unless --force.

When a value is missing and both stdin and stdout are terminals, init asks for it. Otherwise it exits 2 and names the missing flags.

Exit codes: 0 written, 1 error (a file exists without --force, or cannot be written), 2 usage (a missing value, an invalid contract, a glob that matches nothing, init cancelled, or with --set a file exists without --force).

Usage:
  aval init --name NAME --source GLOB... --cacheability CLASS --key NAME|--keyless|--set [--force] -- <command> [flags]

Examples:
  # Write aval.yaml, aval.key, aval.pub and policy.yaml
  aval init --name unit --source 'src/**' --source go.mod --cacheability hermetic --key aval.key -- go test ./...

  # Start a TestSet: aval.yaml and .github/aval/policy.yaml with a placeholder identity
  aval init --set --name unit --source 'src/**' --cacheability hermetic -- go test ./...

Flags:
      --cacheability string    hermetic, controlled-environment, external-dependencies or non-deterministic
      --force[=true|false]     replace existing aval.yaml, policy.yaml and key files (.github/aval/policy.yaml with --set)
  -h, --help[=true|false]      help for init
      --key string             signing key pair NAME.key and NAME.pub to create and trust in policy.yaml; a trailing .key is dropped
      --keyless[=true|false]   sign keyless with Sigstore: no key and no policy are written
      --name string            test name (metadata.name): what the test checks
      --set[=true|false]       write aval.yaml as a kind: TestSet and .github/aval/policy.yaml with a placeholder identity, no key
      --source stringArray     source glob relative to the current directory (scope.source); repeat it for more

Global Flags:
      --plain[=true|false]   plain aval run output even on a terminal, as in CI (also $AVAL_OUTPUT=plain or TERM=dumb)

docs.title: aval keygen
docs.text:
keygen writes a new ECDSA P-256 signing key to name.key (unencrypted PKCS#8 PEM, mode 0600) and its public key to name.pub, the file a policy trusts with publicKey. It prints the key id the verify report shows for this signer. It refuses to replace either file without --force. A trailing .key in the name is dropped, so "aval keygen ci.key" writes ci.key and ci.pub.

Exit codes: 0 written, 1 error (name.key or name.pub exists without --force, or cannot be written), 2 usage.

Usage:
  aval keygen [name] [flags]

Examples:
  aval keygen        # aval.key and aval.pub
  aval keygen ci     # ci.key and ci.pub

Flags:
      --force[=true|false]   replace name.key and name.pub if they exist
  -h, --help[=true|false]    help for keygen

Global Flags:
      --plain[=true|false]   plain aval run output even on a terminal, as in CI (also $AVAL_OUTPUT=plain or TERM=dumb)

docs.title: aval push
docs.text:
push signs the result recorded by 'aval run' and publishes it. The result must be for the current inputs: same test id, cacheability and fingerprint. --report-file names the report that run wrote with the result: when its outcome is verified (also under --shadow), push publishes nothing and exits 0; when it records a security event (outcome verification-failed, or a rejected attestation that failed verification), push publishes nothing and exits 5. A non-deterministic test is never pushed: push publishes nothing and exits 0. With --test, the result and the report must both be for that test. --outputs-dir reads the contract's outputs from the directory that 'aval run --outputs-dir' filled, not from the contract root: any entry in it that is not a regular file matched by an outputs glob publishes nothing. The directory may be missing only when the contract declares no outputs. --env-file takes the env section of the fingerprint from the file that 'aval run' wrote with the result (hashes of environment.env, no values), not from this process's environment, so a job with other variables can publish it. Every other input is still hashed from the checkout. A file with another manifest version, a malformed or repeated line, or names other than environment.env publishes nothing. Keyless signing reads the OIDC token from $SIGSTORE_ID_TOKEN. Without --key or $SIGSTORE_ID_TOKEN, signing on a terminal (or with --login) opens the interactive Sigstore login in the browser; no token is stored.

Usage:
  aval push [flags]

Examples:
  aval push --registry ghcr.io/acme/orders-aval --key aval.key

Flags:
  -f, --contract string             path to the test contract (default "aval.yaml")
      --env-file string             take the env section of the fingerprint from this file ('aval run --env-file') instead of this process's environment
  -h, --help[=true|false]           help for push
      --key string                  signing key path (default: keyless OIDC)
      --login[=true|false]          sign keyless after the interactive Sigstore login, even without a terminal (overrides: $SIGSTORE_OIDC_ISSUER, $SIGSTORE_OIDC_CLIENT_ID)
      --outputs-dir string          read the contract's outputs from this directory ('aval run --outputs-dir') instead of the contract root; anything in it that is not a declared output publishes nothing
      --registry string             OCI repository for attestations and run records, e.g. ghcr.io/acme/orders-aval (default: $AVAL_REGISTRY)
      --registry-timeout duration   deadline for this command's registry calls (default 1m0s)
      --report-file string          report written by the same 'aval run'; push nothing when it reused a verified result, and exit 5 when it records a security event
      --result-file string          result recorded by 'aval run' (default ".aval/result.json")
  -t, --test string                 the test to use, by metadata.name: required on a TestSet of more than one test; output files default to .aval/<test>/

Global Flags:
      --plain[=true|false]   plain aval run output even on a terminal, as in CI (also $AVAL_OUTPUT=plain or TERM=dumb)

Deprecated flags, hidden from help:

  • --result: use --result-file

docs.title: aval record
docs.text:
record is the deprecated form of 'aval stats publish FILE'.

Deprecated, hidden from help: use 'aval stats publish FILE' instead.

Usage:
  aval record [flags]

Examples:
  aval stats publish --registry ghcr.io/acme/orders-aval record.json

Flags:
  -h, --help[=true|false]           help for record
      --record-file string          run record written by 'aval run --stats-file' (required)
      --registry string             OCI repository for attestations and run records, e.g. ghcr.io/acme/orders-aval (default: $AVAL_REGISTRY)
      --registry-timeout duration   deadline for this command's registry calls (default 1m0s)
      --source-repo string          source repository (e.g. acme/orders); default: the one in the record

Global Flags:
      --plain[=true|false]   plain aval run output even on a terminal, as in CI (also $AVAL_OUTPUT=plain or TERM=dumb)

Deprecated flags, hidden from help:

  • --repository: use --source-repo

docs.title: aval run
docs.text:
run reuses a verified result for the current inputs when the trust policy accepts it, restoring the contract's outputs; otherwise it runs runner.command and records the result. Anything Aval cannot prove runs the test.

Without a registry and a trust policy the test always runs. --registry-timeout covers lookup and fetch together; --push has its own. runner.command never sees $SIGSTORE_ID_TOKEN, $AVAL_REGISTRY, $AVAL_POLICY, $AVAL_MIN_TRUST_LEVEL or $AVAL_DOCKER_CONFIG, a directory whose config.json Aval reads registry credentials from instead of $DOCKER_CONFIG's (the test keeps $DOCKER_CONFIG).

runner.command and the probes get $AVAL_RUN_STACK, the contracts of the enclosing aval runs. A run whose contract is already there exits 2 before doing anything: runner.command must not start the same contract again. A nested run of another contract works.

Exit codes: 0 pass, 3 fail, 5 verification failed (a security event, after running the test: also a verified result beside a rejected verification-failed attestation, which is never reused, or more attestations than the lookup cap), 1 error or false hit (--shadow), 2 usage. 5 wins over 3 and 1.

Usage:
  aval run [flags]

Examples:
  # Reuse a trusted result, or run the test
  aval run --registry ghcr.io/acme/orders-aval --policy policy.yaml

  # Run, then sign and publish the result keyless
  aval run --registry ghcr.io/acme/orders-aval --push

Flags:
      --ci-run-url string               link to the CI run, stored in the run record
  -f, --contract string                 path to the test contract (default "aval.yaml")
      --env-file string                 where to record the env section of the fingerprint (hashes, no values) with the result, for 'aval push --env-file' in another job (default ".aval/env.txt")
      --explain[=true|false]            print the fingerprint manifest (what was hashed) before the run; 'aval explain' prints it alone
      --fingerprint-only[=true|false]   print the execution fingerprint and exit (same as 'aval explain --digest')
  -h, --help[=true|false]               help for run
      --key string                      signing key path for --push (default: keyless, from $SIGSTORE_ID_TOKEN or the interactive login; no token is stored and runner.command never sees it)
      --login[=true|false]              sign keyless after the interactive Sigstore login, even without a terminal (overrides: $SIGSTORE_OIDC_ISSUER, $SIGSTORE_OIDC_CLIENT_ID)
      --min-trust-level string          raise the trust policy's minTrustLevel to developer, runner or isolated; a value below it exits 2 (default: $AVAL_MIN_TRUST_LEVEL)
      --no-reuse[=true|false]           always run, never reuse (excludes --shadow)
      --outputs-dir string              also copy the contract's outputs to this empty directory when the result is recorded, for 'aval push --outputs-dir' in another job (keep it outside the scope, e.g. under .aval/)
      --policy string                   trust policy file; without it nothing is reused (default: $AVAL_POLICY; an empty flag also falls back to it)
      --push[=true|false]               sign and publish the result after running (needs --registry)
      --registry string                 OCI repository for attestations and run records, e.g. ghcr.io/acme/orders-aval (default: $AVAL_REGISTRY, then registry in the trust policy)
      --registry-timeout duration       deadline for this command's registry calls (default 1m0s)
      --report-file string              also write the lookup decision as a verify report (JSON) to this file
      --result-file string              where to record the result for 'aval push' (default ".aval/result.json")
      --shadow[=true|false]             verify, but run the test anyway and exit 1 on a false hit (excludes --no-reuse)
      --source-repo string              source repository (e.g. acme/orders), stored in the run record for 'aval stats --by repository'
      --stats[=true|false]              publish a run record for statistics after the run (needs --registry; best-effort)
      --stats-file string               also write the run record to this file, for 'aval stats publish'
  -t, --test string                     the test to use, by metadata.name: required on a TestSet of more than one test; output files default to .aval/<test>/

Global Flags:
      --plain[=true|false]   plain aval run output even on a terminal, as in CI (also $AVAL_OUTPUT=plain or TERM=dumb)

Deprecated flags, hidden from help:

  • --record: use --stats
  • --record-file: use --stats-file
  • --report: use --report-file
  • --repository: use --source-repo
  • --result: use --result-file

docs.title: aval stats
docs.text:
stats reads the run records that 'aval run --stats' and 'aval stats publish' published to the registry and aggregates them: runs, hit rate, misses by cause, verification failures, shadow false hits, and total and saved test time, per test (or per source repository with --by repository) and in total. It reads every test with a stats anchor, or only --test. It writes nothing, locally or to the registry.

Run records are unsigned statistics and never affect reuse. Unreadable or invalid records are skipped and counted. Reading stops after 1000 records or 64 pages per listing; prune old records. Raise --registry-timeout for many records.

--since keeps records made at or after a time: a duration back from now (168h, 30d) or a date (2026-11-01, or RFC 3339).

Exit codes: 0 statistics printed, 1 error (registry), 2 usage.

Usage:
  aval stats [flags]
  aval stats [command]

Examples:
  aval stats --registry ghcr.io/acme/orders-aval --since 30d

Available Commands:
  publish     Publish a run record written by 'aval run --stats-file'

Flags:
      --by string                   group by test or repository (the run record's source repository) (default "test")
  -h, --help[=true|false]           help for stats
  -o, --output string               output format: text or json (default "text")
      --registry string             OCI repository for attestations and run records, e.g. ghcr.io/acme/orders-aval (default: $AVAL_REGISTRY)
      --registry-timeout duration   deadline for this command's registry calls (default 1m0s)
      --since string                only records made since: a duration (168h, 30d) or a date (2026-11-01, RFC 3339)
      --test string                 only this test id (metadata.name); default: every test with run records

Global Flags:
      --plain[=true|false]   plain aval run output even on a terminal, as in CI (also $AVAL_OUTPUT=plain or TERM=dumb)

Use "aval stats [command] --help" for more information about a command.

docs.title: aval stats publish
docs.text:
stats publish publishes the run record that 'aval run --stats-file' wrote to FILE, as 'aval run --stats' would have. Use it to publish, from a job with write credentials that runs no tests, the record of a run made without them. Run records are unsigned statistics: run and verify never read them. --source-repo sets the record's source repository.

Usage:
  aval stats publish FILE [flags]

Examples:
  aval stats publish --registry ghcr.io/acme/orders-aval record.json

Flags:
  -h, --help[=true|false]           help for publish
      --registry string             OCI repository for attestations and run records, e.g. ghcr.io/acme/orders-aval (default: $AVAL_REGISTRY)
      --registry-timeout duration   deadline for this command's registry calls (default 1m0s)
      --source-repo string          source repository (e.g. acme/orders); default: the one in the record

Global Flags:
      --plain[=true|false]   plain aval run output even on a terminal, as in CI (also $AVAL_OUTPUT=plain or TERM=dumb)

docs.title: aval upgrade
docs.text:
upgrade downloads a release from GitHub Releases (the latest, or --version), checks that checksums.txt carries a keyless Sigstore signature from Aval's release workflow at that tag and that the archive matches it, then replaces the running binary. Any failed check replaces nothing. A bad signature or checksum is a security event: do not retry it away. Without --version it refuses to move to an older release than the running one.

Exit codes: 0 upgraded or up to date (or --check printed), 1 error (download, signature, checksum, older latest release, replacing the binary), 2 usage.

Usage:
  aval upgrade [flags]

Examples:
  aval upgrade --check

Flags:
      --check[=true|false]   print the current and target versions without installing
  -h, --help[=true|false]    help for upgrade
      --version string       release to install, e.g. v0.4.0 (default: latest)

Global Flags:
      --plain[=true|false]   plain aval run output even on a terminal, as in CI (also $AVAL_OUTPUT=plain or TERM=dumb)

docs.title: aval verify
docs.text:
verify computes the fingerprint, looks up the attestation and verifies its signature and the trust policy, without running anything. It needs a registry; without a trust policy every lookup is a miss.

Exit codes: 0 verified, 4 miss, 5 verification failed (security event: also a verified result beside a rejected verification-failed attestation, or more attestations than the lookup cap), 1 error (registry, policy or fingerprint), 2 usage or invalid aval.yaml.

Usage:
  aval verify [flags]

Examples:
  aval verify --registry ghcr.io/acme/orders-aval --policy policy.yaml -o json

Flags:
  -f, --contract string             path to the test contract (default "aval.yaml")
  -h, --help[=true|false]           help for verify
      --min-trust-level string      raise the trust policy's minTrustLevel to developer, runner or isolated; a value below it exits 2 (default: $AVAL_MIN_TRUST_LEVEL)
  -o, --output string               output format: text or json (default "text")
      --policy string               trust policy file; without it nothing is reused (default: $AVAL_POLICY; an empty flag also falls back to it)
      --registry string             OCI repository for attestations and run records, e.g. ghcr.io/acme/orders-aval (default: $AVAL_REGISTRY, then registry in the trust policy)
      --registry-timeout duration   deadline for this command's registry calls (default 1m0s)
  -t, --test string                 the test to use, by metadata.name: required on a TestSet of more than one test; output files default to .aval/<test>/

Global Flags:
      --plain[=true|false]   plain aval run output even on a terminal, as in CI (also $AVAL_OUTPUT=plain or TERM=dumb)

docs.title: aval version
docs.text:
Print the aval version, Go version and platform

Usage:
  aval version [flags]

Examples:
  aval version

Flags:
  -h, --help[=true|false]   help for version

Global Flags:
      --plain[=true|false]   plain aval run output even on a terminal, as in CI (also $AVAL_OUTPUT=plain or TERM=dumb)

docs.title: The test contract: aval.yaml
docs.text: aval.yaml says what a test is, how to run it and which files it reads. Aval reuses a result only when those declared inputs are identical. An input you do not declare is invisible to Aval. Format: aval.trianalab.io/v1, frozen (Versioning).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
apiVersion: aval.trianalab.io/v1   # required, exact value
kind: Test                      # required, exact value

metadata:
  name: orders-integration      # test identity: WHAT is checked

runner:
  # argv, executed without a shell. Order matters and is part of the fingerprint.
  command: ["go", "test", "-tags=integration", "./orders/..."]

scope:
  source:                       # required, each glob must match >= 1 file
    - "orders/**/*.go"
    - "internal/**/*.go"
    - "testdata/orders/**"
  exclude:                      # optional, removes files selected by source
    - "**/*_bench_test.go"
  dependencies:                 # optional, each glob must match >= 1 file
    - "go.mod"
    - "go.sum"
  allowMutable:                 # optional, accepts a mutable reference on purpose
    - ref: "postgres:16"
      reason: "rebuilt and scanned nightly"

environment:
  toolchain:                    # optional, declared
    go: "1.25"
  probe:                        # optional, checks a toolchain entry before the run
    go: [go, version]
  env:                          # optional, names or PREFIX_* patterns; values are hashed
    - CGO_ENABLED
    - GOFLAGS

cacheability: hermetic          # required, see "Cacheability classes"

Check it locally:

aval explain -f path/to/aval.yaml --digest   # prints sha256:<hex>
aval explain -f path/to/aval.yaml            # the manifest, then the fingerprint

It excludes only the default .aval/result.json; a run that writes --result-file, --report-file or --stats-file inside the scope fingerprints the same only when those paths are under .aval/.

Diff the aval explain output of two machines to see which file, toolchain entry or variable differs. -f takes one path and defaults to ./aval.yaml; the root is the contract file's directory, or the directory scope.root names above it (Contracts in a subdirectory). A kind: Test file holds one test; a kind: TestSet file holds many (Many tests in one file).

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
• Unknown fields and files with more than one YAML document are rejected (exit 2), so a typo like sorce: fails instead of shrinking the scope.
  • Every field is part of the fingerprint.
Field Type Required Rules apiVersion string yes Must be aval.trianalab.io/v1. kind string yes Test, or TestSet for many tests in one file. metadata.name string yes 1-64 chars of [a-z0-9._-], starting and ending with [a-z0-9]. runner.command list of strings yes Non-empty argv, first element not blank. No shell. It must not start aval run on the same contract again, directly or through other contracts: see Nested runs. scope.source list of globs yes At least one glob. Each glob must match a file, and at least one file must remain after exclude. scope.optionalSource list of globs no Hashed like source, but a glob may match nothing yet. A glob may not also be in source. See Optional source globs. scope.exclude list of globs no Removes files from the source and optionalSource set (not from dependencies). May match nothing. scope.dependencies list of globs no Lockfiles and manifests. Each glob must match a file. scope.allowMutable list of {file, files, ref, reason} no Accepts a mutable reference on purpose: ref exactly as Aval reports it, plus a non-blank reason. An optional file (an exact path relative to the contract root, or runner.command) limits it to that file; without file or files, a ref that several files report is not accepted. An optional files, a list of globs relative to the contract root that excludes file, accepts the ref in every file in scope that a glob matches, never in runner.command; each glob must match a file in scope, otherwise the contract is invalid (exit 2). See Pin your dependencies. scope.resolve list of kind: reference no One kind: reference per entry. Kind is one of image, npm, pypi, go, maven, crate, gem, git, url. The reference must not contain credentials. See Resolve references. scope.contracts list of paths no Other contracts this test depends on (Depend on another part of the repo). Each path is relative to this contract's directory: clean (.. only at the start), slash-separated, no spaces, ending in .yaml or .yml, listed once. At fingerprint time the file must be a valid contract inside the git working tree of this contract (the nearest directory at or above it with a .git entry), with no symlink on the path; if this contract's own directory is a symlink, .. is resolved from its real location. No cycles, at most 8 levels and 64 distinct contracts. A referenced contract's mutable references block reuse here too, unless its own scope.allowMutable accepts them. scope.root string no The path from this contract's directory up to the root of its tree: .. segments only (.., ../..). Globs, outputs, allowMutable[].file and files, runner.command and environment.probe resolve from it; scope.contracts does not. The root must lie inside the git working tree of this contract, as for scope.contracts; otherwise aval run, explain, verify and push exit 2. See Contracts in a subdirectory. environment.toolchain map string to string no Keys match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$. Values are not validated. environment.probe map string to list of strings no Each key must be an environment.toolchain key with a non-empty value; each value a non-empty argv, first element not blank. See Probe the toolchain. environment.env list of strings no Variable names matching ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$, or prefix patterns: a name followed by * (APP_*), see Environment variable patterns. AVAL_RUN_STACK is rejected in any case (set by aval run, not an input), and so is a pattern that would match it (AVAL_*, AVAL_RUN_*). environment.paths list of strings no Files or directories outside the tree, each ~/<path>, $NAME/<path> or ${NAME}/<path> with a clean relative path: no globs, no . or .. segments, no other variables, no spaces, no duplicates. See Files outside the tree. cacheability string yes One of hermetic, controlled-environment, external-dependencies, non-deterministic. outputs list of globs no Files the test writes that a reused result restores, such as coverage.xml (Restore coverage and reports on reuse). Same glob rules as scope. When publishing, each glob must match a regular file (no symlink) that is not the contract file, outside the scope, .git and .aval; at most 256 files, 16 MiB each, 64 MiB in total. Otherwise nothing is published (exit 1). To push from another job, aval run --outputs-dir copies them and aval push --outputs-dir publishes them from that copy (the artifact). Omitted from the fingerprint when empty, so existing contracts keep theirs; adding it changes the fingerprint, so a result without outputs is never reused for it.

docs.title: Contracts in a subdirectory
docs.text:
A contract can live below the root of the tree it covers, such as aval/unit.yaml in a monorepo. scope.root says how far up the root is:

# aval/unit.yaml
scope:
  root: ..
  source: ["src/**"]
  dependencies: ["go.mod"]

The contract then behaves as if its file sat in the root:

  • Globs, outputs, allowMutable[].file and files, manifest paths, finding paths and restored output paths are relative to the root. The manifest lists the same source and dependency lines as aval.unit.yaml at the root; only the contract line differs.
  • runner.command and environment.probe run in the root.
  • --result-file, --report-file and --stats-file are skipped only when they are Aval outputs under the root.
  • scope.contracts paths stay relative to the contract file's directory. A referenced contract with its own scope.root uses its own root.

aval explain prints the resolved root after its header. That line is an absolute path that differs between checkouts; it is not part of the fingerprint. The root must lie inside the git working tree that holds the contract (the nearest directory at or above it with a .git entry). If the contract's directory is a symlink, .. is resolved from its real location. A root above the working tree, or no working tree at all, exits 2 (aval run, explain, verify and push). Globs still cannot contain ...

docs.title: Many tests in one file: TestSet
docs.text:
A kind: TestSet declares every test of a project in one file, without repeating shared scope and environment:

apiVersion: aval.trianalab.io/v1
kind: TestSet
defaults:
  scope:
    source: ["VERSION"]
    exclude: ["**/testdata/**"]
    dependencies: ["go.sum"]
  environment:
    toolchain: {go: "1.25"}
    env: [CI]
  cacheability: hermetic
fragments:
  db:
    scope: {source: ["db/**"]}
    environment:
      toolchain: {postgres: "16"}
      env: [DB_URL]
  web:
    scope: {source: ["web/**", "VERSION"]}
tests:
  - metadata: {name: unit}
    runner: {command: [go, test, ./src/...]}
    scope: {source: ["src/**"]}
  - metadata: {name: integration}
    use: [web, db]
    runner: {command: [go, test, -tags=integration, ./...]}
    cacheability: controlled-environment
  - metadata: {name: "shard-{index}"}
    use: [db]
    runner: {command: [go, test, "-shard={index}/2", ./...]}
    matrix: {index: ["1", "2"]}

Top-level keys besides apiVersion and kind:

Key Holds May set defaults what every test inherits scope.*, environment.*, cacheability fragments named blocks a test pulls in with use scope.* except exclude, environment.* tests a list of tests, at least one the body of a kind: Test (metadata, runner, scope, environment, outputs, cacheability), plus use and matrix

Each test expands to a standalone kind: Test and is fingerprinted exactly as that file would be: the set above fingerprints shard-1 like a kind: Test named shard-1 with the merged scope. Paths, globs and scope.root resolve from the TestSet file's directory.

Merge rules, in the order defaults, each used fragment, then the test:

  • Lists (source, optionalSource, exclude, dependencies, allowMutable, resolve, contracts, env) are merged as a set union. Nothing inherited can be removed, so a merge can only widen a test's inputs. exclude is the one way to narrow them, and it is only allowed in defaults or in the test itself, where it is visible.
  • A key of environment.toolchain or environment.probe, or scope.root, set twice with different values is an error that names both sources.
  • metadata, runner and outputs belong to a test only. The test's cacheability overrides the one in defaults.
  • The order of use does not change the result. A fragment cannot use another fragment.

aval gen <language> writes one fragment and one test per unit from the repository's dependency graph into a TestSet, and leaves hand-written entries alone (Generate scope).

matrix maps variables to lists of strings and creates one test per combination. It substitutes {var} into metadata.name, runner.command and the values of environment.toolchain (inherited ones too), in one pass, so a value that holds {x} is not substituted again. Each value is part of the fingerprinted argv or toolchain lines. In a test with a matrix, every {name} in those fields must be a matrix variable: write a shell variable as $VAR, not ${VAR}. In a TestSet test without a matrix, a {name} in a toolchain value is an error. A standalone kind: Test is not checked: it is also what aval explain --expand prints for a matrix leg, whose substituted value may hold {x}. Probe argv, env, scope and outputs are not substituted. A set expands to at most 1024 tests.

A variable can also be {count: N}, with N an integer from 1 to 1024: it takes the values "1" to "N", and {v_count} (here {shard_count}) is N in every test. {v_count} is substituted like any variable but adds no combinations. Shards then state the total once:

tests:
  - metadata: {name: "browser-{shard}"}
    runner: {command: [make, test-browser, "PW_SHARD={shard}/{shard_count}"]}
    matrix: {shard: {count: 3}}

This expands to browser-1 to browser-3 with PW_SHARD=1/3 to 3/3, the same tests and fingerprints as shard: ["1", "2", "3"] with PW_SHARD={shard}/3. Changing N changes the argv, so the fingerprint, of every test that uses {shard_count}. Only count variables have a {v_count}.

One test per platform, each with its own fingerprint, so a result recorded on darwin is never reused on linux:

tests:
  - metadata: {name: "unit-{os}"}
    runner: {command: [go, test, ./...]}
    matrix: {os: [linux, darwin]}
    environment:
      toolchain: {platform: "{os}"}
      probe: {platform: [go, env, GOOS]}

aval run --test unit-darwin records a result only where the probe prints darwin. To reuse a result across platforms, do not declare platform.

Each of these exits 2 and names the problem: an unknown fragment, a fragment no test uses, a fragment with use, exclude, runner, metadata, outputs, matrix or cacheability, a conflicting key, an unknown {var}, a {var} in a toolchain value of a test without a matrix, a count that is missing or not an integer from 1 to 1024, a key other than count in the mapping form, a variable v_count beside a count variable v, two tests with the same expanded name, and a scope.contracts entry that points at a TestSet (share scope with fragments instead).

docs.title: Select a test
docs.text:
aval run, explain, verify and push take -t/--test <name>, the expanded metadata.name of one test:

aval run --test shard-1
aval push --test shard-1
  • On a TestSet of more than one test, a missing --test exits 2 and lists the names. Nothing runs every test of a set at once.
  • On a kind: Test file, or a TestSet of one test, --test is optional; a name that matches no test exits 2.
  • With --test, the output files default to .aval/<name>/result.json, report.json, record.json and env.txt (--result-file, --report-file, --stats-file, --env-file), so tests never overwrite each other's outputs and aval push --test <name> finds the result and report of the run. aval run --test <name> removes a stale .aval/<name>/ before it runs. A flag you pass wins. Without --test the defaults are unchanged.

aval explain --test <name> --expand prints the test as the standalone kind: Test it expands to. aval explain --all checks every test of the file without running anything (no probe, no command): it prints one name fingerprint line per test, reports every failing test by name instead of stopping at the first, and exits 2 if any is invalid, else 1 if any fingerprint cannot be computed. -o json prints the same as {"tests": [{"name", "fingerprint"} or {"name", "error"}]}. A file that does not expand prints every problem on stderr and nothing on stdout.

aval init --set writes a TestSet of one test and one fragment, plus .github/aval/policy.yaml with a placeholder identity, as a starting point (Write a contract).

docs.title: Nested runs
docs.text:
aval run sets AVAL_RUN_STACK for runner.command and the probes: the absolute, symlink-resolved paths of the contracts of the enclosing runs plus its own, joined by the OS path list separator (: or ;). A run whose contract is already in the stack exits 2 before it probes, looks up or runs anything:

aval: aval.yaml is already running in an outer aval run (/repo/aval.yaml): runner.command must not start the same contract again

The outer run then records a failed test (exit 3). This catches a make target that calls aval run and a contract whose runner.command calls that target, and a cycle through several contracts. A runner.command that runs aval run on a different contract works. AVAL_RUN_STACK is not an input: it is never hashed nor recorded, and environment.env cannot list it.

docs.title: Globs
docs.text:
scope.source, scope.optionalSource, scope.exclude, scope.dependencies and outputs use the same globs:

Glob Matches src/**/*.go src/a.go and src/x/y/a.go *.go top-level files only: * does not cross / dir/** every file under dir; globs never match directories ** every file Rejected /a, ./a, ../a, a//b, a\b, foo**, **.go, [a-
  • Relative to the contract root (scope.root, by default the contract's directory); a glob cannot escape it.
  • Case-sensitive and byte-exact: Makefile is not makefile, NFC is not NFD.
  • Order does not matter.
  • Symlinks are never followed nor hashed. A symlink under which a source or dependencies glob could match files is an error, unless exclude covers its name and no dependencies glob reaches it. A symlink to a regular file needs only its name excluded: tests/fx/link.yaml skips a link to real.yaml. Any other symlink (to a directory, dangling, or a loop) needs its contents excluded too: **/node_modules/** skips pkg/web/node_modules/.bin/tool, and ["pkg/bin", "pkg/bin/**"] skips a symlinked pkg/bin. pkg/bin or pkg/bin/** alone does not. If a name-excluded link later points to a directory, fingerprinting fails.

docs.title: Optional source globs
docs.text:
Every source glob must match a file, which catches typos. A test that finds its inputs by pattern (it walks the tree for every *testdata*.yaml) reads files that may not exist yet. Leaving the pattern out of the scope means the first such file is not hashed, and a stale result is reused. Declare it in optionalSource:

scope:
  source: ["src/**"]
  optionalSource: ["**/*testdata*.yaml"]
  • Files it matches are hashed as source lines, with the same exclude, symlink and path rules. Adding the first matching file is a miss; removing the last one returns to the earlier fingerprint.
  • The only difference is that a glob may match nothing. At least one file from source and optionalSource together must still remain after exclude.
  • aval explain names each optional glob that matched nothing on stderr (optional: scope.optionalSource glob "<glob>" matched no files yet), so check it after writing one.
  • Use it only for patterns the test discovers, not to silence a source glob that matches nothing: that is usually a typo.

docs.title: Test identity vs execution fingerprint
docs.text: metadata.name says what is checked. The fingerprint says with which inputs. Renaming a test changes its fingerprint.

docs.title: Cacheability classes
docs.text:
Class Use it when Reused hermetic the test reads only the declared files yes controlled-environment it uses services you pin, such as a Compose image by digest yes external-dependencies it calls something you do not control only if the policy allows it non-deterministic the same inputs can give a different result never

A reusable class still needs a signed result your policy trusts. A non-deterministic test is never looked up. A hermetic or controlled-environment test with a mutable reference that allowMutable does not accept is a miss, and its result is not published (Pin your dependencies).

docs.title: What goes into the fingerprint
docs.text:
The fingerprint is sha256:<hex> of a line-oriented manifest (format aval-fingerprint/v2). aval explain prints the exact text that was hashed, in this order:

aval-fingerprint/v2
contract <sha256 of canonical contract JSON>
source <sha256> <mode> <path>
dependency <sha256> <mode> <path>
toolchain <key>=<value>
env <NAME> <sha256 of value | unset>
path <entry> <mode> <sha256> | <sha256> | absent | unset
resolve <kind> <reference> <version> <immutable id>
contract <path> <name> <fingerprint>
Line Holds Not affected by header aval-fingerprint/v2, bumped when an existing contract's manifest would change contract sha256 of the parsed contract as JSON comments, formatting, key order, the order and duplicates of set-like lists (argv order counts; an empty list equals an omitted one) source, dependency sha256 of the content, x (any exec bit) or -, path. A file in both sets appears twice owner, timestamps, other permission bits toolchain key=value as written; checked against the installed tools only by environment.probe env sha256 of the value, or unset (empty is not unset); values never appear in clear, but the hash of a short or guessable value (a low-entropy secret) can be found by trying values, so declare secrets only if aval explain output and the env file may be seen. A prefix pattern gives one line per set variable it matches and none when nothing matches path one line per environment.paths entry, as declared (not expanded): <mode> <sha256> for a file, for a directory the sha256 of its sorted <sha256> <mode> <relpath> lines, absent if nothing is there, unset if its variable is unset; only with environment.paths. The hash of a short or guessable file (a low-entropy secret) can be found by trying values, as for env where ~ or the variable points, as long as the content is the same resolve kind, reference, version or floating, immutable id; only with scope.resolve, and needs the network (Resolve references) the registry address contract <path> one line per scope.contracts entry: the path as written, the referenced contract's metadata.name and its fingerprint, computed from its own directory and inputs (so references are transitive). aval explain also prints the tree, one depends on <path> (<name>) <fingerprint> line per reference

Lines are sorted within each section, so checkout path and walk order do not matter. Paths are hashed byte for byte. Windows has no exec bit, so an executable file fingerprints differently there than on Unix.

docs.title: Environment variable patterns
docs.text:
A tool configured by prefix (viper SetEnvPrefix with AutomaticEnv, Go envconfig, pydantic-settings env_prefix, Spring relaxed binding) reads any PREFIX_<KEY>. List the prefix instead of every name:

environment:
  env: ["APP_*", GOFLAGS]

* may only end the entry, after at least one name character: *, *_TOKEN, APP*X and APP_? are rejected. The pattern hashes every variable set when the fingerprint is computed whose name starts with the prefix, one env NAME <sha256> line each, so setting, unsetting or changing one changes the fingerprint. A pattern that matches nothing adds no line; the pattern itself is in the contract line. An exact name a pattern also matches yields one line.

Names compare as the platform does: case-sensitively on Linux and macOS (APP_* matches neither APPX nor app_a), case-insensitively on Windows, where a matched name is written upper-cased in the manifest.

A pattern also hashes credentials that share the prefix, such as APP_REGISTRY_TOKEN, as it would a listed name. Their sha256 digests are in the manifest that aval explain and --explain print (CI logs), and the published fingerprint is a hash over that manifest, so anyone who knows the other inputs can test guesses of a short or guessable secret against it. When the prefix covers secrets, list the exact names instead.

docs.title: What does not go in
docs.text: Not hashed Note files no source, optionalSource or dependencies glob matches the main risk: keep the scope honest .git (directory, file or symlink) exact name, at any depth; covers linked worktrees and submodules. An exact glob such as pkg/.git matches no file and fails .aval/ directories and the command's --result-file/--report-file files so ["**"] stays stable; keep them under .aval/. A path in scope that holds a real input exits 2. In a scope.contracts reference they stay inputs (a miss, never a false hit) commit, branch, VCS metadata two commits with the same scope share a result environment variables not in environment.env the real toolchain, OS and architecture unless declared; probe output is never hashed

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text:
Declared scope means some changes are invisible by design. A test that depends on one of these can reuse a result it should not:

  • a file the test reads that scope does not match, including a case or Unicode mismatch under a wildcard glob
  • an environment variable the test reads that environment.env does not list
  • a file outside the tree the test reads (~/.config/<app>, ~/.npmrc) that environment.paths does not list
  • content behind a name the scanner does not recognize, or a network service: use scope.resolve or external-dependencies
  • the installed toolchain, OS and architecture, unless environment.probe checks the toolchain entry
  • git state the test reads (log, worktree or submodule layout), the same as commit and branch

Mitigation: review the contract, use aval run --shadow, pick the right cacheability class.

docs.title: Fail-closed errors
docs.text:
