Aval cannot prove the inputs: aval run reports outcome error, runs the test and records nothing; aval explain, aval verify and aval push exit 1 (as do run --fingerprint-only and run --explain, which aval explain --digest and aval explain replace).

Message Fix source glob "<glob>" matched no files fix the glob; a case or Unicode mismatch also matches nothing scope.source matched no files exclude removed every source and optionalSource file, or optionalSource matched nothing and exclude removed every source file source "<path>" is excluded only by a trailing "**" exclude it by name, or narrow the glob dependency glob "<glob>" matched no files fix the glob only regular files are supported in scope remove the symlink, device or socket from scope environment.paths <entry>: <reason> the entry or a file under it is a symlink, a special file or unreadable, or ~ or its variable is not an absolute path (Files outside the tree) "<path>" is a symlink a glob could match files under symlinks are not followed: remove it, or exclude it with no dependencies glob reaching it (Globs). The message names the fix: its name alone for a link to a regular file, its name and contents (pkg/bin plus pkg/bin/**, or **/node_modules/**) for anything else. The contract directory itself may be a symlink control characters in path are not supported rename the file (newline or carriage return) resolve <kind> <reference>: <reason> see When resolution fails scope.contracts <path>: <reason> any error above in the referenced contract, or: missing or invalid contract, leads outside the repository root (also its scope.root), no git working tree (.git) at or above <dir>, <path> is a symlink, <path> is not a regular file, cycle: a/aval.yaml -> b/aval.yaml -> a/aval.yaml, more than 8 levels or 64 contracts any I/O error while walking or reading make the file or directory readable; the walk only enters directories a glob can match

docs.title: Files outside the tree
docs.text:
A program that reads per-user state (~/.config/<app>, ~/.npmrc, ~/.docker/config.json) has an input that scope globs cannot reach. environment.paths declares it:

environment:
  env: [XDG_CONFIG_HOME]
  paths: ["~/.config/pacto", "${XDG_CONFIG_HOME}/pacto"]
  • ~ is the home directory, $NAME and ${NAME} the variable's value; both must be absolute paths. Aval knows no application layout: if a program falls back from $XDG_CONFIG_HOME to ~/.config, declare both.
  • The manifest holds the entry as written, so machines with a different $HOME and the same content share a result.
  • absent means "require absent": a result recorded without the file is reused only where the file is still missing. An empty file or directory is not absent.
  • A symlink at or under the entry, a device, socket or FIFO, an unreadable file or directory, or any stat error other than "does not exist" fails the fingerprint (environment.paths <entry>: <reason>, exit 1); none of them is read as absent. An entry that leads inside the contract's scope root is a contract error (exit 2): declare those files with a scope glob.
  • A whole directory is hashed, so keep caches out of it, or turn them off with a variable in environment.env.
  • aval push --env-file carries only the env lines: path lines are hashed again on the machine that pushes.

docs.title: Probe the toolchain
docs.text:
environment.toolchain is a claim. environment.probe checks it: before the lookup, aval run runs each probe in the contract root, without a shell, with a 10 s timeout and without $SIGSTORE_ID_TOKEN. The declared value must appear in the output (stdout and stderr) as a version token: not preceded by a digit or a dot, not followed by a digit. 3.13 matches Python 3.13.1; it does not match Python 3.130, and 3.1 does not match Python 3.13.

environment:
  toolchain:
    python: "3.13"
  probe:
    python: [python3, --version]

On a mismatch, a probe that cannot start, a non-zero exit, a timeout or output over 4 KiB (it is signed into the predicate), aval run looks nothing up (outcome error; the reason names the probe, the declared and the observed value), runs the test, records and publishes nothing, warns aval: warning: result not recorded: <reason>, and exits with the test's code (0 passed, 3 failed). With --push it exits 1 instead (result not published: <reason>), or 3 if the test failed. On a match, the output goes into the predicate's execution.environment as probe.<key>.

Only aval run executes probes. aval verify, aval push, aval explain and the browser demo never do: a consumer never executes commands from a contract. aval explain prints the manifest and never runs a probe. The probe argv is part of the contract, so adding or changing one changes the fingerprint; its output is not hashed, since it varies by build and platform.

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text:
aval.trianalab.io/v1 is frozen; policy files use the same value. Within v1 the schema only gets new optional fields. An older aval rejects a field it does not know, which fails closed: a policy with the optional registry field (#209) fails to load in an older aval, so nothing is reused. The same holds for a kind it does not know: an older aval rejects a kind: TestSet file with exit 2.

aval.dev/v1alpha1 is rejected: change that line. Rules: artifact format.

docs.title: Future work
docs.text: • Observed inputs: trace which files the test actually reads, to flag undeclared inputs or suggest scope. v0 never infers scope. Until then, find undeclared inputs by hand.

docs.title: Install
docs.text: How do I get aval? One static binary for Linux, macOS and Windows (amd64, arm64) from GitHub Releases, checked before it is installed.

docs.title: Linux and macOS
docs.text:
curl -fsSL https://aval.run/install.sh | bash

Installs into /usr/local/bin (sudo only if needed). Needs curl or wget, and sha256sum or shasum.

Variable Flag Windows Effect DESIRED_VERSION=v0.2.0 --version v0.2.0 yes install this release, not the latest AVAL_INSTALL_DIR=<dir> yes install here USE_SUDO=false --no-sudo no never use sudo AVAL_NO_VERIFY=1 --no-verify yes skip the cosign and gh checks (sha256 still runs) AVAL_DOWNLOAD_URL=<url> yes download from a mirror; the signer stays pinned AVAL_SHA256=<hex> --sha256 <hex> yes the archive must have this sha256; <os>_<arch>=<hex> pins one platform (repeat the flag, or separate with spaces) AVAL_REQUIRE_VERIFY=1 --require-verify yes fail if cosign is missing; needs a version, excludes --no-verify AVAL_REQUIRE_PROVENANCE=1 --require-provenance yes fail if gh 2.49 or later is missing; needs a version, excludes --no-verify

Piped, pass flags after bash -s --:

curl -fsSL https://aval.run/install.sh | bash -s -- --version v0.2.0

docs.title: Windows
docs.text:
In PowerShell 5.1 or 7:

irm https://aval.run/install.ps1 | iex

Installs into %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\aval and adds it to your user PATH, no admin rights. Settings: the variables marked Windows above.

docs.title: What the installers check
docs.text:
Check Runs the archive's sha256 matches checksums.txt always the archive's sha256 is the pinned one with --sha256 checksums.txt has a Sigstore signature from Aval's release workflow at that tag if cosign is on PATH; required with --require-verify the archive matches the release's SLSA provenance if gh 2.49 or later is on PATH (no login); required with --require-provenance

A failed check installs nothing. A check that cannot run is reported, or is an error with --require-verify / --require-provenance.

docs.title: In CI
docs.text:
Install one exact release and nothing you cannot verify. Vendor the installer at a release tag, so a change on main cannot alter your pipeline, then pin the version and the archive's sha256 (from that release's checksums.txt):

curl -fsSLo .ci/get-aval.sh https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TrianaLab/aval/v0.8.2/scripts/get-aval.sh

# cosign (and gh for --require-provenance) must be on PATH.
bash .ci/get-aval.sh --version v0.8.2 \
  --sha256 linux_amd64=<sha256 of aval_0.8.2_linux_amd64.tar.gz> \
  --sha256 darwin_arm64=<sha256 of aval_0.8.2_darwin_arm64.tar.gz> \
  --require-verify --require-provenance

The entry for the runner's platform is required. A re-tagged release, a mirror serving another build, or a missing cosign fails the install. --sha256, --require-verify and --require-provenance first ship in v0.8.1 (the v0.8.0 tag has no release). Aval's GitHub actions (integrations/github/run and publish) install their pinned release the same way.

docs.title: Upgrade
docs.text:
aval upgrade                    # to the latest release
aval upgrade --version v0.4.0   # to a given release
aval upgrade --check            # print the current and target versions, change nothing
  • It checks the Sigstore signature of checksums.txt itself (issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com, signer: Aval's release workflow at that tag), then the sha256. No cosign needed.
  • A failed check replaces nothing and exits 1. A bad signature is a security event: do not retry it away.
  • Without --version it never downgrades; a dev build is always replaced.
  • Directory not writable? Use sudo or the installer.

aval version prints the version, Go version and platform.

docs.title: By hand
docs.text:
Download, check, then put aval on your PATH:

VERSION=0.2.0
OS=linux        # or darwin
ARCH=amd64      # or arm64
BASE=https://github.com/TrianaLab/aval/releases/download/v$VERSION
curl -fsSLO "$BASE/aval_${VERSION}_${OS}_${ARCH}.tar.gz"
curl -fsSLO "$BASE/checksums.txt"
curl -fsSLO "$BASE/checksums.txt.sigstore.json"
curl -fsSLO "$BASE/provenance.sigstore.json"
cosign verify-blob checksums.txt --bundle checksums.txt.sigstore.json \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com \
  --certificate-identity "https://github.com/TrianaLab/aval/.github/workflows/release.yaml@refs/tags/v$VERSION"
sha256sum --ignore-missing -c checksums.txt   # macOS: shasum -a 256 --ignore-missing -c checksums.txt
gh attestation verify "aval_${VERSION}_${OS}_${ARCH}.tar.gz" --bundle provenance.sigstore.json --repo TrianaLab/aval
tar -xzf "aval_${VERSION}_${OS}_${ARCH}.tar.gz" aval
sudo mv aval /usr/local/bin/

docs.title: From source
docs.text: go install github.com/TrianaLab/aval/cmd/aval@latest. The binary reports version dev and has no release checks.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text: Delete /usr/local/bin/aval (or your AVAL_INSTALL_DIR), or %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\aval on Windows and remove it from your user PATH.

docs.title: Consume evidence
docs.text: Three surfaces are stable: the OCI artifact, the Go package pkg/evidence, and aval verify -o json. Nothing else (internal packages, CLI text output, the manifest layout) is a contract. The formats are frozen (compatibility rules).

docs.title: 1. OCI artifact and predicate
docs.text: A result is an in-toto v1 Statement in a DSSE envelope, found through the tag sha256-<fingerprint hex> and the OCI 1.1 referrers of the manifest it points at, and consumed by digest. Predicate type https://aval.trianalab.io/attestation/execution/v2; fields and layout: artifact format.

docs.title: 2. Go package github.com/TrianaLab/aval/pkg/evidence
docs.text:
pkg/evidence has no dependency on the rest of the module and is the only public Go API:

Symbol Purpose Parse(data []byte) (*Predicate, error) decode predicate JSON and run Validate; no signature check (*Predicate).Validate() error structural checks: schemaVersion == "v2", subject, test.id, result, fingerprint format, runner.identity, timestamps Verify(ctx, *Envelope, VerifyOptions) (*Verification, error) check the signature, match the signer against the policy, enforce the minimum level, decode the statement, require the expected fingerprint, test id and a reusable cacheability; every failure is a *VerificationError SignatureVerifier, Signer checks a signature cryptographically and returns the signer it binds, with no policy. pkg/evidence ships no implementation, to stay free of Sigstore; a public Sigstore one is planned for milestone 5 MatchIdentity(ids, issuer, subject) (Identity, bool) the keyless identity that grants a signer the highest level; SubjectRegexp matches the whole subject; sets TrustLevelName from the entry's level MatchSigner(ids, Signer) (Identity, bool) MatchIdentity for keyless signers, PublicKey entries for key signers; sets TrustLevelName from the entry's level PublicKeyID(pem) (string, error) base64(sha256(DER)) of a PEM public key, the key hint in key-based bundles VerifyOptions expected fingerprint and test id, accepted Identities, MinTrustLevel, AllowedCacheability, Signature (required) ErrNotFound no attestation for the fingerprint: a miss, run the test ErrVerification an attestation failed signature or policy checks: a security event Report, ReportVersion the document aval verify --output json prints RunRecord, RunRecordVersion, ParseRunRecord a run record (run records); unsigned statistics, never a basis for trust StatsReport, TestStats, RepositoryStats, RunStats, MissCauses, StatsReportVersion, StatsUnknownRepository the document aval stats --output json prints (stats report)

ExpectedFingerprint and ExpectedTestID come from your local contract, never from the attestation; both are required and must equal the predicate's execution.fingerprint and test.id. Levels are numbers in reports: 0 unknown, 1 developer, 2 runner, 3 isolated (trust model).

A complete consumer that imports only pkg/evidence: Consume from Go. ErrNotFound comes from your lookup step, not from Verify.

docs.title: Go API compatibility
docs.text:
pkg/evidence follows semantic versioning as part of the module github.com/TrianaLab/aval. Within a major version its exported API changes additively only: new identifiers, new struct fields that keep a comparable struct comparable, new methods on concrete types. Anything else (removing or renaming, changing a type or signature, adding a method to an exported interface) needs a new module path, github.com/TrianaLab/aval/v2. The exported surface is snapshotted in pkg/evidence/testdata/api-v1.txt and checked in CI.

The Go API and the wire formats are versioned separately: a breaking format change gets a new identifier, and supporting it is an additive Go change.

docs.title: 3. aval verify --output json
docs.text:
aval verify computes the fingerprint, looks up the attestation, verifies it against the trust policy and runs nothing. With -o json it prints the verify report on stdout; stderr adds one aval: SECURITY: ... line when an attestation failed verification. Exit 2 prints no report, and neither does exit 1 when fingerprinting failed (exit codes).

CI snippet that keeps miss and verification failure apart:

set +e
report=$(aval verify --registry ghcr.io/acme/orders-aval --policy aval-policy.yaml -o json)
code=$?
set -e

outcome=$(jq -r '.outcome // "error"' <<<"$report")
case "$code:$outcome" in
  0:verified)
    echo "reusing $(jq -r .reference <<<"$report") (result: $(jq -r .result <<<"$report"))"
    [ "$(jq -r .result <<<"$report")" = passed ] || exit 1
    ;;
  4:miss)
    echo "no attestation for $(jq -r .fingerprint <<<"$report"), running test"
    ./run-tests.sh
    ;;
  5:verification-failed | 5:verified) # 5:verified: a rejected candidate failed verification
    echo "::error::untrusted attestation for $(jq -r .testId <<<"$report")"
    ./notify-security.sh "$report"
    ./run-tests.sh
    ;;
  *)
    echo "aval could not decide (exit $code), running test"
    ./run-tests.sh
    ;;
esac

Check both the exit code and outcome. Exit 5 is a security event whatever the outcome: with verified, a rejected candidate failed verification. Treat any other disagreement as error.

docs.title: Guidance
docs.text:
• Always verify. Parse and Validate only check structure; a parsed predicate is a claim, and runner.identity is self-reported.
  • Pin versions. Check schemaVersion == "v2" on predicates (Validate does this) and version == "aval.trianalab.io/verify-report/v1" on reports. Reject versions you do not know. Within a version, ignore unknown fields.
  • Treat verification-failed as a security event, fail closed, consume by digest and never widen cacheability: see fail closed.
  • Your metadata goes in annotations with reverse-DNS keys (dev.pacto.service). Aval never reads them and will not add consumer fields.

docs.title: Mutable reference scan
docs.text: Which references does Aval report, and what can it miss? The full rules behind Pin your dependencies.

docs.title: How the scan works
docs.text:
• It reads files only; it never fetches, resolves or runs anything.
  • At most 1 MiB per file. A bigger or unreadable file it should check is a scan finding that cannot be accepted: shrink or split it.
  • Lockfiles (pnpm-lock.yaml, go.sum, Cargo.lock, ...) are hashed, not scanned.

docs.title: Python
docs.text:
• Generate the file: uv pip compile --generate-hashes requirements.in -o requirements.txt, then pip install --require-hashes -r requirements.txt.
  • Once one entry of a requirements file has a hash, every entry needs one.
  • Any requirements*.txt path is checked, also requirements/dev.txt.
  • Poetry needs poetry.lock and Pipenv Pipfile.lock next to the manifest. A pyproject.toml with [project] dependencies needs uv.lock, pdm.lock or poetry.lock, next to it or at the workspace root.
  • A file named by pip install -r/-c, or by an include line inside a requirements file (resolved next to that file), must be in the scope, or it is reported.

docs.title: Container images
docs.text:
• Images in test code: in *.go, *.py, *.java, *.kt, *.ts, *.js and *.cs files that mention testcontainers, a quoted name:tag without a digest (PostgresContainer("postgres:16")). A localhost, dotted or 4+ digit host:port literal ("localhost:5432", "127.0.0.1:8080", "db:5432"), a clock time ("12:30"), a sha256: digest, a literal with a space or a scheme, and a name without a tag are not reported. Any other quoted name:tag, such as "classpath:schema.sql", is reported and can be accepted in scope.allowMutable; an image whose tag is 4 or more digits without a registry ("app:2024") is taken for a host:port and not reported.
  • Images in docker run, podman run, docker compose and kubectl run/create --image commands. A compose file the command uses must be in scope.source; it can be YAML or JSON (compose.json).
  • An image from a variable Aval cannot resolve (${DB_IMAGE}), a Helm template ({{ .Values.image }}), a YAML alias, block scalar or tag (image: *img, image: >-, image: !!str ...) is reported: write the reference inline, or render the chart into the scope.
  • Dockerfiles are read twice. The line pass reads each line as an instruction (continuations joined with a space, RUN heredocs as scripts). The BuildKit pass splits the file as BuildKit does, for files named Dockerfile, Dockerfile.*, *.dockerfile, Dockerfile plus a name without a dot (Dockerfile-dev), and the same with Containerfile: comment lines stand alone, continuations join with nothing between (FROM db:1\ then 6 is db:16), # escape= sets the escape character (continuations and heredoc words), heredoc bodies are kept apart.
  • Both passes treat COPY --from= and RUN --mount=...,from= like a FROM: a stage name or index is fine, an image needs a digest. An instruction behind ONBUILD is checked like the same one without it.
  • The BuildKit pass also reports a file BuildKit refuses (an invalid # escape=, a repeated directive, an unterminated heredoc), a heredoc name with a quote, \ or $, or an empty one, and a FROM image with a variable that is not a global ARG with a value (FROM alpine:$V): give the global ARG a default, or write the image.
  • Kustomize: an images: (or imageTags:) entry with newName or newTag needs a digest:. Reported by name and index (resources[2]): a remote or out-of-scope resources, components or bases entry (vendor it); a patch or replacements entry that sets an image, or is given by an out-of-scope path; a transformers or generators entry with an image transformer or an out-of-scope path; a helmCharts entry, unless the chart is local (no repo, Chart.yaml in the scope under helmGlobals.chartHome, default charts, inside the kustomization directory) and no valuesInline sets an image; any tagSuffix (kustomize drops the digest). An undecodable kustomization is reported by its path. The overlay is not built.
  • YAML is read twice: the line pass matches image: on every line, also inside a block scalar a template renders; the parser matches every key that decodes to image ("ima\x67e":, ? image, !!binary aW1hZ2U=:). A key with another tag, or one the parser cannot decode in a file it rejects, is reported; in *.tpl files, files under templates/ and rejected files, a key a template writes (ima{{ "ge" }}:) is reported by its text, except a range key variable alone ({{ $key | quote }}:) directly under labels: or annotations:. A Compose build.dockerfile_inline is checked as a Dockerfile, and build.additional_contexts values with docker-image:// as images.
  • JSON is read the same way, but only in Compose files, files under templates/ and files a kustomization in scope lists in resources.

docs.title: Scripts
docs.text:
Reported, also in Dockerfile RUN lines and heredocs:

  • curl … | sh, also through tee;
  • bash -c "$(curl …)", python -c "$(curl …)", eval "$(curl …)";
  • source <(wget …);
  • releases/latest URLs.

Files scanned as scripts: *.sh, *.bash, *.zsh, *.mk, Makefile, and in-scope files without an extension whose first line is a sh, bash, zsh, ksh or dash shebang (./setup). A script with another extension is hashed but not scanned.

docs.title: scope.allowMutable
docs.text:
• ref is the text Aval prints: for a missing lockfile, the manifest path (go.mod); quotes in shell commands are dropped. A finding Aval reports because it cannot tell (a templated key, resources[2], a heredoc name, a FROM line) is in the container ecosystem, accepted by its printed ref.
  • file is the path Aval prints before the line number, relative to the contract (runner.command for the command), and limits the entry to that file. Without it, a ref that two files report (resources[0] repeats) is not accepted, and the finding asks for file.
  • files is a list of globs, matched like scope.source, instead of file (not both). The entry accepts its exact ref in every file in scope that a glob matches, never in runner.command. Each glob must match a file in scope, or the contract is invalid (exit 2). There is no ref wildcard: every accepted reference is one somebody wrote down.
  • With scope.contracts, each contract's entries apply to its own findings.
  • It is part of the contract, so it changes the fingerprint and shows in review.
  • aval run still prints the finding, marked (allowed: <reason>).

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
The scanner reads text and is a safety net, not a guarantee; the guarantee is the declared scope and the pins you write.

  • Not detected: unversioned downloads other than releases/latest (curl -o tool URL, curl URL | tar x); Helm values split into repository and tag, or YAML a template prints; a JSON6902 patch file in the scope named by path:; JSON outside the files above; --build-arg values (the ARG default is checked; outside FROM the last value of a name wins); the BuildKit pass on a source file named like dockerfile_test.go.
  • In test code: an image in a variable built from parts, in a constant or helper in a file that does not mention testcontainers, a module's default image (PostgresContainer() without an image), the Ryuk reaper image, source files larger than 1 MiB or unreadable, and source in other languages or extensions (.rs, .mjs, .tsx, .groovy, .scala). Write the image with its digest ("postgres:16@sha256:<digest>"), or declare it in scope.resolve.
  • Shell commands are split without a full parser: a quoted ; or > also splits, which can cause needless misses.
  • An option Aval does not know to take a value (tool --opt value install x) hides the subcommand.
  • For the gaps, declare the reference in scope.resolve (url, image) and run aval run --shadow.

docs.title: CLI output
docs.text: What exactly does aval run print, and where?

docs.title: Plain output
docs.text:
Output that is not a terminal (CI logs, a pipe), --plain, AVAL_OUTPUT=plain or TERM=dumb give plain lines:

miss hello sha256:d52167b4...
reason: localhost:5001/demo/hello-aval: no attestation found for fingerprint
--- run hello: grep -q hello src/hello.txt
--- end hello: passed (exit 0) in 12ms
ran hello: passed (exit 0)
summary: hello ran: passed in 12ms
  • The first line is <outcome> <test> <digest>.
  • When a value came from AVAL_REGISTRY, AVAL_POLICY or the policy's registry field, a config: line shows the registry and policy in use and where each came from (flag, env AVAL_REGISTRY, policy <file>).
  • The test's own output sits between --- run and --- end, untouched.
  • summary: may add ; saved <time> (display only), ; result pushed, ; reuse was off and ; SECURITY.
  • A failed test shows in summary: and in exit code 3.
  • The test can print a fake summary: line, so a script reads the last line of stdout.

docs.title: On a terminal
docs.text:
• One glyph line per step: ✓ done, ↺ reused, ✗ failed or SECURITY, ⚠ reuse off, · neutral.
  • Digests show as 8 hex characters. The REJECTED line keeps the whole digest.
  • One closing sentence says what happened.
  • After a verification failure nothing is green.
  • NO_COLOR drops colour only. Windows gets no colour.
  • Styled warnings go to stderr only when stderr is a terminal too.

docs.title: Spinner
docs.text:
When stderr is a terminal, a wait of more than 300ms shows a spinner on stderr, such as ⠹ looking up localhost:5001… 4s. It covers:

  • looking up and fetching a result
  • pushing one (aval run --push, aval push)
  • reading run records (aval stats)

It is erased before anything else prints, and on Ctrl-C. Windows gets no spinner.

docs.title: stderr
docs.text:
Line When aval: warning: reuse off: <cause> an error turned reuse off; the test still runs aval: SECURITY: ... a verification failure, or a fingerprint flooded with more attestations than Aval lists; aval run repeats it as the last line aval: running "<command>": ... the command cannot start; no --- end or summary: follows

Outcomes: Outcomes. Exit codes: CLI reference.

docs.title: Pin your dependencies
docs.text:
Goal: no input that can change behind the same name.

flowchart LR
  f([mutable reference]) --> c{cacheability}
  c -- "hermetic,<br>controlled-environment" --> m([miss, nothing published]):::muted
  c -- external-dependencies --> p([printed only])
  c -- non-deterministic --> n([never reused anyway])

Aval hashes the text postgres:16, not the image behind it. A repushed tag would not change the fingerprint, so Aval reports it and does not reuse:

mutable: compose.yaml:3 (container) postgres:16: a tag can be repushed: pin the image by digest (name:tag@sha256:...)
  • The line names file:line, ecosystem, the reference and the fix.
  • aval verify exits 4; aval run --push and aval push publish nothing.
  • aval explain prints it on stderr.
  • The scan reads files only. It never fetches or runs anything.

docs.title: Fix it by ecosystem
docs.text:
Ecosystem Commit and add to scope.dependencies In files and commands, pin Go go.sum go install x@v0.30.0, not @latest or @main JavaScript a lockfile (package-lock.json, npm-shrinkwrap.json, yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml, bun.lock or bun.lockb); without one every range is reported npm ci, npx --yes prettier@3.3.3; to run the lockfile's binary, npx --no vite, npm exec --no -- vite, pnpm exec vite or yarn exec vite Python requirements with == (better with hashes), or poetry.lock, Pipfile.lock, uv.lock, pdm.lock git requirements @<40-hex>; files named by -r/-c must be in scope Rust Cargo.lock (workspace root) cargo install tool --version 1.2.3 Maven, Gradle no SNAPSHOT, LATEST, RELEASE, 1.+, latest.release or ranges in pom.xml, build.gradle(.kts), *.versions.toml Ruby, PHP Gemfile.lock (or gems.locked), composer.lock gem install tool --version 1.2.3 OS packages apt-get install curl=8.5.0-2, apk add jq=1.7.1-r0, dnf/yum/microdnf install curl-7.76.1-26.el9, zypper install vim=9.0, or bake them into an image pinned by digest Helm helm install/upgrade --version 1.2.3 for a chart outside the scope; a chart in the scope is checked as files Git git clone URL && git -C dir checkout <40-hex>, one checkout per clone; no git pull, no submodule branch = or update --remote

Python details: Python.

docs.title: Container images
docs.text:
Pin every image by digest. Keep the tag for readers; the digest decides.

# compose.yaml, Kubernetes manifests, rendered Helm charts
image: redis:7.4-alpine@sha256:c5d34a98396a4775e223c74e929162c35c5a2182901ba26b50ade939941ce14b

# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1@sha256:<digest>
FROM golang:1.25@sha256:<digest> AS build
FROM build AS test          # a stage name is fine
COPY --from=nginx:1.27@sha256:<digest> /etc/nginx /etc/nginx
ADD --checksum=sha256:<sum> https://example.com/tool.tgz /tool.tgz

Find the digest with crane digest <image:tag>. Testcontainers, Dockerfiles, Kustomize and YAML rules: Container images.

docs.title: Scripts from the network
docs.text: curl … | sh, eval "$(curl …)" and releases/latest URLs run whatever the server sends. Vendor the script into the scope, or download a fixed version and check its sha256. All variants and which files are scanned.

docs.title: Resolve a reference instead
docs.text: To follow a tag on purpose, declare it in scope.resolve (Resolve references). The fingerprint then changes when the target moves; the scan still reports it, so pin or accept it.

docs.title: Accept a reference on purpose
docs.text:
Such as an image your team rebuilds and scans every night. Say why in the contract:

apiVersion: aval.trianalab.io/v1
kind: Test
metadata:
  name: orders-integration
runner:
  command: ["docker", "compose", "run", "--rm", "tests"]
scope:
  source: ["**/*.go", "compose.yaml", "deploy/**", "charts/**"]
  allowMutable:
    - ref: postgres:16          # exactly as Aval prints it
      reason: rebuilt and scanned nightly; the tag is ours
    - file: deploy/kustomization.yaml   # only the finding in this file
      ref: resources[0]
      reason: vendored upstream base, reviewed on update
    - files: ["charts/*/values.yaml"]   # every matched file in scope
      ref: ghcr.io/stefanprodan/podinfo:6.5.0
      reason: public demo image, same tag in every chart
cacheability: controlled-environment
  • ref is the text Aval prints; file limits the entry to one file, files to the files its globs match.
  • It changes the fingerprint and shows in review.
  • aval run still prints the finding, marked (allowed: <reason>).

Fine print: scope.allowMutable. The scan is a safety net, not a guarantee: Limits.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
What does Aval do? See it in five minutes on your laptop: a miss, a reuse, a changed input and a rejected result.

You need aval (Install) and Docker. Run the blocks in order in one shell. text blocks show the output; ... changes per run.

docs.title: 1. Set up
docs.text:
Start a local registry on port 5001 (macOS keeps 5000 for AirPlay):

docker rm -f aval-registry 2>/dev/null || true
docker run -d --name aval-registry -p 5001:5000 registry:2

Make a project with one input file. aval init writes:

  • aval.yaml: the test command and the files it reads (scope);
  • a signing key;
  • policy.yaml: a trust policy that trusts that key.

You declare what the test reads (--source); Aval never guesses:

rm -rf aval-demo && mkdir aval-demo && cd aval-demo
mkdir src && echo hello > src/hello.txt
aval init --name hello --source 'src/**' --cacheability hermetic --key aval.key -- grep -q hello src/hello.txt

source matches 1 file: src/hello.txt
wrote aval.key (private: keep it secret, do not commit it) and aval.pub, key id ...
wrote policy.yaml: trusts aval.pub at trust level developer
wrote aval.yaml
added aval.key, .aval/ to .gitignore
next: export AVAL_REGISTRY=<oci repository> AVAL_POLICY=policy.yaml, then aval run --push --key aval.key

Without flags, aval init asks for each value. Now set the registry and the policy once for this shell:

export AVAL_REGISTRY=localhost:5001/demo/hello-aval AVAL_POLICY=policy.yaml

docs.title: 2. First run: a miss
docs.text:
Nothing is stored for these inputs yet: the test runs, then --push signs the result and stores it:

aval run --push --key aval.key

This is the plain output, as in CI. A terminal shows glyph lines instead.

config: registry=localhost:5001/demo/hello-aval (env AVAL_REGISTRY) policy=policy.yaml (env AVAL_POLICY)
miss hello sha256:640f5db75fa5b71422b1afaffb4c645194aaccb223dae9070968e375bccbaf42
reason: localhost:5001/demo/hello-aval: no attestation found for fingerprint
--- run hello: grep -q hello src/hello.txt
--- end hello: passed (exit 0) in ...
ran hello: passed (exit 0)
pushed localhost:5001/demo/hello-aval@sha256:...
summary: hello ran: passed in ...; result pushed

docs.title: 3. Second run: a reuse
docs.text:
Is there a trusted result for these inputs?

aval verify
echo "exit code: $?"

config: registry=localhost:5001/demo/hello-aval (env AVAL_REGISTRY) policy=policy.yaml (env AVAL_POLICY)
verified hello sha256:640f5db75fa5b71422b1afaffb4c645194aaccb223dae9070968e375bccbaf42
signer: key ..., trust level developer
reference: localhost:5001/demo/hello-aval@sha256:...
exit code: 0

Run again. The test is skipped:

aval run

config: registry=localhost:5001/demo/hello-aval (env AVAL_REGISTRY) policy=policy.yaml (env AVAL_POLICY)
verified hello sha256:640f5db75fa5b71422b1afaffb4c645194aaccb223dae9070968e375bccbaf42
signer: key ..., trust level developer
reference: localhost:5001/demo/hello-aval@sha256:...
reused passed result
summary: hello reused: passed; saved ...

docs.title: 4. Change an input: a miss again
docs.text:
Edit a file in scope. New fingerprint, nothing matches, the test runs:

echo "hello, world" > src/hello.txt
aval run

config: registry=localhost:5001/demo/hello-aval (env AVAL_REGISTRY) policy=policy.yaml (env AVAL_POLICY)
miss hello sha256:944c02c002bb6830480c64e44594d52265970351501f2372947e054795c37fc0
reason: localhost:5001/demo/hello-aval: no attestation found for fingerprint
--- run hello: grep -q hello src/hello.txt
--- end hello: passed (exit 0) in ...
ran hello: passed (exit 0)
summary: hello ran: passed in ...

docs.title: 5. A result from an untrusted signer: exit 5
docs.text:
Someone pushes a result signed with a key your policy does not trust (AVAL_POLICY= drops your policy for that one push). Aval rejects it, runs the test and exits 5: a security event, not a miss.

aval keygen other
AVAL_POLICY= aval run --push --key other.key
aval run
echo "exit code: $?"

wrote other.key (private: keep it secret, do not commit it) and other.pub
key id: ...
next: trust other.pub in your policy (publicKey: other.pub) and sign with --key other.key
config: registry=localhost:5001/demo/hello-aval (env AVAL_REGISTRY)
miss hello sha256:944c02c002bb6830480c64e44594d52265970351501f2372947e054795c37fc0
reason: reuse off: no trust policy (set AVAL_POLICY or --policy)
--- run hello: grep -q hello src/hello.txt
--- end hello: passed (exit 0) in ...
ran hello: passed (exit 0)
pushed localhost:5001/demo/hello-aval@sha256:...
summary: hello ran: passed in ...; result pushed; reuse was off
config: registry=localhost:5001/demo/hello-aval (env AVAL_REGISTRY) policy=policy.yaml (env AVAL_POLICY)
aval: SECURITY: 1 attestation(s) for hello failed signature or policy verification; treat it as a security event, see https://aval.run/.../trust-model/
verification-failed hello sha256:944c02c002bb6830480c64e44594d52265970351501f2372947e054795c37fc0
reference: localhost:5001/demo/hello-aval@sha256:...
reason: attestation verification failed: signature: signer key id "..." is not in the trust policy (trust policy policy.yaml)
--- run hello: grep -q hello src/hello.txt
--- end hello: passed (exit 0) in ...
ran hello: passed (exit 0)
summary: hello ran: passed in ...; SECURITY
aval: SECURITY: 1 attestation(s) for hello failed signature or policy verification; treat it as a security event, see https://aval.run/.../trust-model/
exit code: 5

docs.title: What just happened
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  files[src/hello.txt<br>listed in scope] --> fp[fingerprint<br>sha256:fb39...]
  fp --> look{result for this<br>fingerprint?}
  look -- no --> miss([miss: run the test<br>steps 2 and 4]):::muted
  look -- "yes, every signer in policy.yaml" --> ok([verified: reuse,<br>skip the test<br>step 3]):::ok
  look -- "yes, any untrusted signer" --> bad([security event:<br>run the test, exit 5<br>step 5]):::err

Stop the registry:

docker rm -f aval-registry

Next: write a contract, then use GitHub Actions. Already have CI for a monorepo? Integrate Aval in 5 files.

docs.title: Stats
docs.text:
How much does Aval reuse in real CI? Live numbers from every repository that records runs to ghcr.io/trianalab/aval-stats, Aval's own CI included.

Live statistics are not available right now: stats.json is missing, malformed or more than 6 hours old.

Run records are unsigned statistics. They never affect reuse.

docs.title: Where the numbers come from
docs.text:
Twice an hour, and on every push to main, the docs workflow runs:

aval stats --registry ghcr.io/trianalab/aval-stats \
  --by repository --since 30d -o json

and publishes the stats report as stats.json at the site root. If a refresh fails, the previous file stays.

To keep statistics for your own repositories, see Measure reuse. To add a TrianaLab repository to these numbers, see CONTRIBUTING.md.

docs.title: Publish from GitHub Actions
docs.text:
The publish action sends the run record of every artifact in the workflow run, verified hits and verification failures included, to a registry of another repository's package:

- uses: TrianaLab/aval/integrations/github/publish@<sha> # pin by commit SHA
  with:
    stats: "true"
    stats-registry: ghcr.io/trianalab/aval-stats
  • stats-registry is host[:port]/path, with no scheme, credentials or @; anything else exits 2 before anything is pushed. Empty, records go to the policy's registry.
  • The registry credentials (github.token by default) go to it only when it is on the host of the policy's registry.
  • The job's packages: write reaches another repository's package only when that package grants the publishing repository write access (package settings, "Manage Actions access"). Until then each record is a warning.
  • A record that cannot be published never fails the step, and a verification failure still exits 5.

docs.title: Trust model
docs.text: Formats are frozen; see artifact format.

docs.title: What a signature proves
docs.text:
An attestation is a DSSE envelope around an in-toto Statement whose predicate says: "test test.id, with inputs hashing to execution.fingerprint, produced result on subject".

Proves Does not prove who signed: an OIDC issuer and subject (keyless), or a key that the test ran that nobody changed the claim since that it ran honestly (unmodified test code, no skipped cases, no patched runner) that inputs not declared in aval.yaml were the same

Reuse needs all three: a valid signature, a signer the policy trusts at a high enough level, and a fingerprint and test id that match what Aval computed locally. The predicate's runner block is only a claim: identity comes from the verified signer, level from the policy. A key signer matches only publicKey entries, a keyless signer only issuer + subjectRegexp entries.

docs.title: Signing
docs.text:
Mode Where Signs with Rekor Usual level keyless CI an ephemeral key and a short-lived Fulcio certificate for the OIDC token in $SIGSTORE_ID_TOKEN always (the certificate expires in minutes; Rekor's timestamp keeps it verifiable) runner key local an unencrypted ECDSA P-256 PEM key (PKCS#8 or SEC1); Cosign keys are encrypted and not supported no developer

Make a key with aval keygen (writes aval.key and aval.pub). Getting the OIDC token is the caller's job, so no CI vendor or issuer is assumed.

Signing always uses the Sigstore public-good instance (https://fulcio.sigstore.dev, https://rekor.sigstore.dev) (TODO(milestone-5): signing against a private Sigstore deployment; verification already accepts its pinned trustedRoot).

docs.title: Trust levels
docs.text:
Higher is stronger:

Level Name Constant Who Good for 0 unknown TrustUnknown level could not be established never accepted 1 developer TrustDeveloper a developer's local signature personal acceleration only: skip a test you already ran on your machine. Not full trust. 2 runner TrustRunner a CI runner with a verifiable workload identity (e.g. GitHub Actions OIDC) reuse in CI. CI should require at least this level. 3 isolated TrustIsolated an isolated execution with a verifiable attestation of the environment itself reuse where the runner host is not trusted either

docs.title: Policy
docs.text: The trust policy decides which signers are accepted and at what level.

docs.title: Policy file
docs.text:
apiVersion: aval.trianalab.io/v1
kind: Policy
minTrustLevel: runner           # developer | runner | isolated
# trustedRoot: sigstore/trusted_root.json  # keyless only; default: Sigstore public-good, fetched with TUF
identities:
  - issuer: https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com
    subjectRegexp: https://github\.com/acme/orders/\.github/workflows/ci\.yaml@refs/heads/main
    trustLevel: runner
  - publicKey: keys/alice.pub   # PEM public key file
    trustLevel: developer
allowedCacheability: [external-dependencies]
Field Meaning identities the signers you accept: each is an OIDC issuer plus a subjectRegexp matched against the whole certificate subject, or a publicKey PEM file. At least one. trustLevel the level an identity gets: developer, runner or isolated. minTrustLevel the lowest level a result needs to be reused. --min-trust-level or AVAL_MIN_TRUST_LEVEL on run and verify can raise it for one run, never lower it (a lower or unknown level exits 2). allowedCacheability classes reused besides hermetic and controlled-environment; only external-dependencies has an effect, and non-deterministic is rejected. trustedRoot a pinned Sigstore trusted root for keyless signatures; without it, the public-good root is fetched. registry optional: the OCI repository of attestations (host/name), used by aval run and aval verify when neither --registry nor AVAL_REGISTRY is set. No credentials: a value with user:password@ (or any @) exits 2. Logins come from the credential store.

Relative publicKey and trustedRoot paths are read from the policy file's directory. A policy with an unknown field, a bad level or identity, or more than one document is rejected, never half-read (every policy error).

docs.title: Verification order
docs.text:
flowchart TB
  sig{signature valid?} -- yes --> who{signer in<br>the policy?}
  who -- yes --> st{statement and predicate<br>well-formed, subject matches?}
  st -- yes --> fp{fingerprint and<br>test id match?}
  fp -- yes --> cls{signed cacheability equals<br>the contract's?}
  cls -- yes --> lvl{level ≥<br>minTrustLevel?}
  lvl -- yes --> ok([verified]):::ok
  lvl -- no --> miss([miss, exit 4]):::muted
  sig -- no --> bad([verification-failed, exit 5]):::err
  who -- no --> bad
  st -- no --> bad
  fp -- no --> bad
  cls -- no --> bad

A class the policy does not allow (non-deterministic, or external-dependencies not in allowedCacheability) is a miss before any lookup.

A result whose only problem is a level below minTrustLevel, such as a developer result under a CI policy, is routine non-reuse: a miss, listed in rejected, never a security event. Go callers of evidence.Verify get ErrVerification for a level below the minimum; the CLI treats it as a miss.

Signature checks (sigstore-go, against the bundle stored next to the envelope):

  • Keyless: chains to a Fulcio CA in the trusted root, has an embedded SCT from a trusted CT log, a Rekor entry, and a trusted timestamp inside the certificate's validity.
  • Key: verifies with one of the policy's public keys; no Rekor entry.
  • Both: the envelope must be the exact one the bundle signs; no bundle means no verification.

Without --policy or AVAL_POLICY nothing is trusted and nothing is looked up: miss. A policy or trusted root that cannot load: outcome error (exit 1), and the test runs.

docs.title: Keyless verification needs the network and a writable HOME
docs.text:
Keyless policies without trustedRoot fetch the Sigstore root with TUF (tuf-repo-cdn.sigstore.dev) the first time a candidate carries a certificate, and cache it in $HOME/.sigstore. Offline or with a read-only HOME, that candidate is error (never verification-failed) and the test runs. A miss or a key-based result never fetches it.

To avoid the dependency, pin the trusted root in the policy:

  1. Get trusted_root.json once, on a machine with network access. After one keyless aval verify there, sigstore-go has it at $HOME/.sigstore/root/tuf-repo-cdn.sigstore.dev/targets/trusted_root.json.
  2. Commit it next to the policy and set trustedRoot: trusted_root.json (relative to the policy file).
  3. Refresh it when Sigstore rotates keys: a stale root fails to verify new certificates (outcome verification-failed), so watch for that after a Sigstore announcement.

Policies with only publicKey identities never fetch anything.

docs.title: Take the policy from a protected branch
docs.text:
A pull request can change any file in its checkout. If its CI job reads --policy (or --registry) from that checkout, the PR can add its own signing identity, sign a passing result for its own inputs, and get a green check it wrote itself. Read the policy, and with it the registry, from the default branch instead. Not from github.base_ref: a PR can target any branch, including one its author controls.

AVAL_POLICY and AVAL_REGISTRY count the same as the flags (a flag wins; empty is unset). Set them in the step, or from the default branch as below, never from a file in the checkout. The registry has one more source, the policy's registry field: --registry > AVAL_REGISTRY > policy, and the config: line names the source that won (registry=<x> (policy <file>)). The policy is trusted only because it comes from the protected branch, so its registry is too. Nothing else names them: there is no config file and no aval.yaml or TestSet field.

on: pull_request
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Trust policy from the default branch
        env:
          DEFAULT_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}
        run: |
          git fetch --no-tags --depth=1 origin "+refs/heads/$DEFAULT_BRANCH:refs/remotes/origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH"
          git show "origin/$DEFAULT_BRANCH:.aval/policy.yaml" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/policy.yaml"
      - run: aval run --policy "$RUNNER_TEMP/policy.yaml"

Here the registry is the policy's registry field, read from the default branch with the policy. Keep it out of files the PR can change for its own run: put it in that policy, write it in the step, or read it from the default branch the same way. A trustedRoot path in the policy resolves next to the temp file, so read that file from the default branch as well, or use the default root.

Run a pinned aval release, and take any script the step runs from the default branch too, so the workflow file is the only part a PR can change. That part it can still change: on pull_request, GitHub runs the PR's own workflow file, so a hostile PR can edit the step and make its own check green. No check in that run can stop it. What protects the default branch is review: CODEOWNERS for the workflows, the policy and the tests that guard them, a branch rule that requires code-owner review, and a default branch that trusts only its own CI (in Aval's case, ci.yaml on main at runner level, the minimum main raises to).

docs.title: Fail closed
docs.text:
If Aval cannot prove that a previous execution is equivalent and trusted, the test runs.

  • Fingerprint errors (empty scope, a glob that matches nothing, a symlink, an unreadable file): nothing to look up; the test runs.
  • Registry errors (unreachable, auth): outcome error, exit 1; the test runs.
  • Malformed manifest or moved tag: verification failure, exit 5.
  • Consume by digest: the tag sha256-<fingerprint hex> is only an index; everything after lookup uses repo@sha256:... (lookup).
  • No silent replacement: pushes only add results. Every candidate is verified and the highest trusted level wins. A candidate that fails verification is listed in rejected and stays visible; one that cannot be fetched or checked blocks reuse. More than 64 candidates is verification-failed (exit 5) with an aval: SECURITY: line naming the cap: none was verified, so an untrusted one may hide among them.
  • Unknown or missing fields in aval.yaml: rejected, exit 2.

aval run --no-reuse always runs and never looks anything up. What each outcome does: Outcomes.

docs.title: Safeguards in aval run
docs.text:
• $SIGSTORE_ID_TOKEN is removed from the environment before runner.command starts, so the code under test cannot sign as the CI job.
  • $AVAL_DOCKER_CONFIG, the registry credentials Aval uses instead of $DOCKER_CONFIG's, is removed the same way, so a CI step can hand Aval a read token the test does not get through its environment. It is not a sandbox: code in the same job, as the same user, can still reach the job's files and processes.
  • A --report-file that cannot be written disables reuse: the test runs, and a verification failure still exits 5.
  • Reasons from attestations are escaped on text output and stderr (\n, \x1b, \u2028), so they never start a line of their own; the JSON report keeps them as is.
  • --shadow verifies and runs the test anyway, and exits 1 with aval: FALSE HIT: ... when a verified result disagrees with the real run.
  • --stats publishes an unsigned run record for every outcome; it never affects reuse or the exit code (run records).
  • Restored outputs are as trustworthy as the signer that published them: a signer at the policy's minimum level can publish any coverage or junit content a later gate reads. Aval checks only that the outputs match the signed digests and the contract's outputs globs, are not the contract file, lie outside the scope, .git and .aval, and that no symlink is on the way.

docs.title: Miss vs verification failure
docs.text:
Outcome Go error verified nil miss wraps evidence.ErrNotFound (a level below minTrustLevel: CLI only) verification-failed wraps evidence.ErrVerification; *evidence.VerificationError carries the reason error any other

A verification failure means someone published a result under this fingerprint that does not verify. Run the test and surface it: fail the job or alert. Never fold it into a silent re-run.

docs.title: Cacheability classes
docs.text:
The class is part of the contract, so it is part of the fingerprint, and it is copied into the predicate as test.cacheability.

Class Use it when Reused hermetic the test reads only the declared files yes controlled-environment it uses services you pin, such as a Compose image by digest yes external-dependencies it calls something you do not control only if the policy allows it non-deterministic the same inputs can give a different result never

A candidate whose signed test.cacheability differs from the local contract's is a verification failure.

docs.title: Threats
docs.text: Threat Mitigation Compromised developer key Policy grants developer identities level 1 at most; CI sets minTrustLevel >= 2, so a stolen developer key cannot satisfy CI. It can still poison that developer's own reuse. Prefer keyless (short-lived Fulcio certs, Rekor log) over long-lived keys. Tag swapping (sha256-<fp> repointed to another manifest) Tag is lookup only and must resolve to the fingerprint's deterministic anchor manifest; any other target is verification-failed. Candidates are the anchor's referrers, fetched and verified by digest. Replay of a passing result for a different fingerprint or test id Verification requires the signed fingerprint and test id to equal the ones computed locally. The signed predicate cannot be re-labeled without breaking the signature. Mismatch is verification-failed. Secret hashed into the manifest (an environment.env name or PREFIX_* pattern that covers a token) The manifest --explain prints carries the sha256 of every hashed value, never the value, and the published fingerprint hashes that manifest; a short or guessable secret can be brute-forced from either by someone who knows the other inputs. List exact names instead of a prefix that covers credentials (Environment variable patterns). Undeclared input changed (file outside scope, unlisted env var, network service) Not detected: the fingerprint only covers declared inputs. Mitigated by contract review, external-dependencies not being reusable by default and non-deterministic never being reusable, and the false-hit suite. Observed-input tracing is future work; until then, find undeclared inputs by hand. Content behind a declared name changed (repushed image tag, new upstream release, changed remote script) The scanner reports the mutable references it recognizes in the scope and runner.command; for hermetic and controlled-environment an unaccepted one makes the lookup a miss and blocks publishing. Accepting one needs scope.allowMutable, which changes the fingerprint and shows in review. References it does not recognize stay a known gap (Pin your dependencies). Registry compromise (attacker can write arbitrary manifests and tags) Cannot forge signatures, so it cannot produce reuse on its own; injected attestations show up as verification-failed, or, when another candidate verifies, as a rejected entry with an aval: SECURITY: ... line on stderr that blocks reuse and exits 5. It can delete attestations (forcing re-runs) or deny service (re-run), for example by pushing more than 64 attestations for a fingerprint, which is verification-failed (exit 5) with an aval: SECURITY: line as a possible flooding attempt. Availability is out of scope. Forged or tampered run records (anyone with push access) Unsigned statistics, never read by aval run or aval verify; aval stats skips malformed records and caps how many it reads. Pull request that edits the policy or registry its own CI reads Read both from the default branch (the registry can live in the policy's registry field, so one file read from the protected branch carries both; aval.yaml, TestSets and config files cannot name it) (Take the policy from a protected branch) and verify with a pinned aval release. The workflow file still comes from the PR, so a hostile PR can make its own check green; required code-owner review keeps it off the default branch, which trusts only its own CI. Dishonest but trusted signer (ran a modified test and signed "passed") Out of scope for Aval. A signature proves who claims it, not that the test ran honestly. Limit which identities get which level; level 3 (isolated) exists for this.

docs.title: Vision and roadmap
docs.text: Why does Aval exist, and where is it going?

docs.title: Thesis
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  run([run once]) --> sign[sign] --> reg[registry] --> v{policy trusts it,<br>same fingerprint?}
  v -- yes --> reuse([reuse]):::ok
  v -- no --> again([run the test]):::muted
  • An expensive test runs once and its result is signed and stored in an OCI registry.
  • Any other job with the same inputs verifies it and, if the policy allows, skips the test.
  • Not a cache: a cache tolerates a stale entry now and then. Aval must justify every reuse; when it cannot, the test runs.
  • A signature proves who claims a pass, not that the inputs match. So reuse needs a declared input contract (aval.yaml) and a trust policy.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: Heavy tests (integration, end-to-end, hardware) rerun on every pipeline even when nothing they read changed. Teams pay in time, or skip tests on judgment nobody can audit. Build caches help only teams on a hermetic build system.

docs.title: Design decisions
docs.text: Decision Why No own infrastructure: ORAS, Sigstore (sigstore-go), in-toto/DSSE, OCI 1.1 referrers. Lookup by the tag sha256-<fingerprint hex>, consumption by digest registries, signing and access control already exist and are operated; tags are mutable, digests aren't Scope belongs to the test contract (aval.yaml); nothing is inferred or traced the test author knows what the test depends on, and a declared scope can be reviewed in a PR Fail closed: if input equivalence can't be proven, the test runs. A miss (exit 4) and a verification failure (exit 5) stay separate, and the latter is never downgraded a false hit costs more than a re-run, and a forged result is something someone needs to look at Trust levels (developer, runner, isolated) granted by the policy; no policy, no reuse how much a signed claim is worth depends on where it was produced, and that call belongs to the consumer Test identity (metadata.name) is not the execution fingerprint the same check gets many executions, and policy and reporting need to tell them apart Cacheability classes; non-deterministic is never reusable a matching fingerprint only means something if the result depends on the declared inputs One generic runner: an argv command, the exit code is the result it covers every language, framework and CI vendor

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text:
• No registry, server or database of our own.
  • No runtime tracing or input inference in v0; "observed inputs" is future work, to check declared scope, not replace it.
  • Not a build system or a Bazel replacement.
  • Not a test framework: Aval records an exit code, not test cases.
  • No knowledge of Pacto or any other consumer; consumers use the stable formats.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text: Risk Mitigation Signal it isn't working Bazel or a remote cache is already enough target tests outside a hermetic build graph (integration, e2e, cross-environment) early users are mostly Bazel shops that want Aval for build actions Declaring scope costs more than it saves a small contract (globs, lockfiles, a toolchain map), debuggable with aval explain contracts drift from the code, or teams give up on wide-scope tests Inputs always change, so savings are small the docs say a "whole repo" scope is a bad fit a low hit rate in the example and in early adopters' pipelines Security policies reject developer signatures expected: CI requires runner or higher; developer stays personal the value does not hold with only runner and isolated signatures

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text:
# Milestone Status Done when 1 Fingerprint and contract implemented aval.yaml is validated with unknown fields rejected, and aval explain gives a deterministic aval-fingerprint digest that fails closed on unprovable inputs 2 Push and verify against a registry, with signing implemented aval run --push signs and publishes; aval verify and aval run reuse a trusted result (exit 0), report a miss (exit 4) and a tampered or untrusted one (exit 5); the policy format is defined 3 End-to-end example in GitHub Actions in progress (CI quality gates) a public example where one run publishes, an unchanged run reuses, and a changed run misses, all visible in the logs 4 False-hit suite implemented (false-hit suite, known gaps) every known kind of relevant change is shown not to reuse a previous execution 5 Stable consumption contract in progress the formats, pkg/evidence and the verify report are versioned with only additive changes in v1, and an external consumer verifies with pkg/evidence alone 6 Contract composition for monorepos (Epic 10) in progress: scope.contracts binds other local contracts, transitively (guide) a test in a monorepo reruns when, and only when, the declared inputs of the parts it depends on change

A remote dependency (another repository, by OCI reference) is an idea, not built: its files are not available to fingerprint, so it would bind a published, verified result instead, which raises its own trust questions.

docs.title: How Aval works
docs.text:
How does Aval decide to skip a test?

flowchart LR
  run([aval run]) --> fp[fingerprint] --> reg[registry] --> pol{policy<br>trusts it?}
  pol -- yes --> reuse([reuse]):::ok
  pol -- no --> exec[run the test] --> push([sign and push]):::muted
Step What happens Fingerprint hash aval.yaml and every input it lists into one sha256 Registry look up results stored under that fingerprint Policy the signer must be one your policy trusts Reuse or run trusted: skip the test. Anything else: run it (Outcomes) Push with --push, sign the new result and store it
  • No proof, no reuse: the test runs.
  • Aval does not guess inputs. A file aval.yaml does not list is invisible.
  • No server: results live in an OCI registry you already have.

See it: Quickstart. Specs: contract, trust model, artifact format.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
What does this word mean? Hover a dotted word anywhere in the docs for the short form.

Term Meaning More Attestation a signed statement: test X, with inputs that hash to fingerprint F, gave result R artifact format Cacheability how safe a test is to reuse: hermetic and controlled-environment yes, external-dependencies only if the policy allows it, non-deterministic never classes Contract aval.yaml: what the test is, how to run it, which inputs it reads the test contract Fingerprint one sha256 of every declared input: the contract (command included), files in scope, toolchain, env var values, resolved references. Same inputs, same fingerprint what goes in Mutable reference a tag or range that can point at other content later, such as postgres:16. Blocks reuse for hermetic and controlled-environment tests until you pin it or list it in scope.allowMutable Pin your dependencies Outcome the result of a lookup: verified, miss, verification-failed or error. Only verified skips the test Outcomes Policy your YAML file of trusted signers and their levels. No policy, no reuse Trust Registry the OCI registry that stores signed results, one you already run artifact format Scope the inputs the contract lists: source, dependencies (such as go.mod), resolve and contracts. Aval sees nothing else the test contract Signer who signed a result: a CI job (keyless, OIDC) or a key Trust Trust level how much the policy trusts a signer: developer, runner, isolated. Reuse needs at least minTrustLevel Trust

docs.title: Outcomes
docs.text:
What can a lookup end in? One of four outcomes. Only verified skips the test.

flowchart LR
  start([look up]) --> decide{could Aval<br>decide?}
  decide -- no --> error([error<br>exit 1]):::warn
  decide -- yes --> found{result<br>found?}
  found -- no --> miss([miss<br>exit 4]):::muted
  found -- yes --> valid{verifies?}
  valid -- yes --> verified([verified<br>exit 0]):::ok
  valid -- no --> failed([verification-failed<br>exit 5]):::err
Outcome Means aval run does verified a trusted result exists for these exact inputs reuses it: exit 0 for a pass, 3 for a failure; beside a result that fails verification it runs the test and exits 5 miss nothing to reuse yet runs the test error Aval could not decide, such as an unreachable registry runs the test verification-failed a result exists but does not verify runs the test, then exits 5

The diagram shows aval verify exit codes. All of them: exit codes.

docs.title: A miss is routine
docs.text:
You changed an input, so there is nothing to reuse. Also a miss:

  • no policy, or (for aval run) no registry, or --no-reuse
  • a non-deterministic test, or external-dependencies the policy does not allow
  • a mutable reference you did not pin or accept in scope.allowMutable
  • only signers below minTrustLevel

docs.title: A verification failure is a security event
docs.text:
A result under your fingerprint does not verify: a bad signature, an unknown signer, or a claim of other inputs. The cause is a wrong policy or an attacker. Aval runs the test, prints aval: SECURITY: ... and exits 5. Fail the job and investigate; never hide or retry it.

The same holds when another result verifies beside the bad one (the report says verified and lists the bad one in rejected): nothing is reused and the exit code is 5. More than 64 results for one fingerprint is verification-failed too: none is verified, so one may hide an attacker's.

docs.title: Read more
docs.text:
• What aval run prints: CLI output
  • Branch on exit codes in CI: Consume evidence
  • The JSON report: verify report

docs.title: Trust
docs.text:
Whose results does Aval reuse? Only those of signers your policy trusts. A result cannot vouch for itself.

flowchart LR
  r[signed result] --> sig{valid<br>signature?}
  sig -- no --> fail([verification-failed<br>exit 5]):::err
  sig -- yes --> who{signer in<br>the policy?}
  who -- no --> fail
  who -- yes --> lvl{level high<br>enough?}
  lvl -- no --> miss([miss<br>exit 4]):::muted
  lvl -- yes --> ok([reuse]):::ok

docs.title: Signers and levels
docs.text:
Signer Signs with Usual level CI job (keyless) a short-lived Sigstore certificate for its OIDC identity runner key a local ECDSA P-256 key file developer

Your policy sets the level. The level a result claims is ignored.

Level Name Constant Who Good for 0 unknown TrustUnknown level could not be established never accepted 1 developer TrustDeveloper a developer's local signature personal acceleration only: skip a test you already ran on your machine. Not full trust. 2 runner TrustRunner a CI runner with a verifiable workload identity (e.g. GitHub Actions OIDC) reuse in CI. CI should require at least this level. 3 isolated TrustIsolated an isolated execution with a verifiable attestation of the environment itself reuse where the runner host is not trusted either

docs.title: The policy
docs.text:
A YAML file in your repository. This one trusts the main workflow as runner and Alice's key as developer:

apiVersion: aval.trianalab.io/v1
kind: Policy
minTrustLevel: runner           # developer | runner | isolated
# trustedRoot: sigstore/trusted_root.json  # keyless only; default: Sigstore public-good, fetched with TUF
identities:
  - issuer: https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com
    subjectRegexp: https://github\.com/acme/orders/\.github/workflows/ci\.yaml@refs/heads/main
    trustLevel: runner
  - publicKey: keys/alice.pub   # PEM public key file
    trustLevel: developer
allowedCacheability: [external-dependencies]
  • With minTrustLevel: runner, Alice's result is a miss: the test runs.
  • No policy: nothing is trusted, every test runs.

docs.title: What a signature proves
docs.text:
• Proves: who signed, and that nobody changed the result since.
  • Does not prove: that the test ran honestly, or that inputs outside the contract were the same.

Grant a level only to signers you would trust to run the test yourself. Full spec: trust model.

docs.title: Depend on another part of the repo
docs.text:
Goal: in a monorepo, rerun the frontend tests when the backend's inputs change, without copying the backend's globs.

flowchart LR
  f[frontend/aval.yaml] -- scope.contracts --> b[backend/aval.yaml]
  b --> bs(["backend scope: api/**"])
  bs -. change .-> miss([frontend misses and runs]):::err

docs.title: The example
docs.text:
The frontend names the backend's contract:

frontend/aval.yaml
apiVersion: aval.trianalab.io/v1
kind: Test
metadata:
  name: frontend
runner:
  command: ["sh", "test.sh"]
scope:
  source: ["src/**", "test.sh"]
  contracts: ["../backend/aval.yaml"]
cacheability: hermetic
backend/aval.yaml
apiVersion: aval.trianalab.io/v1
kind: Test
metadata:
  name: backend
runner:
  command: ["go", "test", "./..."]
scope:
  source: ["api/**"]
cacheability: hermetic

The frontend's fingerprint now includes the backend's:

  • a change in the backend's scope: the frontend misses and runs;
  • a change outside it (a backend README): still reused;
  • contracts the backend names count too.

aval explain shows the link:

contract ../backend/aval.yaml backend sha256:<backend fingerprint>
depends on ../backend/aval.yaml (backend) sha256:<backend fingerprint>
  • Paths are relative and stay inside the git working tree. No other repositories.
  • If Aval cannot read the other contract, the test runs.
  • A mutable reference in the backend blocks the frontend too; only the backend's scope.allowMutable accepts it.

Using only the backend's interface (a generated client)? List the API file (OpenAPI, .proto) in scope.dependencies instead.

docs.title: Workspaces
docs.text:
uv, pnpm and cargo keep one lockfile at the root, and globs cannot use ... Two layouts work. Either one contract per member at the root:

aval.api.yaml
apiVersion: aval.trianalab.io/v1
kind: Test
metadata:
  name: api-unit
runner:
  command: ["uv", "run", "--package", "api", "pytest", "packages/api/tests"]
scope:
  source: ["packages/api/**"]
  dependencies: ["pyproject.toml", "uv.lock"]
cacheability: hermetic

Or a root contract owns the lockfile, and members name it (scope.contracts may use ..):

aval.lock.yaml
apiVersion: aval.trianalab.io/v1
kind: Test
metadata:
  name: workspace-lock
runner:
  command: ["uv", "lock", "--check"]
scope:
  source: ["pyproject.toml"]
  dependencies: ["uv.lock"]
cacheability: hermetic
packages/api/aval.yaml
apiVersion: aval.trianalab.io/v1
kind: Test
metadata:
  name: api-unit
runner:
  command: ["uv", "run", "pytest", "tests"]
scope:
  source: ["src/**", "tests/**", "pyproject.toml"]
  contracts: ["../../aval.lock.yaml"]
cacheability: hermetic

Any lockfile change reruns every member.

Tool Root files to hash Lockfile check uv pyproject.toml, uv.lock uv lock --check pnpm package.json, pnpm-workspace.yaml, pnpm-lock.yaml pnpm install --frozen-lockfile cargo Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock cargo metadata --locked

A member that imports another member lists that member's sources too, or names its contract.

Also check root config (tsconfig.base.json, .npmrc, conftest.py, pytest.ini, .cargo/config.toml, rust-toolchain.toml, .python-version, .nvmrc), patches, build scripts, shared fixtures and environment variables (environment.env): find undeclared inputs.
