docs.title: Generate scope from the dependency graph
docs.text:
Goal: one test per unit (package, module, project) whose scope is the unit's files plus the files of every unit it depends on. A change to a unit re-runs its test and the tests of the units that depend on it; every other test is reused.

aval gen <language> writes that scope into a kind: TestSet from the repository's real dependency graph. You run it while authoring and commit the result: aval run, verify and push never call it, and the scope stays declared in aval.yaml.

Languages

JavaScript and TypeScript (below) and Rust (below) ship. The other adapters (Go, Python, Java, .NET) are the next stories of Epic 16. aval gen --help lists the languages your build has.

docs.title: What it writes
docs.text:
Given units a and b where a imports b, aval gen go adds:

fragments:
  go.a:
    scope:
      source:
        - a/*.go
  go.b:
    scope:
      source:
        - b/*.go
tests:
  - metadata: {name: go.a}
    runner: {command: [go, test, ./a]}
    use:
      - go.a
      - go.b
  - metadata: {name: go.b}
    runner: {command: [go, test, ./b]}
    use:
      - go.b
  • One fragment per unit with its own files, one test per unit that uses the fragments of the unit and of everything it reaches. Aval computes the closure; a dependency cycle puts every unit on it in each other's tests.
  • Names are <language>.<unit>: the unit lower-cased, / turned into ., other characters outside [a-z0-9._-] into -. A name over 64 characters is cut and ends in a hash of the unit. A name depends on its unit alone, so adding a unit never renames another. Two units that get the same name are an error.
  • Entries are sorted by name, so the output is the same on every run and platform.

docs.title: Ownership
docs.text:
aval gen go owns the fragments and tests named go.* and nothing else:

  • It replaces those entries in place (the first one's position, or the end of fragments and tests) and keeps every other line byte for byte, comments and blank lines included. Comment lines right above a later generated entry go with it, and a missing final newline is added.
  • The prefix is reserved: a hand-written go.* entry is replaced.
  • Two generators share a file: aval gen js owns js.* and leaves go.* alone.
  • fragments and tests must be block style (not {} or []).

Shared inputs stay hand-written. Put lockfiles, root build files, the toolchain, probes, env and cacheability in defaults or in your own fragments; every generated test inherits defaults.

apiVersion: aval.trianalab.io/v1
kind: TestSet
defaults:
  scope:
    dependencies: [go.mod, go.sum]
  environment:
    toolchain: {go: "1.25"}
  cacheability: hermetic
fragments:
  go.web:
    scope:
      source:
        - web/*.go
tests:
  - metadata: {name: e2e}   # hand-written, kept as is
    use: [go.web]           # uses a generated fragment
    runner: {command: [make, e2e]}
  - metadata: {name: go.web}
    runner: {command: [go, test, ./web]}
    use:
      - go.web

A hand-written test can use generated fragments. When the unit behind one disappears, aval gen fails (exit 2) and writes nothing.

docs.title: Keep it up to date in CI
docs.text:
aval gen go --check

--check writes nothing. It exits 0 when the generated entries match the graph, and 1 with a diff when they do not, such as a new import or a dropped one. Run it in the same job as your linters.

docs.title: JavaScript and TypeScript
docs.text:
aval gen js reads the manifests and runs no tool. It makes one unit per workspace package: the workspaces of package.json for npm and yarn, pnpm-workspace.yaml for pnpm (! globs excluded). The root package is not a unit. The lockfile at the contract root picks the package manager and the test command:

Lockfile Command package-lock.json, npm-shrinkwrap.json npm test --workspace <name> pnpm-lock.yaml pnpm --filter <name> test yarn.lock yarn workspace <name> test

A unit's ID is its package name and its files are its directory, so @acme/ui in packages/ui becomes js.acme.ui with packages/ui/**. A dependency becomes an edge when it names another workspace package (any range, or workspace:), or when a file:, link: or portal: path points to one. External packages are not edges: the lockfile in defaults covers them. Exclude node_modules there too.

Two local dependencies that package.json does not name are edges as well:

  • TypeScript configs. Every tsconfig*.json in a package (JSON with comments and trailing commas) adds an edge for each references path that lands in another workspace package. Its extends chain is followed the way TypeScript does (a relative path, a directory meaning its tsconfig.json, .json added when missing, or <workspace package>/<path>): a file in another workspace package is an edge, and a file outside every package, such as a root tsconfig.base.json, joins the unit's own files. extends of an external package is not followed.
  • Relative imports. Every .js, .jsx, .mjs, .cjs, .ts, .tsx, .mts, .cts, .vue, .svelte and .astro file in a package is scanned for relative specifiers (./, ../) of import ... from, export ... from, import "...", import(...) and require(...). One that lands in another workspace package is an edge. Comments are not stripped, so a commented-out import still counts.

The scan skips node_modules, .git and nested workspace packages; hidden directories such as .storybook are scanned. It reads only those references: paths aliases and include globs that reach outside the package are not edges, so declare those by hand.

apiVersion: aval.trianalab.io/v1
kind: TestSet
defaults:
  scope:
    dependencies: [package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, pnpm-workspace.yaml]
    exclude: ["**/node_modules/**"]
  cacheability: hermetic
fragments:
  js.acme.ui:
    scope:
      source:
        - packages/ui/**
  js.acme.utils:
    scope:
      source:
        - packages/utils/**
tests:
  - metadata: {name: js.acme.ui}
    runner: {command: [pnpm, --filter, '@acme/ui', test]}
    use:
      - js.acme.ui
      - js.acme.utils
  - metadata: {name: js.acme.utils}
    runner: {command: [pnpm, --filter, '@acme/utils', test]}
    use:
      - js.acme.utils

No lockfile or lockfiles of two package managers, an unreadable package.json or pnpm-workspace.yaml, no workspaces, a workspace package without a name, and a workspace: or file: reference to something that is not a workspace package are errors: nothing is written, exit 1. So are a relative import that lands outside every workspace package or outside the contract root, or that is computed (a template literal with ${...}), named by file and line; a references path outside every workspace package; and an unreadable tsconfig or a missing, absolute or out-of-root extends. A package without a test script still gets a test; its command fails until you add the script.

docs.title: Rust
docs.text:
aval gen rust reads the Cargo workspace found from the contract root with cargo metadata --no-deps (no network, no build scripts). Each workspace member is a unit named after its package: its scope is the member's directory, its test is cargo test -p <member>, and its path dependencies on other members (normal, dev and build) are its edges. Registry and git dependencies are not units: put the root Cargo.toml (workspace inheritance) and Cargo.lock in defaults.

apiVersion: aval.trianalab.io/v1
kind: TestSet
defaults:
  scope:
    dependencies: [Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock]
  cacheability: hermetic
fragments:
  rust.domain:
    scope:
      source:
        - crates/domain/**
  rust.store:
    scope:
      source:
        - crates/store/**
tests:
  - metadata: {name: rust.domain}
    runner: {command: [cargo, test, -p, domain]}
    use:
      - rust.domain
  - metadata: {name: rust.store}
    runner: {command: [cargo, test, -p, store]}
    use:
      - rust.domain
      - rust.store
  • A path dependency on a crate that is not a workspace member, or a member outside the contract root, is an error: its files would be in no scope.
  • A dev-dependency is an edge like any other, so the tests of a member's dependents use its dev-dependencies too: more re-runs, never a stale reuse.
  • A package at the workspace root gets **: add target/** to defaults.scope.exclude.
  • cargo metadata does not show path overrides, so aval gen reads them from the workspace root: path entries of [patch] tables in Cargo.toml and .cargo/config.toml, and paths in .cargo/config.toml. An override inside a member makes every member depend on that member. One outside every member, or one it cannot read, is an error naming the file. .cargo/config.toml files in parent directories or in CARGO_HOME are not read: keep overrides at the workspace root.

docs.title: Cross-language dependencies
docs.text: A generator sees one ecosystem. Declare a dependency across languages by hand only when no shared file carries it. When a Go binary embeds the frontend build with go:embed, or a client SDK is generated into the tree, those files already sit in a unit's scope. Otherwise add the other side's fragment to a hand-written test's use, or its globs to defaults.

docs.title: Fail closed
docs.text: A missing language tool, a parse error, a dependency on an unknown unit or a unit without files is an error, and nothing is written. Exit codes: 0 written or up to date, 1 error or --check out of date, 2 usage (an unknown language, no kind: TestSet at -f, or a result that is not a valid TestSet).

docs.title: Use GitHub Actions
docs.text:
Goal: each CI job runs its test through Aval in three lines of YAML, and one job on main signs and publishes every result.

flowchart LR
  job([unit job]) --> act[aval run action]
  act -- verified --> skip([reuse]):::ok
  act -- anything else --> test[run the test]
  test -- "push to main" --> art([artifact aval-unit]) --> pub[publish action: aval push] --> reg([registry]):::muted
  act -- "exit 5" --> fail([step fails, SECURITY]):::err

docs.title: The example
docs.text:
A suite job:

  unit:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@<sha> # pin by commit SHA
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: TrianaLab/aval/integrations/github/run@<sha> # pin by commit SHA
        with:
          test: unit

The action integrations/github/run takes test (required), file (default aval.yaml), policy (default .github/aval/policy.yaml), shadow (true adds --shadow), lookup-only (see Skip setup on a hit), min-trust-level (default auto), registry-username and registry-password (default empty: the registry is read anonymously; see Private registry). In order, it:

  1. Refuses pull_request_target and workflow_run, and fails when the job has id-token: write: a suite job can never sign.
  2. Installs the aval release pinned in its action.yml, checked against the per-platform sha256, the release signature and the provenance (Install). Pinning the action by commit SHA pins aval too.
  3. Fetches the policy from the default branch through the contents API with github.token, on every event, never from the checkout. The registry comes from the policy's registry field (Write a trust policy); the job's AVAL_REGISTRY and AVAL_POLICY are ignored; AVAL_MIN_TRUST_LEVEL is not, since it only raises the policy's minimum. With no policy nothing is reused, the test runs and a warning is logged. GH_TOKEN is unset after the fetch, so github.token is not in the test's environment.
  4. Runs aval run -f <file> --test <test> with the CI run URL, the repository and, on a push to the default branch, --outputs-dir. It passes --min-trust-level as the highest of the min-trust-level input, the job's AVAL_MIN_TRUST_LEVEL and the policy's minTrustLevel, never lower than the policy's. Under auto that is runner on the default branch (any event), so main never goes green on a developer result, which aval push would not publish: it is a miss and the test runs. Pull requests and other branches keep the policy's minimum. min-trust-level: developer opts out; a value other than auto, developer, runner or isolated exits 2 before the test runs. The log and step summary show the effective minimum.
  5. Writes the outcome to the step summary and the outcome output. Exit 5 sets the outcome to verification-failed, becomes an aval SECURITY error annotation and fails the step; a miss is routine.
  6. On a push to the default branch only, uploads .aval/<test>/ as the artifact aval-<test>. A re-run of the job replaces the earlier attempt's aval-<test>, so publish signs the result of the attempt that just ran. Run each test in only one job per workflow run: two jobs uploading the same name race.
  7. Warns when the policy trusts a refs/pull/ subject at or above minTrustLevel.

The policy is a separate file on the default branch, so publicKey paths in it are not fetched; use keyless identities. The action needs /usr/bin/jq (GitHub's Ubuntu images, macOS 15 and later). Neither action writes GITHUB_PATH or GITHUB_ENV: the cosign that checks the aval release is pinned by sha256 and installed in $RUNNER_TEMP, off the job's PATH, so the test and later steps see the job's own tools.

Pinned release

Pinning an action by commit SHA pins its aval release too, moved by a PR after each release. Until a pin with --outputs-dir (after 0.8.1, milestone 14), a test with outputs fails with exit 1; others work.

docs.title: Skip setup on a hit
docs.text:
Setup steps (toolchains, caches, browsers) run before the test, also when its result is reused. A lookup-only step lets them be skipped:

  ui:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@<sha> # pin by commit SHA
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: lookup
        uses: TrianaLab/aval/integrations/github/run@<sha> # pin by commit SHA
        with:
          test: ui
          lookup-only: "true"
      - uses: actions/setup-node@<sha> # pin by commit SHA; probed, so never skipped
      - if: steps.lookup.outputs.outcome != 'verified'
        run: npm ci && npx --no playwright install --with-deps
      - uses: TrianaLab/aval/integrations/github/run@<sha> # pin by commit SHA
        with:
          test: ui

With lookup-only: "true" the action does steps 1 to 3 and 7 (same default-branch policy, same trust minimum), then runs aval verify -f <file> --test <test> -o json instead of aval run: it never runs the test, uploads or writes .aval/<test>/. The outcome output is verified, miss, verification-failed or error. A miss (no policy, no attestation, a signer below the minimum) succeeds the step; exit 5 fails it with the aval SECURITY annotation; exits 1 and 2 fail it. A value other than true or false, or shadow: true beside it, exits 2. The final run step stays: it verifies again, restores outputs and gives the job its exit code. The lookup only skips setup, it never decides reuse: if it says verified and the run step then misses (a registry error, a result no longer trusted), the test runs without its setup and fails. The job goes red, never green by mistake. Skip only setup the contract does not probe (dependency installs, caches, browsers): the run step runs every environment.probe before its own lookup, and aval verify runs none, so a skipped toolchain that a probe checks turns a lookup hit into outcome error and a red job.

docs.title: Private registry
docs.text:
A private attestations package (GHCR creates them private) cannot be read anonymously: every lookup is outcome error (not miss, never verification-failed) and the test always runs. Pass registry-username: ${{ github.actor }} and registry-password: ${{ github.token }} to the run action, and set the suite job's permissions to packages: read (with contents: read): github.token has the job's permissions, so that is what makes it read-only. The action then writes the credentials for the host of the default-branch policy's registry only, in a directory of the step under $RUNNER_TEMP that starts from the job's auths (not its credsStore or credHelpers) and is deleted when the step ends. aval reads it through AVAL_DOCKER_CONFIG, which the test never gets: the test keeps the job's DOCKER_CONFIG. No policy, no valid registry, or a pinned aval without AVAL_DOCKER_CONFIG (0.8.2 and older, milestone 15) writes none and warns.

Same job, same user

Neither the token nor AVAL_DOCKER_CONFIG is in the test's environment, but the test runs in the same job as the same user, so a pull request's code can still reach the job's files and processes. Keep the token read-only (packages: read, never packages: write), never pass a write credential, and never give the suite job id-token: write (the action refuses it).

docs.title: Split credentials
docs.text:
One job signs what the suite jobs uploaded, with the workflow's identity:

  publish:
    needs: [unit, ui]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == format('refs/heads/{0}', github.event.repository.default_branch) }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@<sha> # pin by commit SHA
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: TrianaLab/aval/integrations/github/publish@<sha> # pin by commit SHA

The action integrations/github/publish takes file, policy, registry-username, registry-password (default github.actor and github.token), stats and allow-unprotected (both default false) and stats-registry (default empty). In order, it:

  1. Refuses a ref other than the default branch unless allow-unprotected: true, always refuses pull_request_target and workflow_run, and fails without id-token: write.
  2. Downloads this run's aval-* artifacts (so name no other artifact aval-*) into $RUNNER_TEMP. With none, for example when path filters skipped every test job, it prints a notice and exits 0: no install, no policy fetch, no OIDC token, so a publish job on !cancelled() costs seconds and passes before the policy is merged.
  3. Installs the same pinned, verified aval release as the run action.
  4. Fetches the policy from the default branch and logs in to the host of its registry, where results go. No policy or no registry fails the step.
  5. For each aval-<name>, fetches a fresh OIDC token (audience sigstore) and runs aval push --test <name>. It tries them all, then exits with the worst code; 5 is aval SECURITY, never downgraded.
  6. With stats: true, publishes every artifact's run record (hit, miss or verification failure) to stats-registry, or the policy's registry when empty (shared stats); a failure is a warning.

What aval push does with each artifact:

  • An artifact aval-a that holds test b, or a result that does not match the fingerprint push computes from the checkout (environment.env from the artifact's env.txt, as hashed in the suite job), exits 1 and publishes nothing; the other artifacts are still pushed.
  • A reused result (report outcome verified, also under --shadow) and a non-deterministic test print nothing to push: ... and exit 0.
  • A miss or an error publishes the result, failures included: on a tie in trust level a failure outranks a later flaky pass.
  • A report that records a security event signs nothing and exits 5.
  • The artifact holds result.json, report.json, record.json, env.txt and outputs/<path>, the files the outputs globs matched; push publishes those, never the checkout's. No outputs/ for a test with outputs, or a symlink, extra file, input, .git or .aval in it, exits 1, publishing nothing.
  • Trust only this workflow on main: Write a trust policy.

docs.title: Why a composite action
docs.text: The publish action is a composite action, not a reusable workflow: its steps run in the caller's job, so the Fulcio certificate names the calling workflow (https://github.com/acme/app/.github/workflows/ci.yaml@refs/heads/main). A reusable workflow would put Aval's workflow in every caller's certificate, and one subjectRegexp would trust them all. Aval's CI checks this.

docs.title: Pull requests
docs.text: A pull request runs the same suite job and reuses what main published. Its own policy edits change nothing, because the policy comes from the default branch. The workflow file itself still comes from the PR, so a hostile PR can make its own check green; required code-owner review is what protects main (protected branch).

docs.title: Consume from Go
docs.text:
Goal: check an Aval result from your own Go program with pkg/evidence, and tell a miss from a security event.

flowchart LR
  fetch([envelope bytes,<br>fetched by digest]) --> check[Check]
  check -- nil bytes --> miss([ErrNotFound:<br>run the test]):::muted
  check -- ErrVerification --> alert([alert,<br>do not reuse]):::err
  check -- ok --> p([predicate]):::ok

docs.title: The example
docs.text:
go get github.com/TrianaLab/aval@latest

Check from examples/evidence-consumer, a module that imports only pkg/evidence:

// Check returns the verified predicate of a DSSE envelope fetched by digest.
// nil envBytes means the lookup found nothing: evidence.ErrNotFound, a miss.
// Every other failure wraps evidence.ErrVerification, a security event. The
// caller runs the test unless Check returns a passed predicate.
func Check(ctx context.Context, envBytes []byte, opts evidence.VerifyOptions) (*evidence.Predicate, error) {
    if envBytes == nil {
        return nil, evidence.ErrNotFound
    }
    var env evidence.Envelope
    if err := json.Unmarshal(envBytes, &env); err != nil {
        return nil, &evidence.VerificationError{Reason: "decoding envelope: " + err.Error()}
    }
    v, err := evidence.Verify(ctx, &env, opts)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    return v.Predicate, nil
}
Check returns Do a predicate with Result == evidence.ResultPassed reuse it evidence.ErrNotFound a miss: run the test evidence.ErrVerification alert, run the test, do not reuse a predicate with another Result a trusted failure: the test failed

docs.title: What you bring
docs.text:
• Envelope bytes, fetched by digest with any registry client (layout).
  • A SignatureVerifier. pkg/evidence checks the policy, not the cryptography. The example brings ed25519; a Sigstore one is planned for milestone 5.
  • Identities from your own policy, never from the predicate.

Reading aval verify -o json instead? Use evidence.Report, as the example's Reuse does.

docs.title: Integrate Aval in 5 files
docs.text:
Goal: put a monorepo's CI on Aval by adding 2 files and editing at most 3, without touching the Makefile or the scripts.

flowchart LR
  a[aval.yaml<br>added] --> j[suite jobs:<br>aval run action]
  p[.github/aval/policy.yaml<br>added] -- from the default branch --> j
  w[ci.yml<br>edited] --> j
  j -- "push to main" --> pub[publish job:<br>aval publish action] --> reg([registry]):::muted
  g[.gitignore<br>edited]:::muted

The example is examples/github-monorepo: a Go module (cmd/, internal/, pkg/), a Node UI, a Dockerfile, a data directory, an end-to-end suite in 3 shards and one suite that calls an outside service. Aval's tests check that its integration is exactly these files, and run every test through the CLI.

docs.title: 1. Add aval.yaml
docs.text:
One TestSet: defaults for every test, a fragment per part of the repo, and a matrix for the shards. Each test reads only its fragments, so a change to ui/ reruns ui and nothing else:

# Every test CI runs through Aval, and the files each one reads.
# test-external calls a service this repository does not control, so it is
# not here: CI runs it as a plain make job.
apiVersion: aval.trianalab.io/v1
kind: TestSet
defaults:
  scope:
    dependencies: [Makefile]
  cacheability: hermetic
fragments:
  go:
    scope:
      source: ["cmd/**", "internal/**", "pkg/**"]
      dependencies: [go.mod]
    environment:
      toolchain: {go: "1.25"}
      env: [GOFLAGS, CGO_ENABLED]
  ui:
    scope:
      source: ["ui/src/**", "ui/test/**"]
      dependencies: [ui/package.json, ui/package-lock.json]
    environment:
      toolchain: {node: "24"}
  image:
    scope:
      source: [Dockerfile, "data/**"]
      allowMutable:
        - files: ["data/fixtures/*.yaml"]
          ref: ghcr.io/stefanprodan/podinfo:6.5.0
          reason: public demo workload; the e2e suite only starts it
tests:
  - metadata: {name: unit}
    use: [go]
    runner: {command: [make, test]}
    outputs: [coverage.out]
  - metadata: {name: ui}
    use: [ui]
    runner: {command: [make, ui]}
  - metadata: {name: "e2e-{shard}"}
    use: [go, image]
    runner: {command: [make, e2e, "SHARD={shard}"]}
    scope: {source: ["e2e/**"]}
    matrix: {shard: ["1", "2", "3"]}
    cacheability: controlled-environment
  • allowMutable[].files accepts the one tag the data fixtures share, in those files only. The same tag anywhere else blocks reuse.
  • outputs restores coverage.out when unit is reused.
  • Check every test without running anything: aval explain --all.

Leave out what must always run: a non-deterministic test is never reused, and an external-dependencies test only when the policy lists it in allowedCacheability (Trust model). Here test-external stays a plain make job.

docs.title: 2. Add the trust policy
docs.text:
One runner identity, this workflow on main, and the registry results go to:

# The trust policy. The run and publish actions read it from the default
# branch only, so a pull request that edits it changes nothing.
apiVersion: aval.trianalab.io/v1
kind: Policy
registry: ghcr.io/acme/monorepo-aval
minTrustLevel: runner
identities:
  - issuer: https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com
    subjectRegexp: https://github\.com/acme/monorepo/\.github/workflows/ci\.yml@refs/heads/main
    trustLevel: runner

docs.title: 3. Edit the workflow
docs.text:
In each suite job, the make step becomes the run action:

      - uses: TrianaLab/aval/integrations/github/run@c352441f0c0c06f2b7497b235e4b9c27599100ee # v0.9.1
        with:
          test: unit

A matrix job names its shard, so each shard is its own test and artifact:

      - uses: TrianaLab/aval/integrations/github/run@c352441f0c0c06f2b7497b235e4b9c27599100ee # v0.9.1
        with:
          test: e2e-${{ matrix.shard }}

Add one publish job:

  publish:
    needs: [unit, ui, e2e]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == format('refs/heads/{0}', github.event.repository.default_branch) }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: TrianaLab/aval/integrations/github/publish@c352441f0c0c06f2b7497b235e4b9c27599100ee # v0.9.1

docs.title: 4. Ignore .aval/
docs.text:
Add .aval/ to .gitignore: each test writes its result there. Optionally, say in CONTRIBUTING.md that CI reuses results.

Each action installs the aval release its commit pins. The example pins the commit that pins the latest release.

The run action's artifact carries coverage.out, the output of unit, and the publish job pushes it from there, not from its own checkout (the artifact).

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: Pinning is project work, not part of these files: base images by digest, lockfiles in scope.dependencies, tools at fixed versions. Until then Aval reports each mutable reference and reuses nothing for that test (Pin your dependencies).

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Require code-owner review of .github/workflows/ and .github/aval/: a pull request controls its own workflow file.
  • Trust refs/heads/main only. A runner-level identity for refs/pull/ lets any pull request sign results that are reused.
  • Publish only on a push to the default branch, from a job that runs no tests.
  • The publish action is a composite action, not a reusable workflow, so the certificate names your workflow (Why a composite action).

docs.title: Other CI systems
docs.text:
A wrapper for another CI system has the same duties as the two actions:

  • Install a pinned aval release and verify it (sha256, signature).
  • Read the policy from the protected branch, never from the checkout.
  • Give suite jobs no signing credentials; sign in a separate job.
  • Never swallow exit 5: fail the job and show the security event.
  • Keep one artifact per test (.aval/<test>/), named after the test.
  • Publish only on protected refs, with that job's own identity.

docs.title: Measure reuse
docs.text:
Goal: find out how often Aval would reuse a result, and whether reuse would have been right, before you let it skip any test.

flowchart LR
  run([aval run --shadow]) --> v[verify] --> t[run the test anyway]
  t --> same{same result?}
  same -- yes --> ok([reuse would be correct]):::ok
  same -- no --> fh([FALSE HIT, exit 1]):::err

docs.title: Estimate from history
docs.text:
scripts/estimate-reuse.sh fingerprints past commits and counts repeats as hits:

scripts/estimate-reuse.sh services/orders/aval.yaml --max-count=200 main

<commit> miss sha256:4800...
<commit> hit sha256:4800...
200 commits, 61 would reuse a result (30%, an upper bound)

An upper bound: it ignores branches, failing tests and trust policy.

docs.title: Measure in shadow mode
docs.text:
Verify, run the test anyway, compare, and record the run. With AVAL_REGISTRY and AVAL_POLICY set (or --registry/--policy):

aval run --shadow --stats
You see It means shadow: reuse of <ref> would have been correct safe to turn shadow off for this test aval: FALSE HIT: ... (exit 1) the contract misses an input: fix scope

No write access in the test job? Write the record to a file and publish it from another job:

aval run --stats-file record.json --source-repo acme/orders
aval stats publish --registry ghcr.io/acme/aval-stats record.json

docs.title: Read the numbers
docs.text:
aval stats --registry ghcr.io/acme/aval-stats --since 7d

It sums hits, misses by cause, verification failures, shadow false hits and time saved, per test:

run records in ghcr.io/acme/aval-stats since 2026-10-31T12:30:00Z
orders-unit: 1 runs, 1 reused (hit rate 100.0%), test time 0s, saved 1m30s
  not reused: 0 no trusted result, 0 error, 0 verified but run (shadow)
  verification failures: 0, shadow false hits: 0
total: 1 runs, 1 reused (hit rate 100.0%), test time 0s, saved 1m30s
  not reused: 0 no trusted result, 0 error, 0 verified but run (shadow)
  verification failures: 0, shadow false hits: 0
  • --test limits it to one test, --by repository groups by --source-repo, -o json prints the stats report.
  • Records are unsigned statistics. aval run and aval verify never read them, so a forged record cannot cause reuse.
  • A record that cannot be published only warns; the exit code stays. Fields: run records.

docs.title: Shards and matrices
docs.text:
Goal: one result and one fingerprint per CI shard, each bound only to what that shard reads.

flowchart LR
  m([matrix]) --> s1[shard 1: aval run -f aval.shard-1.yaml] --> r1([result 1]):::muted
  m --> s2[shard 2: aval run -f aval.shard-2.yaml] --> r2([result 2]):::muted
  c[change under packages/app] -. reruns .-> s2

Patterns A and B need no new field: -f, scope and environment.env do it. Pattern C uses a TestSet matrix. Example: examples/uv-monorepo.

docs.title: Pattern A: one contract per shard
docs.text:
Best reuse. Each shard has its own contract, side by side at the root:

# Shard 1 of 2: the core package's tests. It lives at the workspace root,
# beside aval.shard-2.yaml, because globs cannot leave the contract's
# directory and the uv workspace files are here. Run with
# `aval run -f aval.shard-1.yaml`.
apiVersion: aval.trianalab.io/v1
kind: Test
metadata:
  name: uv-monorepo-core
runner:
  command: ["uv", "run", "--locked", "--package", "core", "pytest", "packages/core", "--cov=core", "--cov-report=xml:coverage-shard-1.xml"]
scope:
  source: ["packages/core/**/*.py"]
  # uv checks the lock against every member's pyproject.toml.
  dependencies: [pyproject.toml, "packages/*/pyproject.toml", uv.lock, .python-version]
environment:
  toolchain: {python: "3.12", uv: "0.9.18"}
cacheability: hermetic
outputs: [coverage-shard-1.xml]

Shard 2 tests app, which imports core, so core is in its scope:

# Shard 2 of 2: the app package's tests. app imports core, so core's code is
# in scope here too; app's files are not in shard 1's scope.
apiVersion: aval.trianalab.io/v1
kind: Test
metadata:
  name: uv-monorepo-app
runner:
  command: ["uv", "run", "--locked", "--package", "app", "pytest", "packages/app", "--cov=app", "--cov-report=xml:coverage-shard-2.xml"]
scope:
  source: ["packages/app/**/*.py", "packages/core/src/**/*.py"]
  dependencies: [pyproject.toml, "packages/*/pyproject.toml", uv.lock, .python-version]
environment:
  toolchain: {python: "3.12", uv: "0.9.18"}
cacheability: hermetic
outputs: [coverage-shard-2.xml]

A change under packages/app reruns shard 2 only. A change to core or uv.lock reruns both.

docs.title: Pattern B: one contract, shard variables
docs.text:
Simpler, less reuse: a change anywhere reruns every shard.

# One contract for every shard of examples/uv-monorepo. Each matrix job sets
# SHARD_INDEX and SHARD_TOTAL, so each shard gets its own fingerprint over
# the whole suite's scope. Splitting by index needs a pytest plugin such as
# pytest-shard, which the example does not lock. pytest-shard counts
# SHARD_INDEX from 0: set it to `${{ strategy.job-index }}` and SHARD_TOTAL
# to `${{ strategy.job-total }}`.
apiVersion: aval.trianalab.io/v1
kind: Test
metadata:
  name: uv-monorepo-tests
runner:
  command: ["sh", "-c", "uv run --locked --all-packages pytest packages --shard-id=$SHARD_INDEX --num-shards=$SHARD_TOTAL"]
scope:
  source: ["packages/**/*.py"]
  dependencies: [pyproject.toml, "packages/*/pyproject.toml", uv.lock, .python-version]
environment:
  toolchain: {python: "3.12", uv: "0.9.18"}
  # Leave one out and every shard shares one fingerprint: a false hit.
  env: [SHARD_INDEX, SHARD_TOTAL]
cacheability: hermetic

Declare both variables

Leave SHARD_INDEX or SHARD_TOTAL out of environment.env and shards share a fingerprint: shard 2 reuses shard 1's result, a false hit.

docs.title: Pattern C: one TestSet, a matrix
docs.text:
One file, and each shard is its own test: matrix writes the shard into runner.command, so it is part of the fingerprinted argv and no variable can drift between the job that runs a shard and the job that pushes it. Reuse is the same as pattern B, since the shards share one scope. Rules: Many tests in one file.

# Every shard of examples/uv-monorepo in one TestSet. The matrix writes the
# shard into runner.command, so each shard has its own fingerprint and no
# variable can drift between the job that runs it and the one that pushes.
apiVersion: aval.trianalab.io/v1
kind: TestSet
defaults:
  scope:
    source: ["packages/**/*.py"]
    dependencies: [pyproject.toml, "packages/*/pyproject.toml", uv.lock, .python-version]
  environment:
    toolchain: {python: "3.12", uv: "0.9.18"}
  cacheability: hermetic
tests:
  - metadata: {name: "uv-monorepo-shard-{index}"}
    runner:
      command: [uv, run, --locked, --all-packages, pytest, packages, "--shard-id={index}", --num-shards=2]
    matrix: {index: ["0", "1"]}

Run one shard by its name; its result goes to .aval/<name>/, so shards never overwrite each other's outputs:

aval run --test uv-monorepo-shard-0

aval explain --all checks every shard and prints its fingerprint (Select a test).

For a runner that counts shards from 1, matrix: {shard: {count: 3}} with {shard}/{shard_count} in the command states the total once, so the shard list and the total cannot disagree.

docs.title: One test per platform
docs.text:
matrix also substitutes into environment.toolchain values, so each platform is its own test with its own fingerprint:

# One test per platform. The matrix writes the platform into the toolchain,
# so each leg has its own fingerprint: unit-darwin never reuses unit-linux.
# The probe records a leg's result only on the platform it declares.
apiVersion: aval.trianalab.io/v1
kind: TestSet
defaults:
  scope:
    source: ["**/*.go"]
    dependencies: [go.mod]
  cacheability: hermetic
tests:
  - metadata: {name: "unit-{os}"}
    runner: {command: [go, test, ./...]}
    matrix: {os: [linux, darwin]}
    environment:
      toolchain: {platform: "{os}"}
      probe: {platform: [go, env, GOOS]}

unit-darwin never reuses a result of unit-linux. Run the leg of the machine you are on: the probe of the other leg does not match, so its result is not recorded. To reuse across platforms, do not declare platform.

docs.title: The matrix
docs.text:
One job per shard, each with its own --result-file and coverage outputs:

# A two-shard matrix for this example as its own repository: copy it to
# .github/workflows/ and set REPO and POLICY. Each job runs one shard
# contract with its own --result; on main, reuses a verified result or runs
# the shard; for pull requests read POLICY and REPO from the default branch
# (docs/trust-model.md#take-the-policy-from-a-protected-branch). It uploads that shard's coverage, restored on reuse. Publishing
# needs the push step from Aval's "Use GitHub Actions" guide.
name: tests
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        shard: [1, 2]
    env:
      REPO: ghcr.io/acme/uv-monorepo-aval
      POLICY: .github/aval/policy.yaml
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
        with:
          version: "0.9.18"
          enable-cache: false
      - run: curl -fsSL https://aval.run/install.sh | bash -s -- --version v0.5.0
      - run: >-
          aval run -f aval.shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.yaml
          --result .aval/shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          --registry "$REPO" --policy "$POLICY"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

The same job locally, with AVAL_REGISTRY and AVAL_POLICY exported as in the workflow:

aval run -f aval.shard-2.yaml --result-file .aval/shard-2.json

To publish, add the push step from Use GitHub Actions.

docs.title: Sign results
docs.text:
Goal: sign a test result so that others can check who published it.

flowchart LR
  run([aval run]) --> result[.aval/result.json] --> push[aval push]
  push -- key file --> keyed([key]):::muted
  push -- OIDC token --> keyless([keyless]):::ok

docs.title: The example
docs.text:
KeyKeyless

Make a P-256 key and a policy that trusts it (aval init --key aval.key does both for a new project):

aval keygen
cat > policy.yaml <<'EOF'
apiVersion: aval.trianalab.io/v1
kind: Policy
minTrustLevel: developer
identities:
  - publicKey: aval.pub
    trustLevel: developer
EOF
aval run --push --key aval.key --registry ghcr.io/acme/orders-aval

Put an OIDC token in $SIGSTORE_ID_TOKEN and leave out --key. GitHub Actions gets one itself (Use GitHub Actions):

export SIGSTORE_ID_TOKEN="<OIDC token for audience sigstore>"
aval run --push --registry ghcr.io/acme/orders-aval

On a laptop with a terminal, leave out the token too: Aval opens the Sigstore login in the browser and signs with that identity, such as your GitHub email. The token is used once, never stored. Give such an identity developer.

The identity is your verified GitHub email, issuer https://github.com/login/oauth. In CI set $SIGSTORE_ID_TOKEN or use --key: a terminal without a browser prints the login URL and waits for a pasted code.

docs.title: Which one
docs.text:
Key Keyless Who signs whoever holds the key file a CI job or a person, proven by OIDC Policy entry publicKey: aval.pub issuer and subjectRegexp Usual trust level developer runner Network to verify no yes, unless the policy pins trustedRoot
  • Keys: unencrypted ECDSA P-256 in PEM (PKCS#8 or SEC1). Cosign keys are encrypted and do not work.
  • aval push signs later the result aval run saved in .aval/result.json. It refuses a result whose inputs changed. With --report-file it publishes nothing after a run that reused a verified result: split credentials.
  • --login asks for the browser login without a terminal. $SIGSTORE_OIDC_ISSUER and $SIGSTORE_OIDC_CLIENT_ID override the defaults (oauth2.sigstore.dev, client sigstore).

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Goal: go from an exit code or an error message to its cause and its fix. Text in <...> changes per run.

flowchart LR
  code{exit code} -- 2 --> u([Flags and files]):::warn
  code -- 1 --> e([Errors]):::warn
  code -- 4 --> m([Misses]):::muted
  code -- 5 --> s([Verification failures]):::err

docs.title: Start with the exit code
docs.text:
Code aval run aval verify aval push 0 the test passed, or a verified passing result was reused a verified result exists (passing or failing) and no attestation failed verification pushed 1 error (the test still runs when it can), or a false hit in --shadow error: registry, policy, trusted root or fingerprint error: signing, registry or a result that does not match the current inputs 2 bad flags or invalid aval.yaml bad flags or invalid aval.yaml bad flags or invalid aval.yaml 3 the test failed, or a verified failing result was reused not used not used 4 not used: a miss runs the test miss: no result the policy can reuse not used 5 verification failed, after running the test: a security event, also beside a verified result (never reused then) or over the 64-attestation cap; wins over 3 and 1 verification failed: a security event, also beside a verified result (the report keeps outcome verified) or over the 64-attestation cap not used 6 reserved, never returned reserved, never returned reserved, never returned

docs.title: Write a trust policy
docs.text:
Goal: a policy.yaml that says whose results you reuse, and nobody else's.

flowchart LR
  p([policy.yaml]) --> id["identities:<br>issuer + subjectRegexp,<br>or publicKey"] --> tl[trustLevel] --> min{"≥ minTrustLevel?"}
  min -- yes --> ok([reuse]):::ok
  min -- no --> m([miss]):::muted

docs.title: The example
docs.text:
Trust one GitHub Actions workflow on main (the policy of Aval's example-go-compose job):

# Trust policy for the GitHub Actions demo (the example-go-compose job in
# .github/workflows/ci.yaml): reuse only results signed keyless by that
# workflow on main. Anything else that sits under the fingerprint, such as a
# result signed with some key, is a verification failure (exit 5).
apiVersion: aval.trianalab.io/v1
kind: Policy
minTrustLevel: runner
identities:
  - issuer: https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com
    subjectRegexp: https://github\.com/TrianaLab/aval/\.github/workflows/ci\.yaml@refs/heads/main
    trustLevel: runner

For a key: Sign results. Pass it with --policy, or set AVAL_POLICY once (the flag wins):

aval verify --registry ghcr.io/acme/orders-aval --policy policy.yaml

To skip --registry, add registry: ghcr.io/acme/orders-aval to the policy. The flag and AVAL_REGISTRY still win, and the config: line says which one was used. Never put user:password@ in it: logins come from docker login.

docs.title: One policy for PRs and main
docs.text:
A policy that also trusts developer keys sets minTrustLevel: developer, so PRs reuse them. On main, raise the minimum for that run only:

aval run --policy policy.yaml --min-trust-level runner

AVAL_MIN_TRUST_LEVEL=runner does the same (the flag wins). Both work on aval run and aval verify and can only raise the policy's minimum: a lower or unknown level exits 2. A developer result is then a miss (exit 4), never exit 5. A policy that trusts only main's CI identity does not need this. The GitHub run action does it by default on the default branch; min-trust-level: developer opts out.

docs.title: The fields
docs.text: Field Meaning identities the signers you accept: each is an OIDC issuer plus a subjectRegexp matched against the whole certificate subject, or a publicKey PEM file. At least one. trustLevel the level an identity gets: developer, runner or isolated. minTrustLevel the lowest level a result needs to be reused. --min-trust-level or AVAL_MIN_TRUST_LEVEL on run and verify can raise it for one run, never lower it (a lower or unknown level exits 2). allowedCacheability classes reused besides hermetic and controlled-environment; only external-dependencies has an effect, and non-deterministic is rejected. trustedRoot a pinned Sigstore trusted root for keyless signatures; without it, the public-good root is fetched. registry optional: the OCI repository of attestations (host/name), used by aval run and aval verify when neither --registry nor AVAL_REGISTRY is set. No credentials: a value with user:password@ (or any @) exits 2. Logins come from the credential store.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Read the policy from a protected branch in CI, never from the PR's checkout (why): its identities and its registry decide what is trusted.
  • Anchor the subject to one workflow file and one branch. A PR branch runs any code: never trust it as runner.
  • Give developer keys developer. Keep minTrustLevel: runner in CI, so CI never reuses laptop results.
  • subjectRegexp must match the whole subject. Escape dots: github\.com.
  • Keyless checks fetch the Sigstore root on first use and cache it under $HOME/.sigstore; offline the test runs. Pin trustedRoot to avoid it (details).

docs.title: Write a contract
docs.text:
Goal: an aval.yaml that lists every input of your test, so a result is reused only when none of them changed.

flowchart LR
  c([aval.yaml]) --> s[scope] --> fp[fingerprint] --> d{reuse?}
  c --> k[cacheability] --> d

docs.title: The example
docs.text:
A Go test against Redis from Docker Compose, examples/go-compose/aval.yaml:

apiVersion: aval.trianalab.io/v1
kind: Test
metadata:
  name: counter-integration
runner:
  command: ["sh", "-c", "docker compose up -d --wait && REDIS_ADDR=localhost:16379 go test -tags=integration -count=1 ./...; rc=$?; docker compose down; exit $rc"]
scope:
  source: ["**/*.go", "compose.yaml"]
  dependencies: [go.mod]
environment:
  toolchain: {go: "1.25"}
cacheability: controlled-environment

aval init writes a first one (Quickstart). For a project that will hold many tests, aval init --set starts from two files instead: aval.yaml as a kind: TestSet with your test and a sources fragment for the globs, and .github/aval/policy.yaml with one placeholder keyless identity:

aval init --set --name unit --source 'src/**' --cacheability hermetic -- go test ./...

The identity's subjectRegexp names <OWNER>/<REPO>, so it trusts no signer until you replace it with your CI's (Trust policy). aval explain --all checks the set.

docs.title: Step by step
docs.text:
1. Name the test. metadata.name says what is checked. It does not change when inputs do.
  2. Say how to run it. runner.command is an argv list. No shell unless you call one.
  3. List the inputs. scope.source for files the test reads, scope.dependencies for manifests and lockfiles. Globs are relative to the contract; ** is any depth. A glob that matches nothing means no fingerprint: the test always runs (exclude globs may match nothing).
  4. Pick a cacheability class. How safe reuse is. Tags and ranges block reuse for hermetic and controlled-environment: pin them.
Class Use it when Reused hermetic the test reads only the declared files yes controlled-environment it uses services you pin, such as a Compose image by digest yes external-dependencies it calls something you do not control only if the policy allows it non-deterministic the same inputs can give a different result never

docs.title: Check the scope
docs.text:
aval explain

It prints one line per input: kind, sha256, x if executable, path. Not listed means not hashed.

docs.title: Restore coverage and reports on reuse
docs.text:
A reused result writes no coverage file. List the files later steps read under outputs, e.g. outputs: [coverage.xml, junit.xml]:

  • aval run --push and aval push publish them, signed. aval push reads them from disk: push right after aval run.
  • aval run writes them back after a result verifies. aval verify writes nothing.

Outputs are published

Anyone who can read the registry can read them. On reuse Aval writes any file a trusted signer published under the globs, except the contract and its inputs. List no secrets and keep the globs narrow: ** can overwrite files later steps read. Caps: outputs.

docs.title: Find undeclared inputs
docs.text:
A file the test reads but scope misses is a false hit waiting to happen. On Linux, compare what the test opens with aval explain:

strace -f -e trace=openat -o trace.txt pytest tests/unit
grep -v ENOENT trace.txt | grep -o '"[^"]*"' | tr -d '"' | sed "s|^$PWD/||" \
  | grep -v '^/' | sort -u > read.txt
aval explain | awk '$1 == "source" || $1 == "dependency"' \
  | cut -d' ' -f4- | sort -u > scope.txt
comm -23 read.txt scope.txt   # prints tests/conftest.py

Read the list, do not paste it: some lines are caches. On macOS use sudo fs_usage -w -f pathname <process>, on Windows Process Monitor. Anywhere: copy only the scope to an empty directory and run the test there.

docs.title: Resolve references
docs.text:
The fingerprint hashes the text of your files. postgres:16 is hashed as the words postgres:16, not as the image behind them. Pinning fixes that by writing the immutable id into a file: a digest, a lockfile, a commit. When you cannot or do not want to pin, declare the reference in scope.resolve: Aval looks up what the name points to every time it fingerprints, and hashes that id.

apiVersion: aval.trianalab.io/v1
kind: Test
metadata:
  name: orders-integration
runner:
  command: ["docker", "compose", "run", "--rm", "tests"]
scope:
  source: ["**/*.go", "compose.yaml"]
  resolve:
    - image: postgres:16
    - npm: prettier@^3
    - git: https://github.com/acme/fixtures@main
cacheability: controlled-environment

When someone repushes postgres:16, publishes any new prettier release or moves main, the id changes, the fingerprint changes, and Aval runs the test instead of reusing an old result.

docs.title: Exact or floating
docs.text:
For npm, PyPI, crates, gems and Maven, an exact version binds that release. Anything else (a range, latest, a tag) binds the whole release list, so any new release runs the test again. Aval never picks a version from a range.

Kind Exact Floating hashes npm x.y.z[-pre] every version's dist.integrity and deprecation, every dist-tag pypi one == without * every file's sha256 and yanked flag crate =x.y.z every index entry's checksum and yanked flag gem a plain version every version and platform checksum maven a plain version every listed version's POM and checksums (100 versions at most) go vX.Y.Z (a branch or commit resolves to a version) the version list, plus @latest and its h1: hash, for latest, a prefix, a comparison or +incompatible image the tag's manifest digest git a full commit the commit a branch or tag points to url the bytes

A publish, a yank or a moved tag changes the id: the test runs more often, never on stale inputs. When in doubt, a spec is floating. A spec the tool installs from elsewhere (npm:x, github:, file:, ./dir) or a name outside the ecosystem's rules fails: use git or url, or pin. Each page lists the rules.

docs.title: Pin or resolve?
docs.text:
Pin (digest, lockfile, commit) Resolve (scope.resolve) Works offline; the fingerprint needs no network. Needs the registry every time Aval fingerprints. You update the pin by hand or with a bot. You follow a tag or a branch on purpose; a range follows every release. What you run is what you hashed. The id is read when Aval fingerprints; a push between that and your test's own download is not seen.

Prefer pinning. Use scope.resolve for references you mean to follow: a nightly base image, a tool at latest, a fixtures branch.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• The manifest gets one line per reference, after the env lines: resolve <kind> <reference> <version> <id>, where <version> is floating for a reference that names no exact version. aval run --explain shows them, and prints on stderr how long each lookup took, including those of the contracts in scope.contracts.
  • The list is part of the contract hash; its order and duplicates do not matter. Contracts without scope.resolve never touch the network.
  • scope.resolve binds the artifact you name, not its dependencies. npm, pip, cargo install without --locked and gem install still pick transitive versions when they install. Pin those with a lockfile.
  • No cache: every fingerprint asks the registry again.

docs.title: scope.resolve and the scanner
docs.text: scope.resolve never clears a scanner finding: a move changes the fingerprint, but the reference still blocks reuse. Pin it in place, or accept it with scope.allowMutable.

docs.title: When resolution fails
docs.text: A reference that cannot be resolved (network, credentials, an exact version that is not published, a listed version without a checksum, a download over 256 MiB, the 2-minute deadline) fails the fingerprint. Nothing is looked up, the test runs, and the reason names the reference: fingerprint: resolve npm left@9.9.9: version 9.9.9 is not published. aval verify exits 1; aval run --push runs the test and publishes nothing.

docs.title: Registries and credentials
docs.text:
Kind Registry (default) Credentials image the host in the reference (Docker Hub) Docker config (docker login) npm $npm_config_registry (registry.npmjs.org) //host/:_authToken= in ~/.npmrc, else ~/.netrc pypi $AVAL_PYPI_URL (pypi.org, JSON API) ~/.netrc go first proxy in $GOPROXY (proxy.golang.org) ~/.netrc maven $AVAL_MAVEN_URL (repo.maven.apache.org/maven2) ~/.netrc crate $AVAL_CRATES_INDEX (index.crates.io, sparse) ~/.netrc gem $AVAL_RUBYGEMS_URL (rubygems.org) ~/.netrc git the URL in the reference git's own (credential helpers, SSH keys) url the URL in the reference ~/.netrc
  • Only machine entries of ~/.netrc (or $NETRC) are used, never default, and only over https or to a loopback host (also after a redirect). $npm_config_userconfig (any letter case) points npm's file elsewhere. Credentials go in headers, never in the manifest, a URL or an error; a user, password or path in a registry variable is masked in errors and refused over plain http to a host that is not loopback.
  • A reference with credentials is rejected without echoing it: a password in any URL, a user in an http(s) or scheme-less //user@host URL (an ssh://git@host user is fine), an @ in the authority of a URL that does not parse, or a query parameter named token, private_token, access_token, key, apikey, api_key, sig, signature, X-Amz-Signature, X-Goog-Signature, auth, password, secret, credential, security_token, x_amz_security_token, client_secret, session or sessionid (any case, - read as _, a trailing [] ignored).
  • The registry address is not hashed: the same content on a mirror resolves to the same id. Requests carry the User-Agent aval/<version> (+https://github.com/TrianaLab/aval).

The resolved id vouches for the registry in the table, not for the one the tool installs from. Where the tool's own setting points elsewhere, resolution fails:

Kind Fails when npm ~/.npmrc has a @scope:registry or registry line, or an npm_config_@scope:registry variable is set, that differs from Aval's registry; two spellings of an npm_config_* variable differ; a ~/.npmrc line cannot be read go $GOPROXY starts with direct or off; $GOPRIVATE or $GONOPROXY matches; GOSUMDB=off, $GONOSUMDB, $GOINSECURE or -insecure in $GOFLAGS pypi $PIP_INDEX_URL or $PIP_PYPI_URL names another index; $PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL or $PIP_FIND_LINKS is set; $PIP_NO_INDEX is true (any spelling pip reads); two spellings of one PIP_* variable (the option in any case, - equal to _, an optional leading --; on Windows PIP_ in any case) differ maven <latest> or <release> is a SNAPSHOT or not listed

Not read: pip.conf, a project .npmrc, go env -w settings, Cargo's config.toml, Maven's settings.xml, .gemrc. If one of them points the tool to another registry, set the Aval variable to the same registry.

docs.title: Rust crates
docs.text:
crate: <name>@=<version> hashes the .crate checksum of that version from the crates.io index.

For npm, PyPI, crates, gems and Maven, an exact version binds that release. Anything else (a range, latest, a tag) binds the whole release list, so any new release runs the test again. Aval never picks a version from a range.

scope:
  resolve:
    - crate: cargo-nextest@=0.9.81   # exact
    - crate: serde@1                 # floating (Cargo reads it as ^1)
    - crate: tokio                   # floating
  • Exact means Cargo's =x.y.z; a bare 1.2.3 means ^1.2.3, so it is floating. A yanked version is not resolved: Cargo does not pick it either.
  • The name is a crates.io name (a letter, then up to 63 letters, digits, _ or -). A spec with :, / or #, or starting with . or ~/, fails: use git or url, or pin.
  • Floating: every index entry with its checksum and yanked flag.
  • Index $AVAL_CRATES_INDEX (sparse protocol); credentials from ~/.netrc.

Pin instead for your crate's dependencies: commit Cargo.lock and add it to scope.dependencies. Resolve is for cargo install tool in runner.command. Only the crate is bound: without --locked, cargo install picks new versions of its dependencies.

scope.resolve never clears a scanner finding: a move changes the fingerprint, but the reference still blocks reuse. Pin it in place, or accept it with scope.allowMutable.

docs.title: Ruby gems
docs.text:
gem: <name>@<version> hashes the checksums of all platform gems of that version.

For npm, PyPI, crates, gems and Maven, an exact version binds that release. Anything else (a range, latest, a tag) binds the whole release list, so any new release runs the test again. Aval never picks a version from a range.

scope:
  resolve:
    - gem: rubocop@1.66.1   # exact
    - gem: rails@~>7.1      # floating
    - gem: bundler          # floating
  • Exact means a plain version (7.1.3, 7.2.0.beta1) with no operator. It binds every number RubyGems holds equal to it (7.1.3.0 too).
  • The name is a RubyGems name (a letter or digit, then letters, digits, ., _ or -). A spec with :, / or #, starting with . or ~/, or a name ending in .gem fails: use git or url, or pin.
  • gem install also reads a matching <name>-<version>.gem file in the current directory, which Aval does not see: run it where no such file lies.
  • Floating: every version, platform and checksum.
  • Registry $AVAL_RUBYGEMS_URL; credentials from ~/.netrc.

Pin instead for your application's gems: commit Gemfile.lock and add it to scope.dependencies. Resolve is for gem install tool in runner.command. Only the gem is bound, not the dependencies gem install picks.

scope.resolve never clears a scanner finding: a move changes the fingerprint, but the reference still blocks reuse. Pin it in place, or accept it with scope.allowMutable.

docs.title: Git references
docs.text:
git: <url>@<ref> asks the remote, with git ls-remote, which commit a branch or tag points to, and hashes the commit id.

scope:
  resolve:
    - git: https://github.com/acme/fixtures@main
    - git: https://github.com/acme/fixtures@v1.4.0   # an annotated tag: its commit
    - git: ssh://git@github.com/acme/private@refs/heads/release
  • The ref is a branch, a tag, HEAD or a full ref name. A name that is both a branch and a tag fails: write refs/heads/<name> or refs/tags/<name>. A full commit id resolves to itself, unless a branch or tag has that exact name, which fails.
  • URLs: https, http, ssh, git or file, with a scheme (ssh://git@host/repo, not git@host:repo).
  • Needs git on the PATH. Credentials come from git itself: credential helpers, SSH keys. Git never prompts.

scope.resolve never clears a scanner finding: a move changes the fingerprint, but the reference still blocks reuse. Pin it in place, or accept it with scope.allowMutable.

The entry hashes the commit, so a moved branch changes the fingerprint.

Pin instead with a commit: git clone URL && git -C dir checkout <40-hex>, or a submodule. Resolve is for a branch you mean to follow, such as shared test fixtures.

docs.title: Go modules
docs.text:
go: <module>@<query> hashes the module zip the way go.sum does (h1:). What a query binds depends on its form, as the go command reads it:

Query Binds vX.Y.Z, optional -pre (pseudo-versions too) that version's zip (exact) a branch, a commit or another non-semver query (main, 4f3c2a1) the zip of the version the proxy resolves it to, usually a pseudo-version; the manifest line names it latest (or no query), a prefix (v1.2), a comparison (<v1.3.0), +incompatible the proxy's version list, its @latest and that version's h1: hash (floating) 
scope:
  resolve:
    - go: golang.org/x/tools@v0.26.0   # exact: binds v0.26.0
    - go: github.com/acme/lib@main     # a branch: binds its current commit
    - go: golang.org/x/net@latest      # floating: binds the version list
  • For a floating query, other versions are bound by name: the checksum database keeps every version the go command accepts fixed.
  • The module path must pass golang.org/x/mod's module.CheckPath, and names the module, not a package inside it.
  • Proxy: the first entry of $GOPROXY (https://proxy.golang.org); credentials from ~/.netrc.
  • Fails when the go command would bypass the proxy or the checksum database: $GOPROXY starting with direct or off, $GOPRIVATE or $GONOPROXY matching, GOSUMDB=off, $GONOSUMDB or $GOINSECURE matching, or -insecure in $GOFLAGS. go env -w settings are not read. Aval never clones: pin the module or use git.

Pin instead for your module's dependencies: commit go.sum and add it to scope.dependencies. Resolve is for go install tool@v1.2.3 in runner.command.

scope.resolve never clears a scanner finding: a move changes the fingerprint, but the reference still blocks reuse. Pin it in place, or accept it with scope.allowMutable.

docs.title: Container images
docs.text:
image: <name>:<tag> resolves the tag to the digest of its manifest. For a multi-arch image that is the digest of the index, so a new build for any platform changes it.

scope:
  source: ["compose.yaml", "**/*.go"]
  resolve:
    - image: postgres:16                     # Docker Hub
    - image: ghcr.io/acme/orders-db:nightly  # any OCI registry
  • A name without a host is a Docker Hub name: postgres:16 is docker.io/library/postgres:16, and so are docker.io/postgres:16 and index.docker.io/postgres:16. No tag means latest.
  • The digest Aval reads is the registry's, not the runner's. Compose without pull_policy: always, or Kubernetes with IfNotPresent, can run a copy pulled earlier: pull before the test, or pin by digest.
  • Also covers what the scanner cannot see, such as Helm values that split repository and tag: declare the image those values make.

  • An image test code starts through testcontainers is declared the same way. The scanner reports the literal; resolving the tag puts its digest in the fingerprint:

    // db_test.go
pg, err := postgres.Run(ctx, "postgres:16")

    scope:
  source: ["**/*.go"]
  resolve:
    - image: postgres:16
  allowMutable:
    - ref: postgres:16
      reason: resolved in scope.resolve

  • Credentials come from docker login ($DOCKER_CONFIG). A loopback registry (localhost:5000) is reached over plain HTTP.

scope.resolve never clears a scanner finding: a move changes the fingerprint, but the reference still blocks reuse. Pin it in place, or accept it with scope.allowMutable.

Pin instead when you want what you run to be exactly what you hashed: image: postgres:16@sha256:<digest> in the file. Find the digest with crane digest postgres:16.

docs.title: Maven artifacts
docs.text:
maven: <group>:<artifact>:<version> hashes the POM of that version together with the checksums the repository publishes for its artifacts (.sha256, else .sha1).

For npm, PyPI, crates, gems and Maven, an exact version binds that release. Anything else (a range, latest, a tag) binds the whole release list, so any new release runs the test again. Aval never picks a version from a range.

scope:
  resolve:
    - maven: org.postgresql:postgresql:42.7.4         # exact
    - maven: org.junit:junit-bom:5.+                  # floating
    - maven: org.apache.commons:commons-lang3:RELEASE # floating
  • Group and artifact ids: a letter, digit or _, then letters, digits, _, . or -, with no ...
  • Exact means a plain version: no +, [, ( or ,, and not LATEST, RELEASE or latest.*.
  • Floating: the <versioning> block of maven-metadata.xml and each listed version's POM and checksums. No versions, more than 100 (popular artifacts such as guava list more than 200), or a <latest>/<release> that is a SNAPSHOT or not listed fails: use an exact version.
  • A SNAPSHOT version, in any case, fails, and so does a floating list that holds one: a snapshot is redeployed under the same name.
Packaging Bound jar (default), bundle, maven-plugin, ejb POM and .jar checksum (required) war, ear, rar, aar POM, that file's checksum, and the .jar checksum if present pom (a BOM or parent) POM, and the .jar checksum if present

A missing checksum, a checksum file that holds none (a proxy's error page) or another packaging fails. Aval never downloads the jar. Not covered:

  • classifier artifacts (-sources, -linux-x86_64)
  • Gradle module metadata (.module), from which Gradle can pick another file
  • a jar overwritten on a private repository without redeploying its checksum
  • a repository that publishes only .sha1: the id rests on SHA-1

Repository $AVAL_MAVEN_URL; credentials from ~/.netrc.

Pin instead in pom.xml or build.gradle with exact versions; Gradle can also lock dependencies (gradle.lockfile).

docs.title: npm packages
docs.text:
npm: <name>@<version> hashes the dist.integrity of that version.

For npm, PyPI, crates, gems and Maven, an exact version binds that release. Anything else (a range, latest, a tag) binds the whole release list, so any new release runs the test again. Aval never picks a version from a range.

scope:
  resolve:
    - npm: prettier@3.3.3      # exact: binds 3.3.3
    - npm: typescript@latest   # floating: binds every release and tag
    - npm: "@types/node@22.x"  # floating
  • Exact means x.y.z, with an optional -pre and no operator. A name without a version means latest. A spec with +build is never found (the registry strips it) and fails.
  • Fails for any spec npm installs from elsewhere: an alias (npm:other), github:, org/repo, git+https:, a tarball URL, file: or a path (any spec with :, /, # or \, starting with . or ~/, or ending in .tgz, .tar.gz or .tar). Use git or url, or pin.
  • The name follows npm's legacy rules, which npm still installs (JSONStream): at most 214 characters, an optional lowercase @scope/, then [A-Za-z0-9-~][A-Za-z0-9-._~]*. A name ending in .tgz, .tar.gz or .tar fails: npm reads it as a local file.
  • Floating: every version with its dist.integrity and deprecation, and every dist-tag. A publish, an unpublish, a deprecation or a moved tag changes the id.
  • Registry $npm_config_registry; token from the //host/:_authToken= line of ~/.npmrc (or $npm_config_userconfig), ${VAR} expanded. As in npm, npm_config_* variables are read in any letter case, with _ equal to - after the first character. A project .npmrc and the global npmrc are not read.
  • ~/.npmrc is read as npm reads it (ini: quotes removed, ; and # comments, keys under a [section] ignored). A line Aval cannot read as key=value fails the fingerprint, and no token is sent. Settings that point the package at another registry fail too (details).

Pin instead for your project's own dependencies: commit package-lock.json (or yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml, bun.lock) and add it to scope.dependencies. Resolve is for a tool the test installs on its own, such as npx prettier@3.3.3. Only the package is bound, not the dependencies npm picks for it.

scope.resolve never clears a scanner finding: a move changes the fingerprint, but the reference still blocks reuse. Pin it in place, or accept it with scope.allowMutable.

docs.title: Python packages (PyPI)
docs.text:
pypi: <name>==<version> hashes the sha256 of every file of that release (sdist and wheels).

For npm, PyPI, crates, gems and Maven, an exact version binds that release. Anything else (a range, latest, a tag) binds the whole release list, so any new release runs the test again. Aval never picks a version from a range.

scope:
  resolve:
    - pypi: ruff==0.6.9        # exact: binds 0.6.9
    - pypi: requests==2.32.*   # floating: binds every release
    - pypi: pytest             # floating
  • Exact means one == clause with no *. Extras (requests[socks]) are ignored; environment markers are not supported.
  • ==X binds every release pip would match for it, including local labels (X+cu121) and zero-padded forms (X.0); ==X+label binds only that label. A wheel added to the release later changes the id. Other spellings of a pre-release (1.0c1 for 1.0rc1) are not grouped.
  • Floating: every file of every release, with its sha256 and yanked flag.
  • The name must be a PEP 508 name, with optional [extra,...]. A path, a URL, a marker or an archive file name (.whl, .tar.gz, .zip, ...) fails: pip would install it from disk or elsewhere. Use url.
  • Registry $AVAL_PYPI_URL (an index with the PyPI JSON API at /pypi/<name>/json); credentials from ~/.netrc. PIP_* variables that point pip elsewhere fail (details); pip.conf and uv settings are not read.

Pin instead for your requirements: pip-compile --generate-hashes or uv pip compile --generate-hashes, commit the file, and add it to the scope. Resolve is for a tool the test installs on its own, such as pip install ruff==0.6.9. Only the package is bound, not the dependencies pip picks for it.

scope.resolve never clears a scanner finding: a move changes the fingerprint, but the reference still blocks reuse. Pin it in place, or accept it with scope.allowMutable.

docs.title: Downloaded files
docs.text:
url: <url> downloads the file and hashes its bytes (sha256), up to 256 MiB.

scope:
  resolve:
    - url: https://github.com/acme/tool/releases/latest/download/tool-linux-amd64.tar.gz
    - url: https://example.com/install.sh
  • Also covers what the scanner does not detect: a curl -o tool URL or curl URL | tar x of a URL without a version. The same bytes under another URL give the same id.
  • https or http only. Credentials: ~/.netrc. A presigned URL is rejected (why).
  • Aval downloads the file every time it fingerprints, and the test downloads it again: a change between the two is not seen.

scope.resolve never clears a scanner finding: a move changes the fingerprint, but the reference still blocks reuse. Pin it in place, or accept it with scope.allowMutable.

Pin instead with a versioned URL and a checksum the test checks (sha256sum -c), or vendor the file into the scope.
